headline: Father heads to Washington; asthma begins
summary: Theodore Sr. goes to Washington to push for a law letting Union soldiers set aside part of their pay for their families, and serves as one of three allotment commissioners with Theodore B. Bronson and William E. Dodge. He hires a substitute to serve in the army. About now Teedie's asthma starts. When Port Royal falls to the North, Grandmama weeps for three days.

headline: Grandmama's Southern loyalty
summary: Grandmama Bulloch's lament continues: she would sooner lie in a common grave than see the South rejoin the Union.

headline: Full of mischief and a cold
summary: Mittie tells her husband that Teedie is loving and sweet but getting into everything and in need of his father's firm hand. He also has a bad cold.

headline: North and South under one roof

summary: Exploring the woods, the children stumble on a small house.

headline: Six miles to Cruger's Island
summary: Teedie rides Grant six miles to Cruger's Island.

headline: Wading in the brook
summary: The children spend the day playing in the brook.

headline: Early ride and a visitor
summary: Teedie makes a six-mile ride before breakfast, and Annie Platt arrives.

headline: Brook by day, games by night
summary: Another day of splashing in the brook, followed by games after supper.

headline: Watching wildlife at the pond
summary: Teedie heads to the brook and studies the animals around a pond.

headline: A lost book and talk of birds
summary: Teedie loses his book, which turns up again by September 4, and writes about birds.

headline: Swallows gathering to leave
summary: Teedie's diary records a cold, rainy day and some 75 swallows in the house as they gather to fly south. Cousin Jimmy arrives back from Niagara Falls and the boys play fort for the rest of the day.

headline: Tracking a weasel and a fox
summary: Teedie and Cousin Jimmy find a weasel's hole and a fox's den, then take a long walk.

headline: The first diary ends
summary: Teedie's first diary closes on this date.

headline: Father turns 37
summary: Theodore Sr. marks his 37th birthday.

headline: Corinne turns 7
summary: Corinne has a birthday, turning 7.

headline: Uncle Rob's second household
summary: Without the knowledge of his wife, Aunt Lizzie Ellis, Uncle Robert Roosevelt maintains a mistress, Minnie O'Shea, under the name 'Mrs. Robert F. Fortescue,' just down the street.

headline: Teedie turns ten
summary: Roosevelt celebrates his tenth birthday.

headline: Grant wins the presidency
summary: Voters send Ulysses S. Grant to the White House.

headline: Parents' 15th anniversary
summary: Theodore Sr. and Mittie mark fifteen years of marriage.

headline: A stay in Philadelphia
summary: Mittie brings Teedie to Philadelphia to visit her half-sister Susan and Susan's husband, Dr. Hilborne West.

headline: Bamie turns 14
summary: Bamie has her 14th birthday.

headline: Home in Manhattan
summary: The Roosevelts are in New York City; the record gives only the family's whereabouts for this date.

headline: Ellie turns nine; Central Park done
summary: Ellie celebrates his ninth birthday, and work on Central Park is finished.

headline: Grant takes the oath
summary: Ulysses S. Grant is inaugurated as the 18th President.

headline: A charter for the museum in the parlor
summary: Around now a charter is approved for the American Museum of Natural History, an institution born in the front parlor of the Roosevelts' East 20th Street house.

headline: Forty pages on bugs and fish
summary: Teedie fills about 40 pages with natural history notes under the title 'About Insects and Fishes.'

headline: 'We 3' and the 'big people'
summary: As the family readies for Europe, Aunt Anna, now married to James Gracie, will stay behind. Bamie counts as a grown-up even in the eyes of her siblings, and Teedie explains his shorthand: the three younger children versus the adults.

headline: Rails join at Promontory
summary: The transcontinental railroad is completed at Promontory, Utah, while the Roosevelts prepare in New York for their voyage.

headline: Last day before sailing
summary: The family is still in New York City on the eve of departure.

headline: Sailing for Europe on the Scotia
summary: Teedie's travel journal begins as the family boards Cunard's paddle-wheeler Scotia, then the fastest ship to Europe. He weeps a good deal on the way to the docks. With nursemaid Mary Ann the party numbers seven, and by bedtime he is seasick.

headline: Sick at breakfast, bored at sea
summary: Teedie spots two ships and some fish, is ill at breakfast, finds the voyage dull, and spends the day reading and playing with Ellie and Conie.

headline: Porpoises off the bow
summary: Three ships and a school of porpoises pass by; Teedie fills the day with play, reading and writing.

headline: Dolphins and sails
summary: Dolphins appear and two ships are spotted.

headline: Too ill for Sunday service
summary: Teedie is sick and homesick and misses the Sunday service. Mittie writes of a steward feeding him on deck, and of grubby carpets on an otherwise tidy ship.

headline: Fish and new friends
summary: Teedie sees two ships and lots of fish, and makes friends with some boys on board.

headline: Into the Gulf Stream
summary: The Scotia crosses the Gulf Stream, and Teedie gets to know a West Indian passenger, Mr. St. John.

headline: A shark sighting
summary: A day of reading and play, with two ships, a shark, fish and gulls to watch.

headline: Passing the Tunis
summary: The steamer Tunis is sighted, and Teedie talks again with Mr. St. John.

headline: Landfall at Liverpool
summary: At 4 a.m. the ship calls at Queenstown, Ireland, then crosses the Irish Sea to Liverpool. Mittie marvels that amid the bustle of customs, Teedie sits reading a book.

headline: Bulloch cousins in Liverpool
summary: Teedie meets his Bulloch cousins, and the children race around the hotel.

headline: Church with the Sears family
summary: The Roosevelts attend church with the Sears family and walk in the Botanic Park. Ella Sears is engaged to 27-year-old Uncle Irvine Bulloch.

headline: Out to Waterloo on the Queen's birthday
summary: The family travels about five miles to Waterloo, home of Uncle James Dunwoody Bulloch, on Queen Victoria's 50th birthday.

headline: A canary in the park
summary: The children play in the park, and Teedie sees a canary.

headline: Reading and drawing with cousins
summary: Teedie plays with his cousins and passes time reading, writing and drawing, while Papa visits the Darbys.

headline: Sharp words with Jefferson Davis's son
summary: Visiting his cousins' school at Waterloo, Teedie meets a son of Confederate president Jefferson Davis, and the boys trade sharp words.

headline: Parents to Chester, children to the park
summary: Theodore Sr. and Mittie go to Chester while the three younger children visit Princes Park and trade funny rhymes.

headline: Donkey rides and a cut leg
summary: At Southport with his cousins, Teedie rides donkeys and gashes his leg vaulting a fence.

headline: A sore leg in church
summary: Teedie goes to church, nursing the leg he cut the day before.

headline: An outing to Chatsworth
summary: The family takes the train some 80 miles to Chatsworth, the Duke of Devonshire's estate, in company with Ella Sears and Uncle Irvine, stopping at the Peacock Inn and the Edensor Hotel. Conie has a fright. Back home, the Alabama claims dispute simmers as the U.S. seeks damages from Britain.

headline: A walk with Conie and a castle visit
summary: Ten-year-old Roosevelt strolls with his little sister Conie, stops to admire some puppies, and sees Haddon Hall, an old castle dating to the 11th century, before the family returns to the Chatsworth Hotel in Liverpool.

headline: By rail to the ruins of Furness Abbey
summary: The family rides the train to the ruined Furness Abbey, getting in after nightfall. The diary names the Roosevelts' hired valet, Noel Paovitch.

headline: Exploring the abbey, then on to Ambleside
summary: Roosevelt pokes around the abbey ruins and an old water tower, then the family travels by rail and carriage to Ambleside in the Lake District.

headline: Lake Windermere, a dancing bear, and asthma
summary: At Ambleside, Roosevelt visits Lake Windermere, watches a dancing bear, and goes to church. That night his asthma flares.

headline: Rainy journey north to Edinburgh
summary: Through the rain the family takes a coach to Keswick and then the railway cars to Edinburgh. Roosevelt notes in his diary that they "romped."

headline: Sunday church and a climb on the crags
summary: Roosevelt goes to church in Edinburgh on Sunday and later scrambles up the crags above the city.

headline: Climbing Arthur's Seat with his parents
summary: The family drives to Arthur's Seat, and Roosevelt climbs the hill with his father, his mother Mittie, and his older sister Bamie. He buys himself a sweet cracker.

headline: A visit to Sir Walter Scott's home
summary: Roosevelt, his parents and Bamie take the train to Abbotsford, the house of the novelist Sir Walter Scott, and also see the ruins of Melrose Abbey.

headline: Roslin castle, chapel and a solo lunch
summary: From Edinburgh the family heads out to Roslin, where Roosevelt sees the castle, its dungeons and a chapel, then buys his lunch and eats it on his own.

headline: To Stirling Castle by rail
summary: The family takes the train to Stirling and its castle.

headline: Through the Trossachs to Glasgow
summary: Roosevelt travels through the Trossachs pass and past Loch Katrine and Loch Lomond on the way to Glasgow. The scenery calls to mind Scott's poem "The Lady of the Lake."

headline: A long, grimy train ride to York
summary: An eight-hour rail trip of roughly 140 to 160 miles brings the family to York. Worn out and grubby, Roosevelt leaves the cathedral before seeing all of it.

headline: Bible reading and York's Roman walls
summary: Skipping church, Roosevelt reads the Bible indoors, then walks along York's old Roman walls and crosses the River Ouse by ferry.

headline: Rowing on the Ouse and rock candy
summary: Roosevelt and his brother Ellie row on the River Ouse. Later he and Conie visit a museum by themselves, and two shillings go to rock candy.

headline: A long rail day to Leamington
summary: The family spends six or seven hours on the train to Leamington, and Roosevelt picks up a book at a station along the way.

headline: Warwick Castle and its Saxon giant
summary: From Leamington, Roosevelt visits Warwick Castle, with its legend of a Saxon giant.

headline: Back to Warwick with the valet
summary: Roosevelt, Ellie and Conie return to Warwick with the family valet and play in a garden.

headline: Rain, then garden play
summary: It rains in Leamington, and in the afternoon Roosevelt plays outside in the garden.

headline: Archery and colleges at Oxford
summary: The family travels by train to Oxford, where Roosevelt sees an archery match and the university's colleges.

headline: Headache and a squabble in Oxford
summary: Roosevelt goes to church in Oxford with a headache. When Conie and Ellie make a racket to annoy him, Bamie puts a stop to it.

headline: Arriving in London by hansom cab
summary: The family moves on to London, the three younger children traveling ahead with the valet. Roosevelt, still nursing a headache, gets a ride in a hansom cab.

headline: Let down by the London zoo
summary: At the Zoological Gardens in London, Roosevelt is disappointed to find mostly the same creatures he could see at any other menagerie.

headline: A second, happier zoo visit
summary: Roosevelt goes back to the London zoo and this time is pleased, finding some rarer animals.

headline: Fishing in Hyde Park and Punch and Judy
summary: In Hyde Park, Roosevelt and Conie haul tiny fish out of the lake. He and Ellie then go to a riding school, and the children catch a Punch and Judy show.

headline: Zoo, riding lessons, another headache
summary: Roosevelt spends the morning at the zoo and the afternoon at riding school, and is troubled again by a headache.

headline: Healthy lungs, then thrown at riding school
summary: A London doctor examines Roosevelt and pronounces his lungs sound. At riding school the same day, he is thrown from his mount.

headline: Sunday at Westminster Abbey
summary: Roosevelt attends church at Westminster Abbey and looks at the tombs.

headline: Hyde Park and the waxworks
summary: The three youngest Roosevelts play in Hyde Park and then visit a waxworks exhibit.

headline: Another day of play in Hyde Park
summary: Roosevelt spends the day playing in Hyde Park.

headline: Boats in Hyde Park, then the British Museum
summary: Roosevelt watches boats on the water in Hyde Park and then goes to the British Museum. A letter his mother wrote around this time survives in print.

headline: Separated from the nursemaid in Hyde Park
summary: Roosevelt, Ellie and Conie head to Hyde Park in the care of Mary Ann, lose track of her, and make their own way home.

headline: Indoor play and the British Museum
summary: Roosevelt plays inside the hotel, spends time in Hyde Park, and then visits the British Museum with the valet.

headline: Asthma sends him to the seaside at Hastings
summary: Roosevelt's asthma grows so severe that his father takes him to Hastings on the coast, where they walk the beach and see the castle.

headline: A gloomy Independence Day by the sea
summary: In Hastings, Roosevelt goes to church and walks along the cliffs, but it is a dreary Fourth of July. His asthma is so bad he lacks the breath to blow out his candle.

headline: Breakfast alone and a croquet win
summary: Roosevelt has breakfast by himself in Hastings, goes out with his father to a spot he calls "Roar valley," and wins a game of croquet.

headline: A paper knife and the trip back to London
summary: His father buys Roosevelt a paper knife before they return to London. A visit to the museum in Hyde Park is foiled because it is closed.

headline: A trip to the Crystal Palace
summary: Roosevelt visits the Crystal Palace.

headline: Crystal Palace again on Mittie's birthday
summary: The three younger children return to the Crystal Palace. It is their mother Mittie's 34th birthday.

headline: Richmond outing and a sibling quarrel
summary: Roosevelt, Ellie and Conie go out to Richmond, and Ellie and Conie get into an argument.

headline: Head on the block at the Tower of London
summary: The whole family tours the Tower of London with a guide in old warder's dress. Roosevelt looks over the armor, lays his head on the executioner's block, and glimpses the Princess of Wales.

headline: Bible reading and Kensington Gardens
summary: Roosevelt spends Sunday at home reading the Bible, then goes to Kensington Gardens.

headline: Blind man's buff and the zoo
summary: Roosevelt plays blind man's buff at the hotel in the morning and goes to the zoo in the afternoon.

headline: Seasick crossing to Antwerp
summary: The family sails down the Thames and across to Antwerp, and Roosevelt is seasick on the way.

headline: First to step onto the Continent
summary: Roosevelt is the first of the family ashore on the European mainland. In Antwerp he sees a church and the town hall.

headline: Botanic gardens, then on to The Hague
summary: In Antwerp's botanical garden the children play at bear hunting. A rail and boat journey then carries the family to The Hague.

headline: Chinese curios and a glimpse of the queen
summary: At The Hague, Roosevelt visits a museum with Chinese objects and the summer palace, sees the Dutch queen, and notices that the city has horse-drawn streetcars.

headline: A Dutch farmhouse and stories from Father
summary: A carriage ride takes the family to a Dutch farmhouse, where they eat fruit. They go on by train to Amsterdam while his father tells stories.

headline: Sunday church in Amsterdam
summary: Roosevelt attends church in Amsterdam.

headline: Amsterdam galleries and tidy Delft
summary: Roosevelt tours the museum of paintings in the palace and a privately owned gallery in Amsterdam, then the family drives to Delft, a spotless town where he sees wooden figures.

headline: Seven hours by rail to Cologne
summary: The family enters Germany, riding the train for seven hours to Cologne.

headline: Up the Rhine by boat from Mainz
summary: After a train ride to Mainz, the Roosevelts spend eight or nine hours on a boat traveling up the Rhine.

headline: Sightseeing in Frankfurt
summary: In Frankfurt, Roosevelt sees a museum, a cemetery, the Kaiser Hall and the promenade, eats at an outdoor restaurant, and goes to the zoo with the valet.

headline: Through Heidelberg to Baden
summary: The family passes through Heidelberg and continues by rail to Baden.

headline: Donkeys and a hike to the old castle
summary: At Baden, Roosevelt and his father hike up to the old castle while Ellie and Conie ride donkeys.

headline: Verses, the Black Forest, and a letter to Edith
summary: Roosevelt stays in on Sunday to learn verses and read the Bible, then walks in the Black Forest. He also writes to his childhood friend Edith Carow.

headline: Rocky hills and Strasbourg Cathedral
summary: The family drives among rocky hills, then takes the train to Strasbourg, where Roosevelt sees the cathedral.

headline: Feeling ill on the way to Basel
summary: Roosevelt is sick as the family takes the train to Basel, Switzerland.

headline: Into the Jura Mountains
summary: The family heads into the Jura Mountains and stops for the night at Münster around 8 p.m.

headline: Shoelaces in a walled village
summary: Roosevelt spends two and a half hours crossing the Jura, sees a lake and the walled village of Auberg, and buys shoelaces. Back in America, Alice Lee turns eight.

headline: A brook, Bern, and a view of the Alps
summary: After playing in a brook, the family travels by carriage and rail to Bern. Roosevelt sees the cathedral, eats ice cream, takes in the Alps from a hilltop, and tours two museums.

headline: Wildflowers and a ride to Ouchy
summary: Roosevelt and Conie gather wildflowers. After a drive around Bern, the family takes a three-hour train ride to Ouchy on Lake Geneva.

headline: A black cat and a sculptor's shop
summary: Roosevelt wanders around town, spots a black cat, looks in at a sculptor's shop, and reads the Bible.

headline: A rainy day in the grotto
summary: His parents go off to Geneva while rain falls all day in Ouchy, and Roosevelt plays in a grotto.

headline: The dungeons of Chillon
summary: From Ouchy, Roosevelt travels by steamer and rowboat to the Castle of Chillon and explores its dungeons.

headline: Down Lake Geneva and uphill toward Mont Blanc
summary: The family sails down Lake Geneva to Geneva, sees Mont Blanc, and sets out for Chamonix in a four-horse wagon. On a long climb an extra mule and horse are hitched on; Roosevelt, suffering a sharp pain, walks up himself and arrives at 7.

headline: Climbing Mont Blanc on his own legs
summary: At Chamonix, Roosevelt climbs to about 8,000 feet on Mont Blanc and does it without riding a mule. Back home, Edith Carow turns eight.

headline: Back on the glacier
summary: Roosevelt goes out on the glacier again, spends time at the hotel, and buys specimens for his museum.

headline: A cascade between the cliffs
summary: The family hikes to a waterfall along a trail squeezed between steep cliffs, and Roosevelt notes passing a pair of drunks.

headline: Sick on the trail, riding a mule
summary: On an outing Roosevelt writes as "the Shapo," a stomach pain and nausea force him to ride a mule rather than walk.

headline: Drawing birds on a rainy day
summary: Rain keeps the family indoors. Roosevelt draws birds, plays with Ellie and Conie, and listens as Bamie reads aloud to the three of them.

headline: Nineteen miles over the Tête Noire
summary: Crossing the Tête Noire pass, the family logs its mileage: his father 22, Roosevelt 19, sister Bamie 18, brother Ellie 12, mother Mittie 9 and little Conie 3. At the border he stands with a foot in each country.

headline: Rail and carriage to Visp
summary: The family takes the train and then a carriage to Visp, stopping at a waterfall where Roosevelt throws stones.

headline: By mule and on foot to Zermatt
summary: Riding mules part of the way and walking the rest, the family reaches Zermatt.

headline: Hike to a mountain chalet
summary: Roosevelt climbs on foot to a chalet high on the mountainside.

headline: Learning Bible verses
summary: Roosevelt spends Sunday learning verses from the Bible.

headline: Thirteen miles back to Visp
summary: Roosevelt walks 13 miles as the family returns to Visp.

headline: Snow at the top of the Eggishorn
summary: The family heads for the Eggishorn by way of Fiesch, with Ellie and his father walking while Roosevelt rides a horse. He reads "Henry of Greece," reaches the frigid summit, and plays in the snow before coming down.

headline: Rhône Glacier and a toothache
summary: Roosevelt sees the Rhône Glacier, and the family pushes on to Andermatt through a snowstorm. He has a bad toothache.

headline: A climb near Andermatt
summary: Roosevelt hikes up a peak the diary calls "Ardorne."

headline: Twenty miles through the Grimsel Pass
summary: The family crosses the Grimsel Pass on foot, Roosevelt covering 20 miles to his father's 22.

headline: Labeling crystals and English church
summary: Roosevelt labels his crystal collection, plays with Ellie in the park, and attends the English church.

headline: Haircut and paper-ball mischief
summary: Roosevelt gets his hair cut, goes shopping, plays indoors, and pelts the waiter and chambermaid with balls of paper.

headline: A fall on the Grindelwald glacier
summary: At Grindelwald, Roosevelt buys a tiny butter churn and takes a 20-foot fall on the glacier.

headline: Hearing avalanches on the Wengernalp
summary: Roosevelt goes up to the Wengernalp and hears two avalanches.

headline: Galloping donkeys and a snake
summary: The three younger children stay behind, take a galloping donkey ride, and see a poisonous snake that goes after the chambermaid.

headline: Homesick in Lucerne
summary: The family moves to Lucerne and goes out on the lake. Roosevelt feels very homesick.

headline: Souvenirs and getting lost with Conie
summary: Roosevelt and Conie buy keepsakes, including picture frames and candy, lose their way, and find their way back to the hotel.

headline: Sick in bed, with stories from his parents
summary: Ill, Roosevelt spends the whole day in bed eating arrowroot, while first his mother and then his father tell him stories.

headline: A drawing torn up
summary: Still sick in the morning, Roosevelt is left on his own in the afternoon. He draws a landscape and a church, then rips it up.

headline: Croquet, an island row, and homesickness
summary: The children go to Brunnen to play croquet and climb on rocks, and row out to an island. Roosevelt is homesick. A letter from Edith, undated, tells of a pulled tooth and laughing gas and encloses a leaf for him.

headline: Exploring the house in the rain
summary: Ellie is sick and it rains in Lucerne. Roosevelt and Conie explore the house and are spooked by a gurgling noise.

headline: Donkey ride, still homesick
summary: Roosevelt goes on a donkey ride in Lucerne and is again homesick.

headline: A cold day on the Rigi
summary: The family goes up the Rigi, where it is bitterly cold.

headline: Walking most of the way to Zurich
summary: Traveling to Zurich, Roosevelt and his father cover most of the distance on foot.

headline: Church and a bath in Zurich
summary: Roosevelt goes to church and has a bath.

headline: On to Bad Ragaz
summary: The family travels to Ragaz, close to Liechtenstein. There is talk that Mary Ann may soon be let go.

headline: Pfäfers gorge and a solo castle hike
summary: After visiting the gorge at Pfäfers, Roosevelt and Conie climb trees back at Ragaz, and he walks three miles alone to the castle of Wartenstein.

headline: Picnic high above the Rhine at Splügen
summary: At Splügen the family picnics, and a man drops a stone into the Rhine some 200 feet below.

headline: Crossing into Italy on foot
summary: Roosevelt and his father hike out of Switzerland at 10:30, and he straddles the Italian border. At Chiavenna the journal he has kept ends; he finds Italy cold, gloomy and foul-smelling.

headline: Moonlight row on Lake Como
summary: At Cadenabbia on Lake Como, the family is rowed across the water under the moon.

headline: Lakeside villas as the weather clears
summary: Roosevelt sees the Villa Carlotta and Villa Melzi. Rain gives way in the afternoon to what he calls "True Italy of the poets." His mother writes that he is ill with asthma.

headline: Writing by a waterfall
summary: After church, Roosevelt visits another villa on Lake Como and sits alone by a waterfall writing in his journal.

headline: Lizards and a moonlit row to Lugano
summary: The family travels by rowboat on Lake Como toward Lugano. Roosevelt catches two lizards, the party steams down Lake Lugano, and they row under the moon.

headline: Isola Bella and a bad night
summary: Sick at Stresa, Roosevelt rides by carriage to Lake Maggiore and Isola Bella and eats lemons. That night he is very ill.

headline: A lost watch and The Last Supper
summary: Roosevelt loses his watch. The family takes the train to Milan, where he sees Leonardo's Last Supper in what he calls "barracks."

headline: Early to the cathedral, rough play
summary: Roosevelt rises at six to see Milan's cathedral. Later the children play "hotel," and Conie gets hurt in a rough game.

headline: Games indoors and ice cream
summary: Roosevelt, Ellie and Conie stay inside playing games, then get ice cream after dinner.

headline: To Venice, fifty novels later
summary: The family takes the train to Venice. Roosevelt figures he has gotten through some 50 novels since the family sailed, and they ride a gondola after dark.

headline: Gnats, sleeplessness and collapse in Venice
summary: Kept awake all night by gnats, Roosevelt is sick. While the family goes out, he later makes it to St. Mark's but collapses from exhaustion.

headline: Resting indoors, then a gondola
summary: Roosevelt stays inside reading and drawing, then takes a gondola ride late in the afternoon.

headline: Well again on Father's birthday
summary: Feeling better, Roosevelt sees the churches of Santi Giovanni e Paolo and the Frari, the Doge's Palace, and a glassworks. It is his father's 38th birthday.

headline: The lost watch returns
summary: His watch is found and sent on to him. Roosevelt climbs the Campanile, visits the Lido, and sees a prince and princess glide by in a gondola.

headline: Asthma in Venice on Black Friday
summary: Sick with asthma, Roosevelt still visits a gallery, St. Mark's Square and the Ducal Palace. Across the ocean, the Black Friday gold panic hits Wall Street.

headline: Midnight boat for Trieste
summary: Roosevelt sees St. Mark's Square, the basilica and the glassworks while Mittie and Bamie shop. At midnight the family boards a boat for Trieste.

headline: Asthma, and a cigar as remedy
summary: Asthma keeps Roosevelt up for four hours, and he is made to smoke a cigar for it. The boat reaches Trieste by six; he rests, walks alone and sleeps.

headline: A lone climb at Adelsberg
summary: At Adelsberg, Roosevelt walks alone for two hours up a steep hill to a castle. The lane reminds him of Madison, New Jersey.

headline: Twelve hours by rail to Vienna
summary: The family spends twelve hours on the train to Vienna.

headline: Sick indoors in Vienna
summary: Roosevelt is ill and stays inside all day.

headline: Crowns, museums and Conie's birthday
summary: Recovered, Roosevelt sees the imperial treasury and the crowns of Charlemagne and Rudolf II, and goes with his father to the natural history museum. Conie turns eight and is honored with a formal outdoor supper at a château.

headline: Schönbrunn, the opera, and no more "baby"
summary: In Vienna the three younger children give up their game of "baby," meet their father at Prince Eugene's palace, and look without success for a riding school. Roosevelt drives out to Schönbrunn with his parents and Bamie and sees the Parliament buildings. Mittie writes that he has suffered two weeks of stomach trouble and near-asthma.

headline: A country rest at Bad Vöslau
summary: Sick again, Roosevelt goes with his father to Vöslau in the countryside, which he thinks resembles Hastings, and has Sunday school in the woods.

headline: Museum and a doctor's visit
summary: Back in Vienna, Roosevelt visits a museum with his parents and Bamie and then sees a doctor with his father.

headline: Suits of armor at Ambras
summary: Roosevelt, Ellie and Conie go to the Ambras collection and see suits of armor.

headline: Letters from home on the way to Ischl
summary: During an eight-hour train ride toward Bad Ischl, Roosevelt reads newly arrived letters from America. Four hours by carriage follow, and the family stays at a German inn.

headline: Fourteen horses to Salzburg
summary: A six-and-a-half-hour carriage ride, with fourteen horses changed in relays, carries the family to Salzburg.

headline: A nightmare and illness on the way to Munich
summary: Roosevelt has a bad dream about the devil and comes down with what he calls "cholera morbus" during an eight-hour train ride to Munich.

headline: Riding school on a rainy day
summary: It rains in Munich, and the boys go to riding school.

headline: Sick, then a walk at Starnberg
summary: Very ill, Roosevelt is soothed by his mother's stories and rubbing. In the afternoon he, his father and Ellie take a walk at Starnberg.

headline: The royal palace and two galleries
summary: Feeling better, Roosevelt returns to Munich and tours the royal palace and two picture galleries with Bamie and his parents.

headline: Five months gone, seven to go
summary: After a bad night, a homesick Roosevelt counts five months away from America with seven still ahead. The family rides five hours by train to Nuremberg.

headline: Churches of Nuremberg
summary: Roosevelt sees the churches of Nuremberg.

headline: Twelve hours by rail to Dresden
summary: The family spends twelve hours on the train to Dresden in Saxony.

headline: A harsh chest rub in Dresden
summary: Roosevelt's chest is rubbed so hard that it bleeds. He also sees forests, gets a haircut, and visits the picture gallery.

headline: Christmas shopping for china
summary: Roosevelt visits a Dresden china shop and buys Christmas presents.

headline: Homesick by the fire
summary: After church, Roosevelt lies by the fire feeling homesick.

headline: Helping his siblings shop
summary: Roosevelt helps Ellie and Conie pick out souvenirs and plays with a "Miss Wolf."

headline: Dresden's historical museum
summary: Roosevelt visits the historical museum in Dresden.

headline: Counting animals at the natural history museum
summary: Roosevelt goes alone to the natural history museum and tallies 101 animals, then visits Miss Wolf. His journal for this period ends.

headline: Children first to Berlin
summary: The three children travel five hours to Berlin, in Prussia, with the adults following six hours behind.

headline: A pulled tooth and the royal palace
summary: The whole family visits the dentist, and Roosevelt has a tooth pulled. He also sees the royal palace, the stock exchange and a synagogue.

headline: Walking to Charlottenburg
summary: Roosevelt and Brilliot, a servant, walk four or five miles to Charlottenburg.

headline: Listening to the organs
summary: The family visits two churches to hear their organs and then attends the American church in the rain.

headline: Sick, with a stop at riding school
summary: Roosevelt is sick, goes to riding school, and otherwise stays indoors.

headline: Illness cuts the Berlin stay short
summary: Sick, homesick and suffering a headache, Roosevelt still goes to riding school and the zoological museum. The family leaves Berlin because he is ill.

headline: Back to Cologne
summary: After seeing an aquarium, the family rides the train twelve and a half hours to Cologne, where they had been four months earlier.

headline: Eleven presents for his eleventh birthday
summary: In snowy Cologne the family celebrates Roosevelt's eleventh birthday. He receives eleven presents, including a writing desk, and Mittie dresses in full evening attire for his party.

headline: Six hours to Brussels
summary: The family takes a six-hour train ride to Brussels.

headline: A rainy day with Ellie
summary: Rain keeps Roosevelt inside, where he plays with Ellie.

headline: Indoors in Brussels
summary: Roosevelt spends the day at the house.

headline: To the market with the valet
summary: Roosevelt walks to the market and plays with the valet.

headline: Shoemaker, then the train to Paris
summary: After a stop at the shoemaker's, the family rides six hours by train to Paris. Another journal volume closes.

headline: Comfortable rooms and a carousel
summary: In Paris the family settles into pleasant rooms, and Roosevelt rides a merry-go-round.

headline: Play along the Seine
summary: On a wet day that grows dark early, Roosevelt plays in the hotel and beside the Seine.

headline: Glowing hands from match heads
summary: Out shopping for Christmas gifts, Roosevelt rubs the phosphorus off matches onto his hands and makes them glow.

headline: Fruit market and homemade candy
summary: On a rainy day Roosevelt visits a fruit market and makes sugar candy.

headline: Sunday church in Paris
summary: Roosevelt goes to church.

headline: Teased for a favorite phrase
summary: Mittie pokes fun at Roosevelt for constantly saying "pretty Papa, Pretty Mama."

headline: A sore toe and the Vendôme Column
summary: Despite a corn on his toe, Roosevelt climbs the Vendôme Column with the valet.

headline: A riverside walk and a steam bath
summary: Roosevelt walks by the Seine with the valet and takes a steam bath.

headline: Steam bath with Mother and a new stamp book
summary: Roosevelt takes a steam bath with his mother and buys a stamp album.

headline: Halfway home
summary: Roosevelt marks the halfway point of the trip abroad with a cheer. He and Ellie visit a Russian steam bath.

headline: Thirty stamps collected
summary: Roosevelt and Mittie take steam baths, and he sees a doctor with his father. His stamp album now holds 30 stamps.

headline: Sick, and sharing the stamp album
summary: Roosevelt is ill and takes a steam bath. He, Mittie and his father look over his stamp collection together.

headline: Pillow fight and a letter to Edith
summary: Still sick and taking steam baths, Roosevelt gets into a pillow fight and writes to Edith Carow.

headline: Johnny Lampson and the chambermaids
summary: Roosevelt stays in, plays with Johnny Lampson, and gets into a scuffle with the chambermaids.

headline: A walk instead of a bath
summary: Roosevelt skips his bath and goes walking with his mother.

headline: Father leaves for London
summary: His father goes to London while the rest of the family stays in Paris. Roosevelt explores the house with Johnny Lampson and takes a walk.

headline: Gymnastics and a pop gun
summary: While Mittie takes a steam bath, Roosevelt and Ellie do gymnastics, and he buys a pop gun. At home in America, Edith Carow writes Conie that she misses her.

headline: Too rough with Johnny Lampson
summary: Roosevelt and Ellie do gymnastics and go to a little theater. Their rough play with Johnny Lampson gets them told to stop.

headline: Mittie's thirteen brothers and sisters
summary: Staying in, Roosevelt listens as his mother tells about her 13 siblings and what became of them; four are still living.

headline: Edith's portrait stirs homesickness
summary: In the evening Mittie shows Roosevelt a portrait of Edith Carow, and the sight of her face fills him with longing for home and the past.

headline: Wooden horses and the Arc de Triomphe
summary: After a doctor's visit, Roosevelt plays with Johnny Lampson, sees a theater, rides the carousel, and visits the Arc de Triomphe.

headline: Stiff neck and two letters
summary: With a stiff neck and headache, Roosevelt writes two letters and feels worse as the day goes on. Edith writes him from America.

headline: New medicine, toast and tea
summary: The doctor calls and changes Roosevelt's medicine for the third time. He has no appetite and eats only tea and toast.

headline: Kept indoors
summary: Roosevelt stays in the house.

headline: Another day inside
summary: Roosevelt spends the day indoors again.

headline: Indoors but improving
summary: Still confined to the house, Roosevelt starts to feel better.

headline: Too tired to enjoy play
summary: On his sixth straight day indoors, Roosevelt has a visit from Johnny Lampson but is too worn out to enjoy their evening games.

headline: Tears of homesickness on the way to Dijon
summary: The family travels to Dijon. Roosevelt cries from homesickness, wishing to escape a land of people who cannot speak his language.

headline: A cold walk and a night train
summary: In bitter cold, Roosevelt walks around Dijon, and the family spends the night on a train to Marseille.

headline: Seeing Marseille with Father
summary: Ellie is sick, so Roosevelt and his father explore Marseille: the exchange, the harbor and docks, the cathedral, the forts and the old town. He closes his second journal book with a roll call of the children's ages.

headline: First sight of the Mediterranean
summary: Leaving Marseille, the family rides the train until 6:30 and Roosevelt sees the Mediterranean. His father calls the three youngest "bothers," and Roosevelt takes his medicine.

headline: Coins and reading on a rainy day in Nice
summary: It rains in Nice. Roosevelt plays with his coins and reads. The family's two servants are the valet, called "B," and Mary Ann.

headline: Donkey on the beach and Revolutionary ancestors
summary: On the beach at Nice, the adults walk, the two younger children stand by, and Roosevelt rides a donkey. Mittie tells of family ancestors who served in the American Revolution.

headline: Beach, hillside and a far view of the Alps
summary: Roosevelt plays on the beach, as do Mittie and Bamie, runs up a hill, spots the Alps in the distance, and plays with his coins.

headline: A new knife for Ellie
summary: Roosevelt goes to the post office with the valet and buys Ellie a knife to replace the one he lost the day before.

headline: Talking over the trip with Mother
summary: On a wet day, Roosevelt plays with tin animals, eats at an English restaurant, and talks with Mittie about the journey so far.

headline: Rowing out to the U.S.S. Sabine
summary: The three youngest play a chasing game, buy gifts for Mary Ann and the valet, and row out to see the American warship Sabine anchored in the harbor.

headline: An outing to Monaco
summary: After a trip to the post office, Roosevelt visits Monaco and its casino, then plays on the hotel steps.

headline: Beach day in Nice
summary: Roosevelt plays on the beach.

headline: An unimpressive Roman amphitheater
summary: Conie pretends to be sick. Roosevelt goes to church and on a walk, finds the Roman amphitheater dull, and notices painted scenes on the houses.

headline: Along the Corniche to San Remo
summary: Behind four horses and a mule, the family climbs the steep Corniche road 37 miles to San Remo. Roosevelt straddles the French-Italian border, and another journal volume ends.

headline: Feeding beggars at Finale
summary: Roosevelt walks with his mother as the family continues by carriage into Italy. At Finale his father buys cakes, and he and the children toss them to beggars.

headline: Keepsakes, a pageant, and Savona
summary: The three youngest buy mementos; Mittie and Bamie admire them while their father makes fun of them. Roosevelt goes to church and watches a pageant in Savona.

headline: Sightseeing on foot in Genoa
summary: After a morning romp, the family reaches Genoa and takes a long walk around the sights.

headline: Genoa, Chiavari and four coins
summary: Roosevelt tours Genoa and then goes by train to Chiavari. Ellie loses his knife, Roosevelt gets four coins, and their parents are still behind.

headline: Walking beside the carriage to La Spezia
summary: On a climb over a high mountain, Roosevelt, Ellie and his father walk alongside the carriage past many beggars. From La Spezia they take the train to Pisa.

headline: Sunday at the Leaning Tower
summary: Roosevelt goes to church in Pisa, sees the Leaning Tower and the cathedral, and attends Sunday school.

headline: Up the Leaning Tower
summary: Roosevelt climbs the tower and returns to the cathedral. His diary notes the "League of the Cross" for the first time.

headline: A flooded rail trip to Rome
summary: A long train ride through flooding from heavy rain, by way of Livorno, takes the family to Rome.

headline: Rome in the rain on an anniversary
summary: Rain keeps Roosevelt in the hotel, playing and looking at coins; he finds Rome dirty and dreary. It is his parents' 16th wedding anniversary.

headline: Coins, books and a rainy walk
summary: Roosevelt plays with his coins, plays with Conie and Ellie, and reads. After dinner he and Conie go walking in the rain.

headline: Hanging stockings in Rome
summary: Excited about Christmas, Roosevelt plays in the hotel and hangs up his stocking.

headline: Christmas morning and the Pope at St. Peter's
summary: Before six the children burst in on their parents to open their stockings. Later Roosevelt visits St. Peter's and sees Pope Pius IX.

headline: Temple of Vesta and St. Paul's
summary: Roosevelt attends church and sees the Temple of Vesta and the Church of St. Paul.

headline: Writing a story
summary: Roosevelt writes a story, reads and plays.

headline: Through hail to Naples
summary: An eight- or nine-hour train trip in hail takes the family past Albano, Roman ruins, Velletri, Segni and Cassino to Naples. Roosevelt and Mittie read about the mountains along the way.

headline: Vesuvius in view
summary: With Vesuvius in sight, Roosevelt visits the church of San Martino and sees a Pietà.

headline: Carriages to Pompeii
summary: On a sunny day the family rides two carriages about two hours to Pompeii and sees the House of Diomedes.

headline: Snowballs on smoking Vesuvius
summary: Roosevelt climbs Mount Vesuvius, sees lava still smoking, and joins a snowball fight.

headline: Old Naples, Sorrento, and a letter to Edith
summary: Roosevelt sees the old quarter and market of Naples before going on to Sorrento. Answering Edith Carow's letter, he tells her that the day before he poked an alpenstock into the volcano and it caught fire.

headline: Rocks by the sea and a letter to Aunt Annie
summary: Skipping church, Roosevelt goes to the seaside and plays on the rocks. He writes to Anna Gracie.

headline: Back to Naples and the museum
summary: In the rain, the family returns to Naples, where Roosevelt visits the museum.

headline: Volcanic ground and a Roman vase
summary: Two carriages take the family to Lake Agnano, the Grotto of Posillipo, the Solfatara crater and Roman temples. His father gives Roosevelt a Roman vase and coin.

headline: A night cough and ipecac
summary: Sick in the night with a cough, Roosevelt is dosed with ipecac. He and Conie stay home while the others go to Pompeii.

headline: Donkey ride and rooftop play
summary: Roosevelt reads, plays, buys journal books, rides a donkey and plays on the roof.

headline: Fishing from the rocks
summary: On a rainy day, Roosevelt buys a charm, plays with coins, and fishes from the rocks.

headline: By rail past Caserta
summary: On the train, the family stops at Caserta and its villa, and Roosevelt and Ellie play baby.

headline: Meeting an American boy in Rome
summary: Back in Rome, Roosevelt skips church and walks with Ellie. They meet an American boy and invite him to dinner on Thursday.

headline: Rainy-day soldiers and a costume party
summary: Rain falls all day. Roosevelt and Ellie play soldiers and then donkey, and their father throws a dress-up party.

headline: Tin soldiers and leaping posts
summary: Roosevelt plays with tin soldiers and vaults over posts.

headline: Ashamed of dirty clothes
summary: Roosevelt plays by a fountain and is embarrassed by how dirty his clothes get.

headline: At the hunt meet
summary: Roosevelt goes to a hunt meet and plays with lances.

headline: Happy in Rome
summary: Roosevelt goes to the post and buys a Roman coin, and he is enjoying Rome.

headline: Rough soldier games with Charlie
summary: Roosevelt buys a present for Bamie, then he, Ellie and a boy named Charlie play soldier roughly.

headline: A pleasant Sunday at the Villa Borghese
summary: Roosevelt goes to church, walks in the Villa Borghese gardens, has supper with Mittie and attends Sunday school, and has a very good time.

headline: Chasing dogs on the Pincio
summary: Roosevelt, Ellie, Conie and George Cromwell go out on the Pincian Hill, meet priests and chase dogs.

headline: Caps, ancient tombs and Bamie's birthday
summary: Roosevelt and Ellie buy caps, shoot at dogs and play soldier. With his mother he goes to see some old tombs. Bamie turns fifteen.

headline: A gun and a bugle
summary: Roosevelt buys a gun and a bugle and plays soldier with George Cromwell.

headline: Father's dinner for twenty-two
summary: After a poor night, Roosevelt plays soldiers and chases dogs on the Pincio. His father hosts a grand dinner for 22 guests.

headline: Coffee for a sleepless night, then Albano
summary: Awake for two or three hours in a very bad night, Roosevelt is given coffee. After a visit to the Pincio, he, Ellie and his father ride the rail line out to Albano, where they stay overnight.

headline: Donkey ride at Albano
summary: His father returns to Rome while Roosevelt and Ellie go on a donkey ride in the rain. The rest of the family arrives.

headline: Exploring the caves at Albano
summary: Roosevelt skips church, plays baby with Ellie and Conie, and explores caverns that fascinate him.

headline: Monte Cavo and the Appian Way
summary: Riding donkeys, the family climbs Monte Cavo and visits Rocca di Papa, dines at Albano, and rides by carriage to Rome along the Appian Way.

headline: George made captain
summary: George is chosen captain of the boys' soldier company. Roosevelt climbs a tree, plays with coins and has supper with Mittie.

headline: Pushed into the fountain
summary: Roosevelt and Charlie Cromwell go to the Pincio to play soldiers; someone ends up pushed into the fountain. Tea and coins round out the day.

headline: Races on the Pincio
summary: Roosevelt buys caps, runs races and plays horse on the Pincio. A guest recorded as T. Bronzen comes to dinner.

headline: Playing brigands
summary: The three youngest go to the Pincio and play brigands.

headline: Coachman games and coins
summary: Roosevelt plays coachman and looks over his coins.

headline: Church, Villa Borghese and the Pincio
summary: Roosevelt attends church and Sunday school, visits the Villa Borghese and the Pincio, and plays with coins.

headline: Kissing the Pope's hand on the Pincio
summary: While the children play leapfrog, Pope Pius IX passes in his sedan chair. Young "Teedie" has just boasted that no true American believes in popes, yet when the pontiff holds out his hand, Roosevelt kisses it, as Conie later recalled and his diary confirms.

headline: Prisoner's base on the Pincio with Conie
summary: Roosevelt and his little sister Conie head up to the Pincio gardens in Rome and join a crowd of other children in a game of prisoner's base, then take their supper with their mother, Mittie. Back home, young Edith Carow writes Conie that she has been ordered to set her books aside.

headline: Jostled in the crowd at St. Peter's
summary: After hide-and-seek on the Pincio, the family goes to St. Peter's hoping to see the Pope. In the packed crowd a monk shoves young Theodore, and his father pushes the man back, hard.

headline: A birthday party for Ellie in Rome
summary: It is Ellie's birthday. Roosevelt plays horse on the Pincio, and at five o'clock a crowd of friends arrives for the party, where a girl named Elliese Van Schaack gives him a kiss.

headline: Captain of the gendarmes
summary: A full day of games on the Pincio: fort, coins, horses, tag, and robbers-and-gendarmes, with Roosevelt leading the gendarmes as their captain.

headline: Bull, tag, and hide-and-seek
summary: Another afternoon on the Pincio, this time spent playing bull, tag, and hide-and-seek.

headline: Two brothers go to church alone
summary: Roosevelt and his younger brother Ellie attend church on their own. The diary also names two boys, Theodor Bronzen and Elliott de Briskey, apparently playmates.

headline: A new ball for Conie
summary: On the Pincio, Roosevelt buys his sister Conie a ball.

headline: Rainy day of books and sisters
summary: Rain keeps the children indoors. Roosevelt reads about travel and geography and plays with his sisters Bamie and Conie.

headline: Ball and horse despite the weather
summary: The weather is poor, but Roosevelt still gets out to the Pincio for games of ball and horse.

headline: From the Pincio to the Vatican Loggia
summary: After time on the Pincio, Roosevelt visits the Vatican and its Loggia.

headline: Riding up top to Tivoli
summary: The family drives out by carriage to Tivoli, with Roosevelt perched on the driver's box in the bitter cold. They see the waterfalls and Hadrian's Villa.

headline: Ancient Rome while Ellie stays in bed
summary: With Ellie ill at home, the rest of the family rides by carriage through ancient Rome: the Forum, Trajan's Column, the Colosseum, and the Baths of Caracalla.

headline: Church, Sunday school, and battles
summary: A Sunday of church and Sunday school, with battle games in between.

headline: Paintings at the Vatican
summary: Roosevelt goes to the Vatican to look at its paintings.

headline: Pincio and the Farnese pictures
summary: A morning on the Pincio, then paintings at the Farnese palace.

headline: Horse and Indian on the Pincio
summary: Roosevelt spends the day at the Pincio playing horse and Indian.

headline: A visit to Castel Sant'Angelo
summary: After the Pincio, Roosevelt sees the Castle of St. Angelo.

headline: Goodbyes in Rome as Father falls ill
summary: On a last day at the Pincio, Roosevelt plays horse and bids farewell to the friends he has made in Rome. His father is unwell, and guards go through the family's luggage.

headline: Father gravely ill in Florence
summary: Now in Florence, Roosevelt plays in the garden while his father lies very sick.

headline: Father rallies; Mittie tells old stories
summary: His father is much improved. Roosevelt goes to church with Bamie and Ellie, plays coins and baby in the garden, and listens as his mother tells stories about her own girlhood.

headline: Muddy games and San Marco's paintings
summary: Roosevelt plays baby in the garden and ends up covered in mud, then visits the paintings at the convent of San Marco.

headline: A chilly trip up to Fiesole
summary: The family makes a cold outing to Fiesole, in the hills above Florence.

headline: Garden play and gallery paintings
summary: Roosevelt plays in the garden and looks at paintings in a Florence gallery.

headline: Soldiers, coins, and history
summary: In the garden Roosevelt plays soldiers and coins, and he spends time reading history.

headline: Feeling poorly, reading Greek history
summary: A bit under the weather, Roosevelt still plays soldiers and reads Greek history.

headline: Building miniature catacombs
summary: In the garden Roosevelt lays out tiny roads, palaces, and catacombs. He also visits the zoo, has tea, and reads.

headline: Headache keeps him from Sunday school
summary: Roosevelt is sick with a headache and misses Sunday school.

headline: Ellie turns ten
summary: Roosevelt goes back to building little roads in the garden as his brother Ellie celebrates his tenth birthday.

headline: A visit to Mr. Elliott by the river
summary: Roosevelt and Ellie call on a Mr. Elliott, then play in a park along the river in Florence.

headline: Watching the bears at feeding time
summary: With his father sick again, Roosevelt gets a haircut at the barber and visits the zoological garden, where he watches the bears being fed.

headline: The Uffizi and the Ponte Vecchio
summary: Roosevelt looks at pictures in the Uffizi, crosses the Ponte Vecchio, and plays in the garden.

headline: Three children, three little cities
summary: In the garden, Roosevelt, Ellie, and Conie each tend a miniature city of their own.

headline: Through 18 tunnels to Bologna
summary: The family travels to Bologna, passing through eighteen tunnels along the way, while Roosevelt reads Greek history.

headline: Pigeons and carnival in Bologna
summary: Church is held at the hotel in Bologna. Roosevelt watches the pigeons and sees the carnival.

headline: Galleries, then a night train to Turin
summary: After visiting the art galleries in the rain, the family boards a train for Turin following dinner, and Roosevelt plays with his father.

headline: Skeletons and armor in Turin
summary: In Turin, Roosevelt sees the armory, the royal palace, and animal skeletons at a museum.

headline: Fourteen hours by rail into France
summary: A fourteen-hour train ride carries the family over steep mountains into France. This is the last entry in this volume of the boy's journal.

headline: Arriving in Paris, unwell
summary: After four more hours by train the family reaches Paris. Roosevelt is sick but still finds time for his coins.

headline: Playing at the Tuileries
summary: In Paris, Roosevelt plays in the Tuileries, visits the shoemakers, and plays coins.

headline: Toy boats and soldiers
summary: A day of play with boats and toy soldiers in Paris.

headline: Snowy Sunday in Paris
summary: Snow falls on a Sunday of church and Sunday school, with coins for play.

headline: A frozen fountain and the Lampsons
summary: Roosevelt sails his boats, finds the fountain frozen over, and spends time with the Lampson family's Johnny.

headline: Ice on the fountain still
summary: The fountain is still iced over. Roosevelt plays soldiers and hide-and-seek.

headline: Shut in a dark closet
summary: On a rainy day Roosevelt plays soldiers and reads. The diary also mentions a dark closet.

headline: A glimpse of the Emperor
summary: Johnny Lampson comes to dinner after a day of soldiers and boats, and Roosevelt catches sight of Emperor Napoleon III.

headline: Sailing boats with Ellie
summary: Roosevelt and Ellie spend the day sailing their toy boats.

headline: Choosing a school for Bamie
summary: Feeling a little sick, Roosevelt goes by train to Fontainebleau to see the palace. The family inspects Les Ruches, Mlle. Marie Souvestre's private school, where Bamie will remain when the rest go home to America.

headline: Sunday church in Paris
summary: Roosevelt goes to church in Paris.

headline: Rain, soldiers, and boats
summary: A wet day passed with toy soldiers and boats.

headline: More rain, more soldiers
summary: Rain again, and more games with toy soldiers.

headline: A walk and the soldiers
summary: Roosevelt takes a walk and plays with his soldiers.

headline: Boat, ball, and soldiers
summary: Roosevelt plays with his boat, a ball, and his soldiers.

headline: Uncle Silas Weir Roosevelt dies
summary: While Roosevelt plays ball in a Paris garden, his uncle Silas Weir Roosevelt dies back in the United States.

headline: Garden and soldiers
summary: Time in the garden and with the toy soldiers.

headline: Church with Bamie
summary: Roosevelt and Bamie go to church together, followed by a walk, coins, and Sunday school.

headline: Forty-five minutes locked in a closet
summary: Roosevelt spends three-quarters of an hour shut inside a closet, and plays soldiers.

headline: Window-shopping for soldiers
summary: Roosevelt plays boat and marbles and gazes at the toy soldiers in a shop.

headline: Tag and stamps
summary: Outdoors in the garden for tag, then time with his stamps.

headline: A visit to the Louvre
summary: Roosevelt is taken to the Louvre.

headline: Tea with Fanny Lampson
summary: After the Tuileries garden, Fanny Lampson comes over to play and stays for tea.

headline: Tombs at Pere Lachaise
summary: Roosevelt tours the tombs of Pere Lachaise cemetery and the Pantheon.

headline: Sunday church
summary: Roosevelt attends church in Paris.

headline: Back to the Tuileries garden
summary: Another day of play in the Tuileries garden.

headline: Looking at the animals
summary: Roosevelt goes to see animals in Paris.

headline: The porcelain works at Sevres
summary: The family drives by carriage to Sevres and tours the china factory.

headline: Sitting for photographs
summary: Roosevelt has his photograph taken and takes a French lesson.

headline: French class after the Tuileries
summary: A visit to the Tuileries, then French class.

headline: A helmet and a bow
summary: Roosevelt buys himself a helmet and a bow and arrows.

headline: Church and a walk
summary: Sunday brings church and a walk.

headline: Emperor and Prince Imperial review troops
summary: Roosevelt watches Napoleon III and the young Prince Imperial review the French troops in Paris.

headline: Day trip to Versailles
summary: The family travels an hour and a half to Versailles.

headline: Nine boys and an army indoors
summary: Nine boys fill the house for a game of soldiers.

headline: Soldiers, and a scrap
summary: During a day of soldiers, Roosevelt gets into a fight.

headline: Ten soldiers and a ball
summary: Roosevelt plays soldiers, with ten of them noted, and ball.

headline: A sick boy goes to Fontainebleau
summary: After a rough night, Roosevelt goes to Fontainebleau and plays in the garden, though he is ill.

headline: The best Easter of his life
summary: At Fontainebleau, Roosevelt walks in the woods and hunts Easter eggs, and calls it the happiest Easter he has known.

headline: Parents and Bamie head to Paris
summary: His father, mother, and Bamie go up to Paris while Roosevelt stays at Fontainebleau playing in the garden.

headline: By train back to Paris
summary: Roosevelt returns to Paris by train.

headline: Sick in Paris
summary: Roosevelt is ill.

headline: Reading in the shade
summary: Still sick, Roosevelt reads in the shade.

headline: French lesson and garden
summary: A French lesson and time in the garden.

headline: Climbing rocks at Fontainebleau
summary: Roosevelt takes the train to Fontainebleau and scrambles over the rocks.

headline: Rocks in the park
summary: A day in the park at Fontainebleau among the rocks.

headline: The Tuileries and the Champs-Elysees
summary: Back in Paris, Roosevelt visits the Tuileries and the Champs-Elysees.

headline: A full day of lessons and play
summary: Garden, soldiers, a French lesson, reading, and play fill the day.

headline: Rain in Paris
summary: A rainy day in Paris.

headline: Tag and coins in the rain
summary: Despite rain, Roosevelt plays tag and coins and has a French lesson.

headline: Horse and fort
summary: Roosevelt plays horse and fort and reads.

headline: Tearful goodbye to Bamie; on to London
summary: The family leaves Bamie behind at school and everyone cries. After five hours on the train and a slightly queasy Channel crossing from Boulogne to Folkestone, they reach London. Years later Roosevelt said plainly that he disliked the whole trip.

headline: Sent from the table in London
summary: There is no church today. Roosevelt goes to Hyde Park, and at a meal he dips his fingers into the butter dish and is dismissed from the table.

headline: A gift of stamps from a stranger
summary: Roosevelt goes to Wells and to a bank, where a kind gentleman hands him some stamps.

headline: Windsor Castle and Eton
summary: A train ride to Windsor Castle, where Roosevelt sees the farm, stables, and castle, then a stop at Eton before heading home.

headline: A day at the London zoo
summary: Roosevelt visits the zoo in London.

headline: A walk in Hyde Park
summary: Roosevelt walks in Hyde Park.

headline: Stamps and the zoo again
summary: Roosevelt works on his stamps and returns to the zoo.

headline: Liverpool and Uncle Irvine
summary: Roosevelt travels to Liverpool, with his parents coming along after, and meets his uncle Irvine Bulloch. Coins round out the day.

headline: Sunday in Liverpool
summary: Church and a walk in Liverpool.

headline: Cousins, the beach, and rare stamps
summary: Roosevelt sees his cousins, goes to the beach, and comes across some rare stamps.

headline: Digging trenches at Aunt Hattie's
summary: At Waterloo, near Liverpool, with Aunt Hattie, Roosevelt digs burrows and trenches.

headline: Rainy reading day at Waterloo
summary: Rain at Waterloo, and Roosevelt reads.

headline: A cave in the sand hills
summary: Roosevelt plays in the sand hills and finds a cave, then rides into Liverpool in the afternoon.

headline: Waxworks and farewells
summary: A visit to the waxworks, then goodbyes to the Liverpool cousins.

headline: Aboard the Russia, homeward bound
summary: The family sails on the screw steamer Russia across the Irish Sea. It rains, but Roosevelt does not get seasick.

headline: Nine hours at Queenstown
summary: With no church aboard, the ship lies at Queenstown, Ireland, for nine hours. Sunday school is held.

headline: Seasick, then shipboard friends
summary: The first days at sea are rough and Roosevelt gets seasick, but he recovers fast, makes friends, and plays on deck.

headline: Crossing the Atlantic
summary: The Russia steams on across the Atlantic; the diary records only that the family is at sea.

headline: Crossing the Atlantic
summary: The Russia steams on across the Atlantic; the diary records only that the family is at sea.

headline: Crossing the Atlantic
summary: The Russia steams on across the Atlantic; the diary records only that the family is at sea.

headline: Crossing the Atlantic
summary: The Russia steams on across the Atlantic; the diary records only that the family is at sea.

headline: Crossing the Atlantic
summary: The Russia steams on across the Atlantic; the diary records only that the family is at sea.

headline: Sixteen children play Colosseum
summary: Church and Sunday school at sea, a fight in the morning, then tag, hide-and-seek, and a game of Colosseum with sixteen children.

headline: Whales off the bow
summary: The ship takes on a pilot, and Roosevelt sees whales, one of which sprays him with water. His travel journal ends here.

headline: Hip! Hurrah! Home to America
summary: America comes into view. The Russia passes Sandy Hook into New York Bay, and friends meet the family at the pier.

headline: Breakfast and Jimmy's collection
summary: Back in New York, Roosevelt goes round to a neighbor's for breakfast, sees his friend Jimmy, and looks over a collection.

headline: Home all day with Jimmie and Dora
summary: Roosevelt spends the whole day at home playing with Jimmie and chatting with Dora.

headline: The rest of the family goes to the country
summary: While the others head out to the country, Roosevelt stays in the city with his parents and has Jimmie over to play.

headline: Off to Philadelphia with Aunt Susy
summary: No church today. Roosevelt walks with Evelen and reads, then sets off with Aunt Susy on a four-hour train trip to Philadelphia, reading and writing along the way.

headline: China animals and strawberry ice cream
summary: In Philadelphia Roosevelt buys little china animals, shares strawberry ice cream with Aunt Susy, and sees the U.S. Mint. His father arrives that night and goes to the Union League Club.

headline: The young naturalist starts collecting
summary: Roosevelt begins collecting every kind of wild creature he can find, launching a boyhood natural history collection.

headline: Out of the city to Riverdale
summary: After only a few hours back in New York, the family heads up to the country at Spuyten Duyvil in Riverdale for the summer.

headline: Rocks and a brook
summary: Roosevelt scrambles over the rocks and plays in the brook at Spuyten Duyvil.

summary: Daily trips to John Wood's gymnasium begin, with Mittie bringing Roosevelt and Ellie and patiently watching as Wood teaches them the equipment. The children also begin lessons at Mr. Dodsworth's dancing school on Fifth Avenue, alongside Fanny Smith and Edith Carow.

summary: Roosevelt celebrates his 12th birthday.

headline: Alice Lee turns ten
summary: Alice Lee, Roosevelt's future first wife, has her tenth birthday.

headline: An Adirondack party sets out
summary: A family party forms for the Adirondacks: Uncle Cornelius Roosevelt and Aunt Laura, Uncle Hilborne West and Aunt Susy, and cousin West Roosevelt, a boy close to Roosevelt's age. The Carows leave for Renovo, Pennsylvania.

headline: Airgun and steamboat
summary: Roosevelt tries an airgun, takes a steamboat ride, and goes up a mountain.

headline: Up the lake to Ticonderoga's ruins
summary: The party steams up Lake George aboard the Minnehaha, then takes a stagecoach past the ruins of Ticonderoga. Roosevelt picks up a cannonball the record links to the Battle of Plattsburgh.

headline: Quizzing the stage driver about animals
summary: A train ride of an hour and a half and a stagecoach bring the party to Paul Smith's, sixty miles in all. On the way Roosevelt talks with the driver about wild animals.

headline: A snake for the collection
summary: After church, Roosevelt kills a snake to keep as a specimen. Back home, Edith Carow turns ten.

summary: His father, Uncle Hilborne, and the three boys set out by boat on an excursion to Upper St. Regis, practicing with a revolver and landing on an island.

summary: The party moves back upstream to its starting point. The boys chase the guide around, and his father reads them The Last of the Mohicans.

summary: The party crosses the lake by boat to Paul Smith's.

summary: Sunday church and a row on the lake.

summary: Roosevelt visits Ausable Glen and rides a steamboat.

summary: Roosevelt, West, and Ellie spend a whole day on the tough climb up Mount Lafayette, watching for wildlife along the way.

summary: His father celebrates his 40th birthday.

headline: Corinne turns ten
