headline: Shopping in Cairo
summary: The day is spent shopping in Cairo.

headline: Purchases with his father
summary: Roosevelt and his father make some purchases, perhaps including the book on Egyptian birds that Roosevelt later mentions in his Autobiography.

headline: Moving aboard the Ibis
summary: In the afternoon the family settles onto the dahabeah, which Roosevelt finds snug and pleasant.

headline: First bird he ever shot
summary: Out shooting with his father near Cairo, Roosevelt brings down the first bird of his life. He also sees the howling dervishes.

headline: A white wagtail and fifteen species
summary: Roosevelt and his father go shooting and bag a white wagtail; on an hour's walk he counts fifteen kinds of birds.

headline: Sunday near Cairo
summary: Roosevelt goes to church, pays visits and takes a walk.

headline: Shooting and the Boulaq Museum
summary: After a morning's shooting, Roosevelt visits the museum at Boulaq with its collection of ancient Egyptian objects.

headline: Conie sick, the men out shooting
summary: Conie is ill, while Roosevelt and his father spend the morning shooting.

headline: A rare white-tailed plover
summary: Theodore Sr. and Bamie go into Cairo and friends call. Out shooting with his father, Roosevelt spots an uncommon white-tailed plover.

headline: A yellow wagtail in five shots
summary: Roosevelt and his father go shooting, and it takes him five shots to get a yellow wagtail.

headline: Three boats start up the Nile
summary: That afternoon a small flotilla heads upriver: four Harvard men aboard the Rachel, the Clift family on the Gazelle, and the Roosevelts on the Ibis.

headline: Aground near Tura, full game bags
summary: Near Tura the boat runs onto a sandbar. Roosevelt and his father shoot in a palm grove and come back with bulging game bags.

headline: A Sunday pelican near Beni Suef
summary: Near Beni Suef the men of the Rachel shoot a pelican on the Sabbath. Roosevelt watches birds, and his parents mark their nineteenth anniversary.

headline: Skinning a pelican aboard the Rachel
summary: Roosevelt skins the pelican on the Rachel and goes shooting. The American consul calls.

headline: Christmas Eve on horseback
summary: Roosevelt skins birds, then rides horses with his parents. Mr. Clift pays a visit.

headline: A shotgun for Christmas
summary: Christmas gifts are opened in his father's cabin, and Roosevelt's is a double-barreled shotgun. He promptly shoots four doves and calls on the American consul.

headline: Shooting four miles upriver
summary: Four miles above Beni Suef, Roosevelt and his father go shooting.

headline: An ibis, a lark and a collision
summary: At Fechtan Roosevelt shoots an ibis and a lark. The Ibis bumps into the Rachel, which stays behind, and Mr. Waitman appears on the Water Lily.

headline: Villagers object to the shooting
summary: About fifteen miles beyond Fechtan the party goes shooting, and local people complain.

headline: Under sail, watching birds
summary: The Ibis sails on, and Roosevelt watches the birdlife along the river.

headline: Live doves at Golosna
summary: The boat sails and stops at Golosna, where the family buys live doves.

headline: New Year's Eve party on the Ibis
summary: At Minich, Roosevelt and his father shoot eighteen birds, and the Rachel catches up. That night about twenty people from all three boats crowd onto the Ibis to sing, drink eggnog, toast midnight with champagne and dance the Virginia reel.

headline: New Year's Day under sail
summary: The Ibis sails on, about seven miles past Roda.

headline: Stuck again, jackals at night
summary: The boat grounds on a sandbar and the crew must haul and pole it free. Roosevelt hears jackals.

headline: Bumps and groundings on the Nile
summary: The day's excitement comes from collisions, groundings and similar mishaps on the river.

headline: Becalmed below the cliffs of Abu Feda
summary: With no wind opposite Abu Feda, the crew tows and poles the boat. The day closes with a splendid sunset over the cliffs.

headline: A broken tiller at Asyut
summary: At Asyut the Ibis breaks its tiller, and Roosevelt sees a mirage.

headline: Donkeys to the tombs of Asyut
summary: Above Asyut, Roosevelt rides a donkey out to ancient tombs covered in hieroglyphs, and he scorns the scrawls left by modern visitors.

headline: Sailing past Girga
summary: The Ibis sails on below Girga.

headline: Good wind and a sketch of the ibis
summary: With a good breeze above Girga, Roosevelt goes shooting and writes a description of the ibis.

headline: Fair wind above Qena
summary: The boat makes good time with a strong wind above Qena.

headline: Karnak by moonlight
summary: At Thebes Roosevelt walks ashore past the temple of Medinet Habu and the two seated colossi, hands resting on their knees. The boat ties up beside the Temple of Luxor, and that night he sees Karnak under the moon.

headline: Across the river to the Valley of the Kings
summary: Roosevelt crosses the Nile, sees temples on the Valley of the Kings side, and collects several birds.

headline: A Sunday stroll in Luxor
summary: Roosevelt spends the day walking around Luxor.

headline: Royal tombs and a wolf
summary: Roosevelt visits the tomb of Ramesses III and Belzoni's tomb, and on the way back shoots a wolf.

headline: Towed to Armant
summary: The boat is tracked upstream to Armant, where Theodore Sr. shoots a hawk.

headline: A long walk at Sharuna
summary: At Sharuna Roosevelt makes a long hike across a sandbank.

headline: Doves and a misfire near Edfu
summary: Above Edfu Roosevelt walks along the shore and gets some doves, though his gun misfires once.

headline: A full day's sail to Aswan
summary: The Ibis sails from morning to evening to reach Aswan.

headline: Philae by moonlight on Bamie's birthday
summary: Roosevelt hunts in the desert outside Aswan. Everyone dines aboard the Ibis, and by moonlight he sees the ruins at Philae. It is Bamie's eighteenth birthday.

headline: Elephantine Island and Philae by day
summary: After sleeping through much of the morning, Roosevelt visits Elephantine Island and returns to Philae to see it in daylight.

headline: A jackal in the desert
summary: Hunting in the desert near Aswan, Roosevelt sees a jackal.

headline: At the cataracts
summary: Roosevelt visits the Nile cataracts at Aswan.

headline: Desert hunting at Aswan
summary: Roosevelt spends the day hunting in the desert.

headline: Turning back downriver
summary: After one more desert hunt, the Ibis heads downstream in the afternoon. The family has to turn around because Theodore Sr. must be in Vienna by May 1.

headline: Kom Ombo at sunset
summary: Roosevelt hunts along the river and sees the ruins of Kom Ombo at sunset; the boat sails through the night.

headline: A cheerful letter to Aunt Annie
summary: Near Kom Ombo Roosevelt visits a ruin and writes to Aunt Annie Gracie that he is having a fine time.

headline: Edfu's temple, then shooting
summary: Roosevelt tours the temple at Edfu in the morning and shoots in the afternoon.

headline: El Kab's tombs and on to Isna
summary: Roosevelt sees the temple and tombs of El Kab, and the boat reaches Isna in the afternoon.

headline: The temple of Khnum
summary: At Isna Roosevelt sees the temple of Khnum and goes shooting.

headline: Back at Thebes
summary: Returning to Thebes, Roosevelt spends the day shooting.

headline: Fifteen birds and outgrown clothes
summary: On a daylong shooting trip at Thebes Roosevelt takes fifteen birds and visits Medinet Habu. He has shot up so much on the journey that his clothes no longer fit.

headline: Karnak and specimens
summary: At Thebes Roosevelt tours Karnak and collects some specimens. His sister Corinne writes to Edith Carow back home.

headline: Sunday services and Karnak again
summary: The family holds Sunday services, and Roosevelt returns to Karnak.

headline: A crane, snipe and pigeons
summary: Roosevelt goes out shooting and brings back a crane, snipe and pigeons, while his father and Ellie visit a tomb on the far bank.

headline: The temple of Dendera
summary: Stopping two days at Qena, the family visits the Temple of Dendera, and Roosevelt goes shooting.

headline: Shooting at Qena
summary: Roosevelt spends the day shooting at Qena.

headline: Rowing down to El Balyana
summary: The boat is rowed downstream to El Balyana, and Roosevelt shoots.

headline: Abydos and sixteen pigeons
summary: Roosevelt sees the temple at Abydos and kills sixteen pigeons.

headline: Meeting the Zingara
summary: After a morning of shooting, the crew rows all day, and the Ibis falls in with the boat Zingara.

headline: Father preaches to the Rachel's party
summary: The passengers of the Rachel come aboard to hear Theodore Sr. read a sermon. Roosevelt writes to Aunt Annie Gracie.

headline: Shooting and tea
summary: Roosevelt goes shooting and later takes tea.

headline: Shooting at Beni Hasan
summary: At Beni Hasan Roosevelt heads out to shoot.

headline: Rowing Ralph Waldo Emerson to lunch
summary: After touring the Beni Hasan tombs and shooting an owl, Roosevelt helps host Ralph Waldo Emerson and his daughter Ellen for lunch, rowing them over to the family boat himself. Ellen later wrote home describing the ruddy-cheeked, blue-eyed boy at the oars.

headline: Collision with the Moorkat
summary: Roosevelt shoots with his father near Beni Suef. The Ibis runs into another boat, the Moorkat, which smashes the front cabin.

headline: Rough sailing toward Memphis
summary: The boat sails all day toward Memphis, with choppy water in the afternoon.

headline: The Serapeum and back to Cairo
summary: At Memphis Roosevelt sees the Serapeum and the Apis pits, kills two ibises and arrives back in Cairo in the afternoon.

headline: Church in Cairo, still aboard
summary: The family goes to church in Cairo and continues living on the boat.

headline: Rainy day of collecting
summary: Still on the dahabeah, Roosevelt kills birds on a rainy day.

headline: Back to Shepheard's Hotel
summary: The family leaves the boat for Shepheard's Hotel; it rains.

headline: Lounging around a wet Cairo
summary: Roosevelt idles about the city in the rain.

headline: Calling on Dr. Grant
summary: On another rainy day Roosevelt visits Dr. Grant's.

headline: First look at the Suez Canal
summary: At Ismailia, Roosevelt sees the Suez Canal and stays at the Hotel Pagnon. The women of the family go by way of Alexandria to Port Said, where the men will meet them.

headline: Up the canal to Port Said
summary: Roosevelt takes a steamer up the canal to Port Said and stays at the Hotel de France. His asthma flares.

headline: Reunited aboard the steamer
summary: On board the steamer Alphe, Roosevelt and the men rejoin the rest of the party.

headline: Landing at Jaffa, a night in a monastery
summary: The party lands at Jaffa and rides three hours to Ramleh, lodging in a monastery. Theodore Sr. persuades the monks to let the women stay as well.

headline: Racing Mr. Jay to Jerusalem
summary: Roosevelt shoots a kestrel and a lark, then rides to Jerusalem, outracing Mr. Jay on horseback. He finds the city surprisingly small; the family stays at the Damascus Hotel.

headline: Holy Sepulchre and Gethsemane
summary: Roosevelt visits the Church of the Holy Sepulchre and the Garden of Gethsemane.

headline: The Dome of the Rock
summary: Roosevelt sees the Mosque of Omar.

headline: Wailing Wall on Ellie's birthday
summary: After a morning hunt, Roosevelt goes to the Wailing Wall and the tombs of the judges and kings. Ellie turns thirteen.

headline: Photographs and a ride
summary: Roosevelt visits a convent, buys photographs and goes riding.

headline: Sunday church in Jerusalem
summary: Roosevelt attends church in Jerusalem.

headline: Caravan to Jericho
summary: Roosevelt sets out on horseback for the Dead Sea over a rough road. The caravan counts some 35 pack animals and 25 people, with Bedouin guards, and camps near Jericho.

headline: Floating in the Dead Sea
summary: Roosevelt bathes in the Jordan, which strikes him as no bigger than a creek, then swims in the Dead Sea and finds he can't sink.

headline: Bethlehem and the Nativity
summary: After a convent visit, the party rides to Bethlehem by way of the Pools of Solomon. Theodore Sr. pays guards to let them into the site of the Nativity.

headline: Hebron and Abraham's Oak
summary: Roosevelt rides to Hebron, sees Abraham's Oak and the mosque, and goes shooting.

headline: Rain in Jerusalem
summary: Back in Jerusalem, the day is rainy.

headline: Riding back to Ramleh
summary: The party rides to Ramleh.

headline: Farewell to a horse named Grant
summary: Roosevelt rides to Jaffa and boards ship, where he is seasick. He is sad to say goodbye to the horse he rode and named Grant.

headline: Asthma in Beirut
summary: The family sails to Beirut and stays at the Hotel d'Orient. Roosevelt rides a horse and suffers an asthma attack.

headline: Trying out horses
summary: In Beirut the party tests horses for the overland trip.

headline: Seven hours to Ain Tufeh
summary: A ride of about seven hours brings the party to Ain Tufeh. Roosevelt and Ellie are stuck with poor mounts.

headline: Off the Diligence Road to Abla
summary: The party follows the Diligence Road until lunch, then turns off and meets people at Abla.

headline: The ruins of Baalbek
summary: A three-hour canter from Abla brings Roosevelt to the grand ruins of Baalbek, where he shoots a finch.

headline: A cold night in tents
summary: After shooting several birds in the morning, the party rides to Syrahayi and spends a bitterly cold night in tents.

headline: Asthma and stomach sickness
summary: The party rides to Sukr El Wady. That night Roosevelt is struck by a severe asthma attack along with cholera morbus.

headline: Chasing jackals toward Damascus
summary: On a showery day Roosevelt hunts and spots jackals that had killed a goat; he gives chase but they escape. The party reaches Damascus.

headline: Haggling in the bazaar
summary: Roosevelt sees the horse market in Damascus and bargains in the bazaars for a suit.

headline: Up a minaret of 220 steps
summary: Roosevelt tours the Mosque of St. John, climbs a 220-step minaret for the view, and goes shooting with the British consul.

headline: Several birds near Damascus
summary: Roosevelt goes shooting and brings back several birds.

headline: Consulate men to dinner
summary: After another day of shooting, men from the British consulate dine with the family.

headline: Ten changes of horses to Beirut
summary: On the road back to Beirut, Roosevelt sees gazelles; the party switches horses ten times.

headline: Ellie falls ill
summary: In Beirut, Ellie is sick; Roosevelt goes to church.

headline: Dinner at the Blisses'
summary: Roosevelt and Conie dine with Mr. Bliss and his family while Ellie remains ill.

headline: Boarding an Austrian steamer
summary: The family sails from Beirut at seven aboard an Austrian steamer; Ellie is still sick.

headline: Off Cyprus
summary: The steamer passes Cyprus. Ellie is still unwell.

headline: Birds land on deck
summary: Far from land, birds alight on the ship, and Roosevelt pays to have them so he can skin them. Ellie is still ill.

headline: Specimens from the sailors off Rhodes
summary: The sea is too rough to land at Rhodes, but sailors catch specimens for Roosevelt. In the afternoon the ship runs along the coast of Asia Minor, and Ellie improves.

headline: Changing ships at Smyrna
summary: The steamer reaches Smyrna, where the family transfers to another ship.

headline: Candy and tag on a paddle steamer
summary: On a small paddle-wheeler bound for Athens, Roosevelt buys candy, gets seasick and plays tag.

headline: First look at the Acropolis
summary: Seasick still, Roosevelt reaches Piraeus and takes a carriage up to Athens, where he sees the Acropolis. The men and women of the party lodge at separate hotels.

headline: Touring ancient Athens
summary: By carriage, Roosevelt tours the ruins of the Olympieion, a Greek theater, the Acropolis and the Parthenon, in the rain.

headline: Areopagus, then a ship for Constantinople
summary: Roosevelt goes back to the Acropolis and climbs the Areopagus, then drives to Piraeus to board an Italian steamer for Constantinople.

headline: Walking around Smyrna
summary: The steamer reaches Smyrna in the afternoon, and Roosevelt walks through the town.

headline: A late departure
summary: The steamer does not get under way until six in the evening.

headline: Through the Dardanelles
summary: The ship passes through the Dardanelles and the Sea of Marmara while Roosevelt plays on deck.

headline: Ashore at Constantinople
summary: At Constantinople the family rows ashore, walks to the Hotel d'Angleterre, and attends church.

headline: Candle fight with the Lawrence boys
summary: Roosevelt rides out with Frank and Tom Lawrence, who stay for dinner and games of muggins. He, Ellie and Tom end up in a candle fight, flinging hot wax at each other. He writes Edith Carow, mentioning that he has lost his gun.

headline: The old city walls
summary: Roosevelt visits the ancient walls and towers of Constantinople.

headline: Thrown from his horse
summary: Sightseeing on horseback while the others ride in carriages, Roosevelt is thrown. He sees the Süleymaniye Mosque and Hagia Sophia and is sick that night.

headline: A quiet day in Constantinople
summary: Nothing much happens.

headline: A glimpse of the Sultan
summary: The Lawrences and Roosevelts go together to the Sultan's palace, and Roosevelt sees the Sultan.

headline: The Lawrences depart
summary: The Lawrence family leaves for Brindisi.

headline: Sunday church in Constantinople
summary: Roosevelt attends church.

headline: Midnight sailing into the Black Sea
summary: The family boards a steamer at ten in the evening and sets out at midnight across the Black Sea toward Romania.

headline: Varna and a Danube riverboat
summary: Seasick, Roosevelt reaches Varna at six in the evening and transfers to a riverboat on the Danube.

headline: Up the green Danube, gasping
summary: The riverboat steams up the Danube all day through green, rolling country, and Roosevelt suffers a severe asthma attack.

headline: From boat to train
summary: Between Serbia and Austria the family changes boats and then boards a train.

headline: Arriving in Pest
summary: The family reaches Pest around one o'clock, stays at the King of England Hotel, visits a picture gallery and climbs the hill.

headline: Vienna, and Father's exposition duties
summary: The family checks into the Grand Hotel in Vienna. Theodore Sr., who sits on the exposition's board of directors, prepares for its opening.

headline: Sunday church in Vienna
summary: Roosevelt goes to church.

headline: An idle day in Vienna
summary: Nothing in particular fills the day.

headline: Cousins arrive in Vienna
summary: Cousin West Roosevelt, Frank, Aunt Mary and the Misses Tiny and Gertrude Roosevelt pay a visit. Roosevelt buys a rabbit, dissects it, and plays.

headline: In Vienna
summary: Roosevelt is in Vienna; nothing more is recorded.

headline: A week of pleasant sameness
summary: Roosevelt sums up the past week in Vienna in his diary as pleasantly uneventful, spent skinning birds or rabbits. West leaves for Bonn, and Ellie and Theodore Sr. go to Dresden.

headline: Suits of armor at the Ambras collection
summary: Roosevelt goes to see the Ambras collection and its armor.

headline: Panic on the Vienna exchange
summary: Roosevelt is in Vienna as a financial panic hits the city.

headline: Vienna's world's fair opens without him
summary: The great 1873 international exposition opens its doors in Vienna, where the Roosevelt family is staying. Young Roosevelt will not get his first look at it for two more days.

summary: The record places Roosevelt in Vienna but notes nothing more for the day.

headline: First quick look at the exposition
summary: Roosevelt gets his first, brief look around the Vienna exposition, two days after it opened.

headline: An American church opens in Vienna
summary: A church for Americans living in Vienna holds its opening service; twenty-seven worshippers turn out.

headline: Books, birds and a growing congregation
summary: The past few weeks in Vienna have felt dull and repetitive, the record notes, with Roosevelt putting his money toward books and bird specimens. At the American church, attendance has climbed to nearly 200.

headline: Back to the Vienna exposition
summary: Roosevelt returns to the great Vienna exposition for another visit.

headline: Quiet day in Vienna

headline: Night train out of Vienna
summary: At ten in the evening Roosevelt, his brother Elliott and their father Theodore Sr. set off from Vienna bound for Dresden. His travel journal ends here.

headline: Settled with a German family in Dresden
summary: Roosevelt and Elliott move in with the Minkwitz household in Dresden, parents plus three daughters and two sons, to soak up German. headline: Understanding more German than they think
summary: In a letter to his mother, Roosevelt reports that the Minkwitz family assume his German is too weak to follow their remarks about the Roosevelts.

headline: A schoolboy's day in Dresden
summary: Roosevelt's Dresden schedule runs from a 6:30 wake-up through nearly a full day of lessons, broken by lunch, coffee and free afternoons, until bed at ten. Anna Minkwitz drills him and Elliott in German grammar and arithmetic. Homesick Corinne moves in to join her brothers, and his collection now counts 40 animals and 220 coins.

summary: Corinne tells her friend Edith Carow about a club the five American children in Dresden have formed. Each Sunday they gather at Aunt Lucy's to share the poems and stories they wrote that week. Cousins Johnny and Maud Elliott live close by with Aunt Lucy.

headline: Butterfly net in hand on a Saxon outing
summary: Roosevelt joins Elliott and the Minkwitz sisters, Anna and Lina, on a day trip outside Dresden, carrying his butterfly net. Part of the way they travel by boat and catch sight of a castle.

headline: A black eye from boxing Johnny
summary: Roosevelt squares off in a boxing match with Johnnie and comes out the loser, sporting a large black eye.

headline: Confiscated arsenic and evicted mice
summary: Roosevelt writes his father about church and the children's writing club, and tells Aunt Annie that Corinne has joined him and Elliott. His hosts have seized the arsenic he used for preserving specimens and flung his pet mice out the window with tongs.

headline: Bloody nose, then a swim in the Elbe
summary: This time it is Elliott who wins the boxing bout, leaving his brother with a bloody nose. Afterward the boys go swimming in the Elbe.

headline: Sunday club at Aunt Lucy's
summary: Roosevelt heads to Aunt Lucy's for the children's Sunday club, and writes his father about Edward Jacobs, a friend of Johnny's.

headline: Downplaying a hard asthma spell
summary: Writing to his father, Roosevelt treats his asthma as a small matter, though the attack is in fact severe. The letter later appeared in his sister Corinne's memoir of him.

headline: Sent to the Bastei for his health
summary: To help his health, Roosevelt is taken to the Bastei with Elliott, Corinne and the Fräuleins Anna and Emma. He hunts butterflies and reads the Nibelungenlied for the first time. Back in New York, his father watches builders at work on the family's new 57th Street house and on the natural history museum, lodging at the Union League Club meanwhile.

headline: The DLAC sits for a photograph
summary: Roosevelt, Elliott, Corinne and cousins Maud and John Elliott pose for a picture as the Dresden Literary American Club, whose motto 'W.A.N.A.' stood for 'We Are No Asses.' Corinne wrote the poems, Elliott and John the tragedies, and Roosevelt the comic tales, among them 'Mrs. Field Mouse's Dinner Party.'

headline: Caught up with Elliott in grammar
summary: On Independence Day Roosevelt assures his father that the Bastei trip cost him nothing in his studies: extra lessons have brought him level with Elliott in grammar and ahead in writing and poetry. Elliott, writing the same day, asks their father whether America isn't the finest country anywhere.

summary: Roosevelt is struck by another asthma attack along with a severe headache.

summary: Behind closed doors, Roscoe Conkling argues against Roosevelt's father, and his nomination to run New York's customhouse fails a second time. Roosevelt is at college in Cambridge.

headline: Quiet day at Harvard

headline: Father speaks to the Tribune
summary: The New York Tribune reports that Roosevelt's father was reluctant to comment on his defeat, describing it as a contest between party bosses and President Hayes. Roosevelt is at Harvard.

headline: A win in the ring, gains in class
summary: Roosevelt soundly beats a red-haired classmate named Coolidge in a gymnasium boxing match and notes that his grades are running ahead of his freshman year.

headline: Uneasy about Father
summary: Roosevelt tells Bamie he is worried about their father, whom the Senate turned down for the Collectorship by a vote of 31 to 25. The same day his father writes about corruption in government.

headline: Unrecorded day in Cambridge
summary: The chronology places Roosevelt in Cambridge and logs no letters or events.

headline: Father stricken in New York
summary: In New York, Roosevelt's father collapses with what is called acute peritonitis and is gravely ill. That same night Bamie hosts a party and Corinne stays up until 2 a.m. Roosevelt is still in Cambridge.

headline: No entry for the day at college
summary: Roosevelt is at college in Cambridge, with no activity written down.

headline: Aunt Annie comes to help
summary: Roosevelt's father remains very sick in New York, and Aunt Annie Gracie arrives to support the family. Roosevelt is at Harvard.

headline: Called home to Father's bedside
summary: Word reaches Roosevelt in Cambridge that his father is very ill, and he hurries to New York.

headline: Museum opens without Father
summary: The American Museum of Natural History holds its grand opening, but Roosevelt's father, one of its founders, is too sick to go. It is also his parents' 24th wedding anniversary.

headline: Father rallies on Christmas Eve
summary: Roosevelt finds his father much improved. Aunt Annie Gracie helps lay the table and fill the stockings for Christmas.

headline: A shotgun for Christmas
summary: Roosevelt's father seems brighter on Christmas Day, and Roosevelt gets a double-barreled shotgun. The family sits down to dinner without his parents. His diary for the year closes here.

headline: With family in New York
summary: No activity is written down for this day beyond Roosevelt's presence in New York.

summary: Roosevelt and Edith Carow visit Aunt Annie Gracie's house in New York for cream taffy.

headline: Another blank day at home
summary: Only his location survives for this day: New York City.

summary: Roosevelt is home in New York City; nothing else is recorded.

headline: Tallying a year of specimens
summary: Roosevelt closes the year by counting his natural history collections: 16 mammals, 68 birds, 17 reptiles, 61 amphibians and 10 fishes. A separate list of game shot includes a buck, ten ducks, a dozen snipe, three grouse and six plover.

headline: New Year's calls and three dear friends
summary: Roosevelt makes about twenty New Year's Day calls in New York. In his diary he praises Annie Murray and Fanny Smith, and counts Edith Carow as the third of his close girl friends.

headline: Father's blessing, a spill, back to school
summary: Roosevelt's father tells him he has never given him a moment's pain, words Roosevelt treasures. A sleigh overturns and drags him behind the horses, which he calls great fun, and he heads back to Harvard.

headline: Back at his books
summary: Roosevelt returns to Cambridge and picks up his college work.

headline: Taking stock of family and friends
summary: Missing home, Roosevelt fills a diary page with thoughts on his family and friends: Elliott has grown up, Jack Elliott is his closest friend after his brother, and Hal Minot, Will Blodgett, Minot Weld and Harry Chapin look like college friends in the making.

headline: At Harvard, nothing noted
summary: Only his location survives for this day: Cambridge, at college.

headline: Teaching Sunday school again
summary: Roosevelt is back in front of his Sunday school class, his regular weekend duty.

headline: Sizing up the term ahead
summary: With classes rolling again, Roosevelt predicts strong marks everywhere but French and expects to shine in natural history. He is sparring with a boxing instructor five days a week, aiming at the lightweight cups.

headline: Kind words for his science teachers
summary: Roosevelt notes in his diary how helpful and friendly he finds Harvard's natural history faculty.

headline: Dinner with Agassiz
summary: Roosevelt dines with Agassiz and enjoys the evening.

headline: Dinner with 'Piggy' Everett
summary: Roosevelt dines with the man students called 'Piggy' Everett and finds him cultured and charming, if unwashed.

headline: A day without an entry
summary: Roosevelt is a Harvard student in Cambridge; the record is silent otherwise.

headline: Dancing class and Boston belles
summary: Roosevelt goes to dancing class and admires several Boston girls, among them Carrie Goodwin, Bessie Whitney, the Rotch sisters and Pauline Revere. He stays over with Arthur Hooper until Monday.

headline: Jeannie Hooper reads aloud
summary: At the Hoopers', Roosevelt passes a happy evening listening to Jeannie Hooper read, and calls her an unusually sweet girl.

headline: Bird club with Hal Minot
summary: Roosevelt attends a meeting of the Nuttall Ornithological Club with his friend Hal Minot and takes a liking to Brewster and Allen.

headline: Quiet day at Harvard
summary: Roosevelt is at Harvard in Cambridge; the record notes nothing else for the day.

headline: An evening party at the Hoopers'
summary: Roosevelt enjoys a party at the Hooper family's home.

headline: Theatre night on Bamie's birthday
summary: On his sister Bamie's 23rd birthday, Roosevelt spends the evening at the theatre with a group of friends.

headline: Dinner with Harry Shaw
summary: Roosevelt has dinner with his friend Harry Shaw and then heads to a party.

headline: No entry for the day at college

summary: Roosevelt joins the Hooper family for an evening party.

headline: Beats Briggs in the ring
summary: Roosevelt spars with a smaller classmate named Briggs and comes out on top.

headline: A perfect score in natural history
summary: Roosevelt earns 100 percent on a Natural History 3 exam, then spends the afternoon and weekend at Minot Weld's home and goes to dancing class that night.

headline: At Harvard, nothing noted
summary: Only his location survives for this day: Cambridge, at college.

headline: Paper on English sparrows
summary: Roosevelt reads a paper on the English sparrow to the Nuttall Ornithological Club in Cambridge.

headline: A party with friends and the Lane sisters
summary: Roosevelt goes to a party with Minot Weld, Harry Chapin, Bessie Whitney and the two Lane sisters, whom he finds delightful.

headline: Edged out by Bob Bacon
summary: Roosevelt loses a close boxing match to classmate Robert Bacon, though by his own account not by much.

headline: A day without an entry
summary: Roosevelt is a Harvard student in Cambridge; the record is silent otherwise.

headline: Wrestling win over Tebbetts
summary: Roosevelt puts Jack Tebbetts on the mat in a wrestling bout.

headline: Calling with Arthur Hooper
summary: Roosevelt makes a round of social visits with Arthur Hooper.

headline: Sunday with the Hoopers
summary: Roosevelt spends a pleasant Sunday at the Hoopers' and admits that his regard for Jeannie Hooper keeps rising.

headline: Quiet day at Harvard
summary: Roosevelt is at Harvard in Cambridge; the record notes nothing else for the day.

headline: Gets ahead in required history
summary: Roosevelt takes the second-half exam in required history early and scores 83 percent.

headline: Unrecorded day in Cambridge
summary: The chronology places Roosevelt in Cambridge and logs no letters or events.

headline: Top marks, and Father out on a sleigh
summary: Roosevelt scores 91 percent on his midyear history exam and goes sleighing in Cambridge. In New York his father is strong enough to go sleighing with Bamie, and smiles when Mittie reads him a letter from his son.

headline: A second sleigh ride ends in agony
summary: In New York, Roosevelt's father goes sleighing again but is in terrible pain by the time he returns, and a doctor is called. Roosevelt is still at Harvard.

headline: Racing home as Father lies dying
summary: Summoned by urgent word that his father is gravely ill with a bowel tumor, Roosevelt boards the night train for New York. Theodore Sr., 46, dies late that night, hours before his son can reach him.

headline: Flags at half mast for Father
summary: Roosevelt reaches New York to find flags lowered for his father. Orphans and newsboys, the children his father spent his life helping, fill the street and steps outside the 57th Street house.

headline: Home in New York, nothing noted
summary: Roosevelt is home in New York City; nothing else is recorded.

headline: Father laid to rest at Green-Wood
summary: After a short service at home and another at the church on 57th Street, the family crosses by ferry to Green-Wood Cemetery to bury Roosevelt's father. Roosevelt, shattered, pours out his grief in his diary and resolves to live as his father would have wished.

headline: Unrecorded day in New York
summary: The chronology places Roosevelt in New York and notes no events.

headline: Quiet day in the city
summary: Roosevelt is in New York City with his family; the day has no entry.

headline: 'I owe everything to him'
summary: Roosevelt writes a tribute to his father in his diary, remembering his wisdom, his fairness and his unselfishness, and blaming himself for having done nothing for him.

headline: With family in New York
summary: No activity is written down for this day beyond Roosevelt's presence in New York.

headline: Visiting Father's poor and old pupils
summary: Roosevelt calls on some of the poor families his father helped, who speak movingly of him, and is glad to see the boys from his old mission class again.

headline: Praise for Elliott and Bamie
summary: Roosevelt writes that the whole family stood by his father during his illness, singling out his brother Elliott and sister Bamie.

headline: 'A father to the poor'
summary: Roosevelt struggles to accept that he will not see his father again and borrows a line from the Book of Job to describe him.

headline: Grateful for Uncle Jimmie's comfort
summary: Roosevelt thanks everyone for their kindness, above all Uncle James Gracie, and writes Hal Minot that his letter lifted the family's spirits.

headline: Hardest on Mother and his sisters
summary: Roosevelt writes that the loss falls hardest on his mother and sisters, though it is terrible for all of them.

headline: Like a hideous dream
summary: Roosevelt confides that at times his father's death still feels unreal.

headline: Returning to college a grieving son
summary: Roosevelt returns to Cambridge for his first night at college since the funeral. He notes an income of about $8,000 a year from his father's estate, enough to live comfortably.

headline: Living memories of Father
summary: Alone at college on a Sunday, Roosevelt addresses his father directly in his diary.

headline: Back to work, moved by his boxing coach
summary: Roosevelt is working hard again and is touched by the sympathy of his boxing instructor.

headline: Friends rally around him
summary: Roosevelt is grateful for the kindness of his college friends, especially Hal Minot, and notes Harry Shaw's thoughtfulness.

headline: Let down by Will Blodgett
summary: Roosevelt admits in his diary that Will Blodgett has fallen short of his hopes.

headline: Exams, Elliott's birthday and sparrows in print
summary: On his brother Elliott's 18th birthday, Roosevelt, turning down all invitations until May, does well on two midyear exams and tells his mother the boys have been kind. A journal called The Country prints a short summary of his views on English sparrows.

headline: Grateful for kind professors
summary: Roosevelt notes how considerate his Harvard teachers have been in the weeks since his father's death.

headline: A day spent dissecting a seal
summary: Roosevelt devotes most of the day to dissecting a seal.

headline: A good cry and a long ride
summary: After an evening of thinking about his father, Roosevelt lets himself break down and feels better for it. He rides twenty miles on his horse Lightfoot and writes Conie, who is in Philadelphia with their mother and Aunt Susan West.

headline: Leaning on Bamie
summary: Roosevelt writes that the loss is only now sinking in. He asks Bamie for her counsel, telling her she resembles their father more than anyone else in the family.

headline: First glass ball shoot
summary: At the first meeting of a glass ball shooting club, Roosevelt breaks 11 of 25 targets. He forces himself to keep busy but cannot yet face socializing with classmates.

headline: 'Thy will be done'
summary: Roosevelt admits to bitter moments and fears what too much idle time might do to him, yet finds he can accept his loss with humble faith.

headline: Dreaming of a life in science
summary: Measuring himself against his father, Roosevelt feels his own life is weak by comparison. He writes that he would like to become a scientist and will miss his father's advice.

headline: Eleven of 22 at the glass ball club
summary: At another Glass Ball Club meeting, Roosevelt hits 11 of 22 targets.

headline: A month since his father died
summary: The lightweight wrestling matches he had trained for take place, but they feel distant now. Roosevelt marks one month since his father's death, the worst day he has known.

headline: Comforting his mother by letter
summary: Roosevelt teaches Sunday school, then breaks down again thinking of his father. He writes Mittie a tender letter wishing he could be at her side.

headline: Busy enough not to brood
summary: Roosevelt counts himself lucky that a full schedule leaves little time for dwelling on his loss.

headline: Letters from home, none to Father
summary: Roosevelt treasures the loving letters from his family and finds it strange no longer to write to his father.

headline: Coaching Billy Gaston
summary: Roosevelt helps prepare his classmate Billy Gaston for an upcoming wrestling match.

headline: Not ready for Boston society
summary: Roosevelt confesses he still cannot bring himself to visit his friends in Boston.

headline: Father's letters as a talisman
summary: Roosevelt rereads his father's affectionate letters and vows to keep them as a guard against wrongdoing.

headline: Watching the sparring, walking with Dick Morgan
summary: Roosevelt watches a boxing contest and goes on a long walk with Dick Morgan.

headline: Communion Sunday and John 14
summary: On Communion Sunday Roosevelt teaches his class and reads John 14, one of his father's favorite chapters. He writes to comfort Bamie, saying that being at school makes the pain easier for him to bear.

headline: 98 percent in German
summary: Roosevelt scores 98 percent on an hour-long German exam.

headline: Rereading his Egyptian journal
summary: Paging through the journal he kept in Egypt as a boy, Roosevelt finds his father in every scene. He aches for his mother and sisters and wishes he were home.

headline: Quiet day at Harvard
summary: Roosevelt is at Harvard in Cambridge; the record notes nothing else for the day.

headline: Counting his blessings
summary: Roosevelt writes that his father seems part of his own self, and that every event in his life is tied to him. Still, he feels luckier in his family than most men.

headline: Unrecorded day in Cambridge
summary: The chronology places Roosevelt in Cambridge and logs no letters or events.

headline: 95 on a natural history exam
summary: Roosevelt sits a three-hour natural history examination and scores 95 percent, then watches the Athletic Club's third meeting.

headline: Father's rule: morals, health, studies
summary: After Sunday school, Roosevelt writes home and reminds Mittie of his father's order of priorities: character first, then health, then schoolwork.

headline: Tutoring Arthur Hooper in German
summary: Roosevelt is coaching Arthur Hooper in German, admiring his friend's love of poetry and athletic skill. He also boxes Teschmaker and thinks he wins.

headline: 'Father, companion, friend'
summary: In a long diary entry Roosevelt recalls his father's habits, down to the curl that would not lie flat. He marvels that he has carried on with daily life, and calls his father everything to him.

summary: Roosevelt is at college in Cambridge, with no activity written down.

summary: No events survive for this day beyond Roosevelt's presence at Harvard.

headline: A rare book on Italian wildlife
summary: Roosevelt scores 90 percent on a three-hour German midyear and buys a copy of Bonaparte's Fauna Italica, a scarce natural history work.

headline: No man did more good than Father
summary: After Sunday school, Roosevelt writes that no one in New York did as much good as his father or was so loved at home.

headline: Bruised by Bacon, bird club at night
summary: Robert Bacon wears Roosevelt out in a sparring match. He then outshoots Minot Weld at glass balls, though with a poor 6 of 10, and spends the evening at the Nuttall Ornithological Club.

headline: Longing for home, dreading it too
summary: Roosevelt can hardly wait to see his family yet fears walking into a house without his father. He writes that every happy family memory includes him.

summary: The day passes without a recorded event; Roosevelt is at Harvard.
