summary: Back at Chestnut Hill, Roosevelt says how fond he is of the whole Lee family and spends the entire day with Alice.

headline: Alice takes the reins
summary: Alice drives Roosevelt out for a carriage ride, and he records how happy he is.

headline: Dreading six weeks apart
summary: Roosevelt stays close to Alice, already miserable at the thought of the six-week separation that begins in two days.

headline: Reading Hawthorne and Thackeray aloud
summary: Roosevelt spends another full day with Alice, reading to her from Hawthorne and Thackeray. Both love poetry, especially Longfellow and parts of Shelley and Swinburne.

headline: Farewell to Alice, night train south
summary: After a last happy day together, Roosevelt says goodbye to Alice for what he expects will be six or seven weeks and boards the overnight train to New York.

headline: Shopping, then out to Oyster Bay
summary: Roosevelt spends the day shopping in New York and goes out to Oyster Bay that evening, finding his mother there along with Aunt Susie, Uncle Hill and two members of the Locke family.

headline: Tennis and canoeing
summary: Roosevelt plays tennis with Frank and goes out paddling in his cousin Emlen's canoe.

headline: Packing for the West
summary: Roosevelt gets his gear ready for a western hunting trip, and also walks in the woods and takes his mother out in the light wagon.

headline: Elliott arrives; homesick for Alice
summary: His brother Elliott turns up while the family is at church. Roosevelt confesses he is painfully lonely for Alice and thinks of her constantly.

headline: Off to Chicago with Elliott
summary: Roosevelt and Elliott board the overnight train for Chicago to begin a western hunting trip.

headline: Rolling west through Ohio
summary: The brothers ride all day across Pennsylvania's forested hills and Ohio's prairies. Roosevelt delights in traveling with Elliott, noting that the two of them keep their tempers and get things done.

headline: Sweltering Chicago, and a guide found
summary: In Chicago, a big Freemasons' gathering makes rooms scarce and the heat is fierce. That evening the brothers meet a man named Wilcox and agree to go to his farm until September.

headline: First prairie chicken in Illinois
summary: At Wilcox's farm near Huntley, sixty miles out of Chicago, the brothers hunt prairie chickens across the open fields. Elliott misses his bird; Roosevelt drops his. He finds the open-country shooting new and fun, though the farm food is coarse.

headline: A four-hour grouse tramp
summary: The brothers spend four hours walking the fields after prairie chickens. Elliott outshoots Roosevelt, four grouse to one.

headline: A day's shooting by wagon
summary: Roosevelt and Elliott set out by wagon, stopping wherever the cover looked good to hunt stubble and pasture for chickens and the sloughs for ducks, snipe and plover. He calls it one of his most pleasant days.

headline: Hymns with the farmhands
summary: Roosevelt admits Elliott is the better shot but says he is getting better. He likes the farm men despite the plain pork-and-potatoes fare, misses Alice terribly, and that night joins everyone in singing hymns. He writes Corinne and Bamie about it.

headline: Elliott's day with the gun
summary: On a full day's wagon hunt, Roosevelt shoots worse than ever while Elliott seems to hit nearly everything he aims at.

headline: A wet dawn with few birds
summary: The brothers head out before sunrise through soaking prairie grass, but birds are scarce and both shoot poorly.

headline: Rained in with a rowdy crew
summary: Rain keeps the brothers indoors. Two farmhands, a Texan and an Irish youth, get roaring drunk and Roosevelt braces for a brawl that never comes. He tells his mother in a letter how shabbily dressed he and Elliott are.

headline: Poor luck, constant thoughts of Alice
summary: A day of shooting yields little. Roosevelt writes that Alice is his first thought on waking and his last at night.

headline: The fields are hunted out
summary: A morning on foot turns up no game at all. Roosevelt decides the area has been shot clean and plans to leave the next day.

headline: Back to comfort at the Sherman House
summary: The brothers return to Chicago and check into the Sherman House, which feels like a palace after the rough farmhouse.

headline: A Methodist service in Chicago
summary: Roosevelt goes to a Methodist church and admires the earnest, if startling, preacher, noting that most of the congregation are men, unlike the usual crowd.

headline: Sightseeing while waiting for Wilcox
summary: Stuck in Chicago until Wilcox is ready to head west with them, the brothers take in the city's sights.

headline: Turkish bath, theater and a hunting portrait
summary: Still waiting for Wilcox, Roosevelt fills the day with a drive, reading, whist, the theater, a long walk and a Turkish bath. He and Elliott sit for a studio photograph in their hunting clothes, but his longing for Alice keeps growing.

headline: Wilcox finally appears
summary: Wilcox at last shows up, and the brothers expect to head west within a couple of days.

headline: Impressed by Chicago
summary: Roosevelt writes Bamie that Chicago is a remarkable city, huge and wealthy.

headline: Heading west at last
summary: The hunting party sets out from Chicago: Roosevelt, Elliott, an engineer and a former Confederate soldier.

headline: Out on the Iowa prairie
summary: Arriving at Carroll, Iowa, before dawn, the party heads straight out by wagon over the open, unfenced prairie and does not return until 9 p.m. Birds are plentiful and Roosevelt shoots his best yet, despite colic and asthma.

headline: Twenty-five miles south over treeless hills
summary: After breakfast the party drives about 25 miles south through low, bare, thinly settled hills and spends the night at a rough farmhouse. Birds are few and skittish, but Roosevelt shoots as well as Elliott or better.

headline: A lame horse and a near upset
summary: The party works back over the prairie, the dogs mixed in quality. They return after dark with a horse lame and the wagon nearly overturned in a mudhole. Roosevelt loves the cross-country driving and outshoots Elliott.

headline: Snakebite by a bayou
summary: Driving toward Wall Lake, Roosevelt shoots chickens in tall grass, then wades hip-deep in mud to retrieve snipe and is bitten by a snake as he climbs out. The night is spent at a tidy little farmhouse.

headline: Sunrise and pelicans on Wall Lake
summary: Roosevelt hunts yellowlegs along the lakeshore at dawn and admires the sunrise, a big flock of pelicans and thousands of yellow-headed blackbirds. He shoots badly later, while Elliott excels. Asthma bothers him, yet he can walk all day.

headline: His last gun breaks
summary: In crisp fall weather the party bags some two dozen chickens before dinner. Paddling the lake with Elliott in an old flat-bottom boat, Roosevelt's second gun breaks, leaving him without one.

headline: Thrown from the wagon
summary: On the drive back to Carroll the wagon nearly overturns on a large rock, pitching Roosevelt and the driver out headfirst, though neither is badly hurt. He catches the overnight train to Chicago.

headline: Safely in Chicago
summary: Roosevelt arrives back in Chicago without mishap.

headline: Communion and family letters
summary: Roosevelt takes communion at a Methodist church. He reflects that the trip has helped his health but cannot make up for being away from Alice. He writes Corinne, poking fun at Elliott's eating and drinking, and tells his mother the sport has been decent.

headline: New guns, and parting ways
summary: Roosevelt and Elliott buy new guns, split from their two companions, whom they dislike, and take the night train toward St. Paul. Their goal is a reunion in Moorhead, Minnesota, with their cousin Jack Elliott.

headline: To Moorhead with a bobtailed pointer
summary: Armed with two new guns and an old short-tailed pointer, the brothers leave St. Paul in the evening for Moorhead, on the Dakota line, to see Jack Elliott.

headline: Sharp-tailed grouse and cousin Jack
summary: At Moorhead the brothers drive out to vast stubble fields and hunt a new kind of grouse until the old pointer tangles with a skunk. Back at their poor hotel they find cousin Jack Elliott and talk late into the night.

headline: A day with Jack
summary: Roosevelt spends the day with Jack Elliott, whom he has not seen in almost two years, and says he feels strong and healthy.

headline: First jackrabbits
summary: A serious old German drives the brothers north past the Buffalo River to hunt grouse and ducks. Roosevelt sees jackrabbits for the first time, and they ride five miles by full moon to a settler's house for the night.

headline: Best day's sport, despite asthma
summary: The brothers find countless grouse, but Roosevelt, up much of the night with asthma and plagued by colic and rain, shoots badly while Elliott excels. He longs to get back to Alice.

headline: Lost on the prairie in the rain
summary: In cold, lashing rain the party drives more than thirty miles, loses its way more than once, and ends at a Norwegian settler's home. When the sky clears near sunset they bag ducks and grouse.

headline: Sleeping under a buffalo robe
summary: Roosevelt beds down on a settler's floor beneath a buffalo robe while a gale howls outside, then hunts ducks in the cornfields and chickens across the fields all day in wind and rain. He says he feels in superb health.

headline: Camping on the Buffalo River
summary: On a cold, clear day the brothers cross country by wagon, nearly bog down in a slough, shoot grouse and ducks, and drop two geese from a passing flock while hiding behind wheat sheaves. They camp in the timber by the Buffalo River and dine on roast duck and chicken by a big fire.

headline: No tent, no frying pan
summary: Another day of hunting stubble fields for chickens and sharp-tailed grouse, with both brothers shooting well. They again sleep on the ground by the river, with no tent or proper outfit, not even a frying pan.

headline: Head over heels in a mudhole
summary: Roosevelt has great fun wading after ducks in a big slough until he tumbles headfirst into a mudhole, gun and all. That evening the brothers are back in Moorhead with Jack Elliott. He calls it his best hunt ever, though he aches to see Alice.

headline: Tallying the bag: 404 head
summary: Roosevelt spends the day with Jack Elliott and totals the trip's game in his diary: 203 for himself and 201 for Elliott, 404 in all, mostly grouse, with ducks, plover, yellowlegs and much else.

headline: Homeward bound
summary: The brothers leave Moorhead for St. Paul. Roosevelt has loved the trip, but is gladder still that it is over and Alice is near.

headline: Back through Chicago
summary: Roosevelt arrives in Chicago on the way east.

headline: Leaving Chicago on Corinne's birthday
summary: Roosevelt departs Chicago heading east. At home, his sister Corinne turns 19.

headline: A stop at Niagara Falls
summary: Roosevelt breaks his journey east with a stop at Niagara Falls.

headline: Racing to Alice
summary: Roosevelt reaches New York, collects a suitcase Bamie packed for him at the family home on West 57th Street, and hurries on to Chestnut Hill that evening to be reunited with Alice.

headline: Happiness almost too great
summary: Reunited with Alice, Roosevelt writes that she is unchanged yet somehow even more charming, and that he cannot bear to have her out of his sight.

headline: A day with his fiancée
summary: Roosevelt spends the whole day at Chestnut Hill with Alice.

headline: Living in a dream
summary: Roosevelt says his days with Alice feel like a dream of happiness.

headline: Last parting before the wedding
summary: Roosevelt reluctantly returns to New York in the evening, comforted that this is the final separation: the wedding is just over three weeks away.

headline: Wedding errands and law school
summary: Staying with Aunt Annie and Uncle Jimmie Gracie in their snug New York house, Roosevelt busies himself with wedding gifts and preparations. He also enrolls at Columbia Law School.

headline: In New York
summary: Roosevelt is in New York City; nothing more is recorded.

headline: First day at Columbia Law
summary: Roosevelt begins classes at Columbia Law School, where he will spend about six hours a day. He plans Alice's gifts, a diamond crescent, ruby bracelet and sapphire ring worth about $2,500, and vows to be thriftier once married. His wedding gifts alone ultimately cost $3,889.

headline: In New York
summary: Roosevelt is in New York City; the record notes nothing further.

headline: Wedding talk at Oyster Bay
summary: Roosevelt goes out to Oyster Bay and is glad to find Elliott, Corinne, Bamie and his mother at home. There is much to discuss about the wedding.

headline: Beating Elliott and Fred Weeks at tennis
summary: Roosevelt spends the day outdoors, defeating both Elliott and Fred Weeks at tennis. Cousins Emlen and Alfred, with Griswold, arrive to spend Sunday.

headline: Sunday at Oyster Bay
summary: Roosevelt is at Oyster Bay; nothing else is recorded.

headline: Cousins shower Alice with gifts
summary: Back in New York, Roosevelt says he enjoys law school so far. His cousins have been generous with wedding presents for Alice, including a pearl ring from Emlen and a bracelet from West.

headline: Between New York and Boston
summary: The record places Roosevelt in New York City and Boston but gives no details.

headline: Dinner at Edith Carow's
summary: Two weeks before the wedding, Roosevelt dines at the home of his childhood friend Edith Carow, joined by Fanny Smith and Grace Potter, all of whom will attend. Fanny finds him wild with excitement.

headline: In New York
summary: Roosevelt is in New York City; no events are recorded.

headline: Out to Oyster Bay
summary: Roosevelt travels from New York out to Oyster Bay.

headline: Woods and tennis with the Weeks boys
summary: Roosevelt walks in the woods and plays tennis with Johnny and Freddy Weeks.

headline: Last bachelor Sunday at Oyster Bay
summary: Knowing his next visit to Oyster Bay will be with his bride, Roosevelt prays he can make Alice happy and resolves to be as unselfish and cheerful as she is.

headline: Naming the wedding party
summary: Roosevelt heads into New York to wrap up business before leaving for Boston on Friday. He records the wedding party: Corinne, Rosy Lee, Rose Saltonstall and Fanny Peabody as bridesmaids, and ten ushers including cousins Emlen and West Roosevelt.

headline: In New York
summary: Roosevelt is in New York City; nothing more is recorded.

headline: In New York
summary: Roosevelt is in New York City; the record is otherwise silent.

headline: In New York
summary: Roosevelt is in New York City; no events are noted.

headline: Overnight train to Boston
summary: Roosevelt takes the night train to Boston for his wedding.

headline: To Chestnut Hill, then Kernwood
summary: Roosevelt hurries out to Chestnut Hill in the morning to embrace Alice, who has received some 250 wedding presents. In the afternoon he goes with his friend Cottie Peabody to the Peabody estate, Kernwood, in Salem, and admires both the place and the bright, well-read family.

headline: Church in Salem and tea with Fanny Peabody
summary: Roosevelt and Cottie walk into Salem for church, then he calls on old 'Grandma Lee.' They take tea at Fanny Peabody's, and he meets Frank Peabody's fiancée, Rosamund Laurence, whom he finds handsome and cultivated.

headline: Final arrangements, and some tree-felling
summary: Roosevelt settles the last wedding details and in the evening cuts down trees and fools around with Cottie Peabody. Elliott checks in at Boston's Brunswick Hotel, bringing Fanny Smith, Grace Potter and Edith Carow.

headline: Eve of the wedding
summary: Roosevelt comes into Boston, lunches with both families at the Lees', and dines and sleeps at the Brunswick. Elliott will be his best man. At dinner he tips Fanny Smith's chair so far back she fears a backward somersault.

headline: Roosevelt marries Alice Lee
summary: On his 22nd birthday, Roosevelt marries Alice Hathaway Lee at noon in Brookline's Unitarian church, with Elliott as best man. After a reception at the Lee home, where Edith Carow dances the evening away, the couple leave around 4 p.m. for a suite in Springfield.

headline: Honeymoon begins at Oyster Bay
summary: The newlyweds travel from Springfield through New York to Oyster Bay for a two-week stay, with the house to themselves apart from two servants and a groom.

headline: Alice rests
summary: Alice spends the day recovering from the trip.

headline: Honeymoon routine
summary: Roosevelt's horse is in fine shape for lovely drives, the tennis court is marked out and his rowboat is afloat. The couple breakfast at ten, dine at two and take tea at seven.

headline: Bible, autumn walks and Dickens
summary: Instead of church, Roosevelt reads the Bible aloud, and the couple walk among hills turned red and gold. While Alice sews he reads to her from Quentin Durward, The Pickwick Papers and The Newcomes. He writes his mother that the honeymoon at Tranquility is a joy.

headline: Portrait of a honeymoon
summary: Roosevelt sketches honeymoon life at Oyster Bay: wood fires, the servants Mary Ann and Kate, the coachman Davis, a collie named Dare, a calf and a gloomy cat. He adores Alice at the tea table in her pink and gray dress, and their days run to drives, walks, tennis, reading aloud and cards.

headline: First presidential vote: Garfield
summary: Roosevelt drives to Norwich to cast his first-ever vote for president, choosing Republican James A. Garfield. Garfield wins the White House over Winfield Scott Hancock, with Chester A. Arthur as vice president.

headline: At Oyster Bay
summary: Roosevelt and Alice are at Oyster Bay; nothing else is recorded.

headline: Living in dreamland
summary: Roosevelt writes that he and Alice are almost never apart and he wishes the honeymoon could go on forever.

headline: A healthy, happy day
summary: Roosevelt notes another wholesome, contented day at Oyster Bay.

headline: Politics and poetry indoors
summary: Rain keeps the couple inside. Roosevelt loves talking with Alice about everything from politics to poetry and reading to her from history, novels or the daily paper, their only link to the wider world.

headline: A walker who climbs fences
summary: Roosevelt reads the Bible aloud, then takes a long autumn walk with Alice, who strides well and climbs fences nearly as easily as he does. His hunter keeps them in woodcock and partridge. Elsewhere, James Roosevelt and Sara Delano marry and sail for Europe on the Germanic, the ship carrying Elliott toward India.

headline: Drive to the brush plains past Syosset
summary: The couple take a long carriage ride out past Syosset onto the brush plains, returning through the Cold Spring valley, Laurel Hollow and Oak Openings, then play lawn tennis.

headline: Rowing Alice around Centre Island
summary: On a fine Indian summer day Roosevelt plays tennis and reads Manzoni's The Betrothed aloud on the piazza, then rows Alice around Centre Island and watches the sun set over the water.

headline: Happiest honeymoon ever
summary: The couple drive toward Locust Valley and Glen Cove. Roosevelt doubts any honeymoon has been happier.

headline: Rain, then a drive
summary: Rain keeps them in all morning, but they go driving after lunch.

headline: Last day of the honeymoon
summary: On a cross-country walk toward Syosset, Alice stops to pet every animal but flees bulls and turkey cocks, while the collie trots along. Roosevelt is sorry to see the honeymoon end but eager for the life ahead.

headline: Home to West 57th Street
summary: The couple leave Oyster Bay and drive into New York to an enthusiastic welcome, settling at the family home at 6 West 57th Street with his mother, Bamie and Corinne. Elliott is away in the East.

headline: Sunday lunch and the Newsboys' Home
summary: Roosevelt notes that Alice plans to join the Presbyterian church. After services he hosts the family's customary Sunday lunch, and in the evening he goes to the Newsboys' Home. He and Alice will spend the winter living with his mother.

headline: The park and the opera
summary: Roosevelt shows off his smart cart on an afternoon drive with Alice through the park. That night they go to the opera in Hilborne Roosevelt's box.

headline: Alice receives callers
summary: Alice holds her afternoon at-home for visitors.

headline: A law student's daily round
summary: Roosevelt describes his routine: walk downtown to Columbia Law School on Great Jones Street at 8:30 to study under Professor Theodore Dwight, read Blackstone, research his naval history of the War of 1812 at the Astor Library, then hurry uptown so he and Alice can go driving.

headline: St. Andrew's Society and Whitelaw Reid
summary: Roosevelt attends a lively gathering of the St. Andrew's Society and has a long conversation with newspaper editor Whitelaw Reid.

headline: Riverside drive and the opera
summary: Roosevelt drives Alice up through Riverside Park and takes her to the opera that night.

headline: In New York
summary: Roosevelt is in New York City; no entry survives for the day.

headline: In New York
summary: Roosevelt is in New York City; the record notes nothing more.

headline: In New York
summary: Roosevelt is in New York City; no events are recorded.

headline: Evenings full of visitors
summary: Roosevelt notes that even on nights at home, callers pour in, though he and Alice still find quiet time together. He drives her out every afternoon he can, or his mother or a sister when Alice cannot go.

headline: Sleigh ride in the snow
summary: After a heavy snowfall Roosevelt takes Alice on a sleigh ride. He finds his law studies absorbing.

headline: Thanksgiving dinner for 100 newsboys
summary: Roosevelt and his cousin Emlen host a big Thanksgiving dinner for about a hundred newsboys. That evening the family gathers for its own feast.

headline: Dinner at Aunt Annie's
summary: Aunt Annie Gracie gives a dinner for the newlyweds. Roosevelt is seated next to Annie Murray and meets a bright young man named Archie Alexander.

headline: The Lees come to New York
summary: Alice's parents and her sister Kitty arrive in New York, to Roosevelt's delight, and dine with the family.

headline: Alice decides to join the church
summary: The Lees and others come for tea. Roosevelt records that Alice has made up her mind to join the church, and he speaks to the newsboys as he does every Sunday.

headline: A Russian diplomat to dinner
summary: Villamof, a member of the Russian legation whom Roosevelt finds very clever, dines with the family. Roosevelt also takes Kitty Lee for a drive.

headline: Buying land at Cove Neck
summary: Roosevelt buys the first of three Cove Neck parcels near Oyster Bay from Thomas Youngs; together they total 155 acres. When his mother reads Elliott's letters from India aloud, he paces restlessly, longing for the wilds and a rifle.

headline: A drive and the theater with the Lees
summary: Roosevelt takes Alice on a long drive and goes to the theater with the Lees that evening.

headline: In New York
summary: Roosevelt is in New York City; nothing is recorded for the day.

headline: Seated beside Mrs. Astor
summary: While Corinne, Alice and Edith Carow make a trip to Morristown, New Jersey, Roosevelt goes to a large dinner party, sitting between Mrs. Newbold and Mrs. Astor and chatting with Mrs. Cutting and Mrs. Potter. He takes a liking to Astor and Cutting.

headline: Driving Mother; enjoying law
summary: Roosevelt drives his mother through Riverside Park and notes how much he likes his law studies.

headline: A Sunday in New York
summary: Roosevelt is in New York City; no entry survives.

headline: Alice and the city's rush
summary: Alice grumbles that New York keeps her forever hurrying and running after things, such as the horsecars.

headline: A dull dinner at the Millers
summary: Roosevelt attends what he considers a rather boring dinner at the Millers', seated by a Miss Duncan.

headline: Grand ball for Alice and Corinne
summary: The Roosevelts throw a great ball at home for Alice and for Corinne's debut, drawing some 500 guests including Mrs. William Astor and the Vanderbilts, Dodges, Harrimans and Iselins.

headline: In New York
summary: Roosevelt is in New York City; the record is silent.

headline: Preparing for Alice's church membership
summary: Roosevelt attends the preparatory service held before Alice joins the church.

headline: A reception, and pride in Alice
summary: At a grand reception at home Roosevelt enjoys roaming and chatting freely. He confesses he is not much for society, though he likes some married women such as Mrs. Astor, Mrs. Cutting and Mrs. Newbold, and is proud that everyone admires Alice.

headline: Alice joins the church
summary: Roosevelt describes a perfect Sunday: late breakfast, church, dinner, an afternoon with Alice, tea with West, Hilborne, Uncle Jimmie and Aunt Annie, then the newsboys. Alice formally joins the church, and he feels they are now united in all things.

headline: Dinner at the Iselins
summary: Roosevelt goes to a cheerful small dinner at the Iselins'.

headline: Mendelssohn concert
summary: Roosevelt attends a Mendelssohn concert and thinks it excellent.

headline: Riverside drives along the Hudson
summary: With his horse in high spirits and lovely weather, Roosevelt relishes driving Alice up Riverside Park beside the Hudson, or his mother when Alice cannot come, and marvels at his luck in their home life.

headline: In New York
summary: Roosevelt is in New York City; nothing more is noted.

headline: Two afternoon teas
summary: Roosevelt makes the rounds of big afternoon receptions at the Iselins' and the Morans'. He likes these teas because he never lingers with any one girl long enough to run out of talk.

headline: Founding a whist club
summary: At Alice's suggestion Roosevelt hosts a whist club of young men including Douglas Robinson, Ike Iselin, Bob Sedgwick and his cousins West and Emlen. He likes them all, especially Doug, who may join the family.

headline: A Sunday in New York
summary: Roosevelt is in New York City; no entry is recorded.

headline: Waltzing at the Patriarchs' Ball
summary: At the Patriarchs' Ball, Corinne is a belle and Alice is much sought after. Roosevelt enjoys some splendid waltzes, partnering Lucy Tuckerman, Emily Post and Miss Livingston.

headline: In New York
summary: Roosevelt is in New York City; the record notes nothing further.

headline: Winter drives by the Palisades
summary: When the streets are icy Roosevelt swaps the cart for the buggy. He loves driving Alice up Riverside Park, with the snow-covered Palisades set against gray skies above the ice-choked Hudson.

headline: In New York
summary: Roosevelt is in New York City; no events are recorded.

headline: Christmas trip to Chestnut Hill
summary: Roosevelt and Alice travel to Chestnut Hill to spend Christmas with the Lees, happy to see everyone again.

headline: Christmas with the Lees
summary: Roosevelt watches the young Lees open their presents, goes sledding, and joins the whole Saltonstall family at Christmas dinner.

headline: Church and sledding
summary: Roosevelt attends the little Chestnut Hill church in the morning and goes coasting after lunch.

headline: Crashing a sled into a tree
summary: Roosevelt's sledding ends with a smash into a tree. In the afternoon he takes Rosy Lee for a long sleigh ride in excellent conditions.

headline: Measles drive them next door
summary: Returning from errands in Boston, Roosevelt and Alice learn that Rosy has the measles and move at once to the Saltonstalls, who welcome them warmly.

headline: Worried about the measles
summary: Roosevelt laments the measles outbreak, feels for Mrs. Lee, half fears going home, and praises the Saltonstalls' kindness.

headline: At Chestnut Hill
summary: Roosevelt is at Chestnut Hill; nothing else is recorded.

headline: Closing his happiest year
summary: Roosevelt and Alice decide to head home the next day. He calls 1880 by far his happiest year because he won Alice, and closes his diary with a month-by-month cash account and notes on his shooting tallies.

headline: Back to New York
summary: Roosevelt and Alice return to New York from Chestnut Hill.

headline: Sunday routine resumes
summary: Roosevelt goes to the Newsboys' Home in the evening as he does each Sunday, after his cousin West and others come to tea. He and Alice likely spend the day paying calls on their return.

headline: A thirty-mile sleigh ride
summary: On the holiday Roosevelt takes Alice on a 30-mile sleigh ride in splendid snow. They dine with Hill and Frank and go to the theater.

headline: Back to the law books
summary: Roosevelt resumes classes at law school, walking both ways as always. He takes his mother sleighing and plays whist at the Robinsons'.

headline: Mrs. King's ball at Delmonico's
summary: After a long sleigh ride with Alice, Roosevelt dines at James Roosevelt's and then attends Mrs. King's ball at Delmonico's.

headline: Starting a free trade club
summary: Roosevelt dines at the Astors' and works with college friends to organize a free trade club. Every minute of his time is spoken for.

headline: The Rathbone sisters arrive
summary: Two Rathbone sisters come to stay, and there is a pleasant small party at Aunt Annie Gracie's.

headline: Sleighing with Alice Rathbone
summary: Roosevelt takes Alice Rathbone out in the sleigh.

headline: A Sunday in New York
summary: Roosevelt is in New York City; no entry survives for the day.

headline: Sleigh ride and a dinner at home
summary: Roosevelt takes his mother sleighing. At a dinner at home he sits between Grace Rathbone and Lucy Tuckerman.

headline: Fanny Smith and dinner at the Delanos'
summary: Roosevelt takes his friend Fanny Smith sleighing, then dines at the Delanos', seated between Mrs. Astor and Mrs. Drayton.

headline: Sleighing past Harlem
summary: In superb sleighing weather Roosevelt drives Alice out beyond Harlem. The evening brings a lively theater party and supper at the Tuckermans'.

headline: Ball at the Astors'
summary: Roosevelt attends a grand ball given by the Astors.

headline: A private car to Niagara
summary: Roosevelt, Alice, Corinne and Bamie set out in a party of fifteen young people, riding a special railroad car bound for Niagara Falls, a jaunt he calls tremendous fun.

headline: A frolic at Niagara Falls
summary: The party views the falls, rapids and whirlpool, takes long sleigh rides, and finishes with a dance. Roosevelt says they took the hotel by storm.

headline: Under the falls, then home
summary: The group goes to church by sleigh and ventures beneath the falls, a grand sight. Riding the night train back to New York, they swap ghost stories and songs.

headline: Patriarchs' Ball
summary: Roosevelt attends the Patriarchs' Ball.

headline: Cousin John visits on Bamie's birthday
summary: Cousin John Elliott comes to stay, and Roosevelt takes Flora Grant out in the sleigh. It is Bamie's 26th birthday.

headline: Checking on the newsboys' night school
summary: Roosevelt takes his mother sleighing and goes downtown to look in on the newsboys' night school.

headline: Sleighing with Alice
summary: Roosevelt takes Alice out in the sleigh.

headline: A win in moot court
summary: Roosevelt argues a case in the law school's moot court and prevails.

headline: Sleighing with Harriet Lawrence
summary: Roosevelt takes Harriet Lawrence for a sleigh ride.

headline: A Sunday in New York
summary: Roosevelt is in New York City; nothing is recorded.

headline: Dinner for Lowell and friends
summary: The Roosevelts give a dinner at home for Lowell, a Miss G. and Miss Lawrence.

headline: Dinner at Rosy Roosevelt's
summary: Roosevelt enjoys a cheerful dinner at Rosy Roosevelt's.

headline: Daily sleigh rides with Alice
summary: Roosevelt says the sleighing is the best he has ever seen and he takes Alice out every day.

headline: A sleigh outing and a party at home
summary: Roosevelt takes a Miss Peabody out in his sleigh, and the family hosts a party that evening.

headline: Dinner at the Morans
summary: Roosevelt dines with the Moran family.

headline: Juggling at Hilborne's
summary: Roosevelt goes to an evening party at Hilborne Roosevelt's featuring a juggler.

headline: Sunday tea
summary: The family's Sunday tea draws its usual crowd of callers.

headline: Sleighing and an evening club
summary: Roosevelt takes Fanny Peabody sleighing and spends the evening with a group he calls the F.C.D.C. His days run to a three-mile walk to law school under Theodore Dwight, lectures and library study, the walk home, a sleigh ride and a social evening.

headline: Dinner at the Keans' and a coffeehouse
summary: Roosevelt dines at the Keans' and goes downtown with John Fernan to look over a coffeehouse.

headline: Rosy and Rose come to visit
summary: Alice's sister Rosy and Rose Saltonstall arrive to stay.

headline: Sleigh ride and a theater party
summary: Roosevelt takes Rosy sleighing and goes to a theater party in the evening.

headline: Sleighing with Rose Saltonstall
summary: Roosevelt takes Rose Saltonstall out in the sleigh and attends a dinner that night.

headline: Mother, then a small party
summary: Roosevelt takes his mother for a sleigh ride and goes to a small party in the evening.

headline: Corinne says yes to Douglas Robinson
summary: After much wavering and distress, Corinne agrees to marry Douglas Robinson, a wealthy young man whose family fortune is in real estate. Roosevelt is delighted and calls Douglas a splendid fellow.

headline: Aunt Annie's sleigh ride
summary: Roosevelt takes Aunt Annie Gracie sleighing and dines at the Leavitts'.

headline: Dinner at Aunt Laura's
summary: Roosevelt dines at Aunt Laura's.

headline: A spree at the Robinsons'
summary: Roosevelt takes Rosy sleighing and joins a rollicking party at the Robinsons'.

headline: Tea at Julian Weir's
summary: Roosevelt enjoys a tea at Julian Weir's and a dinner at the Griswolds', and finds both great fun.

headline: Communion lecture at Dr. Hall's
summary: Roosevelt attends a preparatory communion lecture given by Dr. Hall and goes sleighing with his mother.

headline: Dinner at the Weekes'
summary: Roosevelt dines with the Weekes family.

headline: An unreadable entry
summary: Roosevelt is in New York City; his diary entry for the day is a single unclear mark.

headline: First step into Republican politics
summary: After a drive with Rose Saltonstall, Roosevelt goes to a political meeting before the Patriarchs' Ball. It is the first mention of the 21st District Republican Association, run by boss Jake Hess from Morton Hall on 59th Street; Roosevelt probably joined the previous fall.

headline: A Mendelssohn concert; Edith's congratulations
summary: Roosevelt attends a Mendelssohn concert. Edith Carow writes Corinne to share her joy at the engagement and hopes to like Douglas Robinson.

headline: Tea and a party
summary: Roosevelt goes to a tea at Percy King's and a small party at Aunt Annie Gracie's.

headline: A Republican primary at Morton Hall
summary: Roosevelt attends a primary of the Republican Association at Morton Hall, drives Alice in the buggy now that the snow has melted, and sees Rosy and Rose off to Chestnut Hill.

headline: A musicale at the Betts'
summary: Roosevelt attends a musical evening at the Betts' home and takes Corinne for a drive.

headline: In New York
summary: Roosevelt is in New York City; no entry survives.

headline: A Sunday in New York
summary: Roosevelt is in New York City; nothing is recorded.

headline: A 'Niagara Party' reunion
summary: The Niagara travelers reunite for a party at the Betts', with tableaux, waxworks and lively dances from the Virginia reel to the Highland schottische. Alice's piano playing is loud enough that cousin Emlen's family hears it through the wall next door.

headline: Chaperoning an overnight party
summary: Alice, with Roosevelt in tow, chaperones a small group of young people on an overnight visit to the Keans' country place.

headline: Back in town
summary: Roosevelt returns to New York and takes Missy Robinson for a drive.

headline: Political club, then the Bachelors' Ball
summary: Roosevelt stops at the Primary Political Club at Morton Hall, then goes on to the very stylish Bachelors' Ball.

headline: A long drive and dinner guests
summary: Roosevelt takes Alice on a long drive; Mr. and Mrs. Meusing come to dinner.

headline: Dinner at the Stuyvesant Fishes'
summary: Roosevelt drives his mother and dines with the Stuyvesant Fish family.

headline: Sunday with the newsboys
summary: Roosevelt spends Sunday evening with the newsboys, as is his custom.

headline: Elliott turns 21 in India
summary: Roosevelt spends the evening with the F.C.D.C. Far away in India, Elliott turns 21. Around this time Roosevelt writes 'Sou' Sou' Southerly,' a story about how he and Elliott nearly drowned in a boat; it was never published.

headline: Law books by day, a party by night
summary: Roosevelt spends an evening at a party given by the Johnsons and notes in his diary that his legal studies have been demanding.

headline: A long carriage ride with Alice
summary: Roosevelt takes his wife Alice out for a lengthy drive around the city.

headline: Dinner guests, then a Republican primary
summary: The Thayer family dines with the Roosevelts, and afterward Roosevelt heads to Morton Hall for a Republican primary meeting.

headline: A night at the theater as Garfield takes office
summary: Roosevelt joins John and Nannie Roosevelt and Walter Suydam for an evening at the theater. In Washington, James A. Garfield becomes the twentieth President.

headline: A quiet Saturday in New York

summary: The Roosevelts visit Bray and Powerscourt and walk the wooded glen of the Dargle, enjoying a life of ease.

summary: Along with Shaw, Weld, Chapin, and the Lawrences, Roosevelt takes a coach out to Epsom for the races, and finishes the day at the theater.

headline: Robinson relatives and the British Museum
summary: Roosevelt lunches with relatives of Douglas Robinson, admires the sculptures at the British Museum, and dines with the Kingsfords.

headline: Rainy coach trip to Windsor
summary: Roosevelt rides out to Windsor Castle by coach despite the rain and dines with Chapin, Weld, and Shaw.

headline: Grosvenor Gallery and shopping
summary: Roosevelt visits the Grosvenor Gallery, goes shopping, and has Shaw and Chapin over for dinner.

headline: Doré's paintings and a fitting
summary: Roosevelt admires the Doré Gallery, buys gifts, and is fitted for new clothes.

summary: Roosevelt shops and returns to the British Museum.

summary: Roosevelt shops, tours the Bois de Boulogne, the Vendôme Column, and the Arc de Triomphe, and writes Corinne about London, its art, and the Channel crossing.

headline: A day at the Louvre
summary: Roosevelt tours the Louvre, admiring the Venus de Milo and works by Rubens and Murillo.

summary: Roosevelt and Alice are in Paris; nothing is recorded.

summary: From the Hotel Bellevue on the Avenue de l'Opéra, Roosevelt writes Corinne with his opinions of the art at the Louvre.

headline: Morning train toward Venice
summary: Roosevelt and Alice leave Paris by morning train, bound for Venice.

headline: Grimy and tired, but enchanted by Venice
summary: After a few mishaps on the way, the couple arrive in Venice dirty and weary. Roosevelt calls it the loveliest place of the trip so far.

summary: The Roosevelts take rooms in the old palace that is the Hotel Danieli, facing San Giorgio Maggiore and the Lido, and in the evening glide through the canals by gondola with Giuseppe Beppo at the oar.

summary: Roosevelt views a Titian masterpiece, tours the Doge's Palace, rides a gondola to the Lido, and ends the night listening to music in Piazza San Marco.

summary: Roosevelt visits San Marco and rows through Venice again after dark. He is able to read the Italian papers aloud to Alice.

headline: On to a sweltering Milan
summary: Roosevelt and Alice travel from Venice to Milan, which is very hot.

headline: Milan Cathedral, then Lake Como
summary: Roosevelt sees Milan's cathedral before moving on to Lake Como. He writes Bamie about Venice.

headline: Friday on Lake Como
summary: The Roosevelts are at Lake Como; no details are recorded.

headline: Como's cathedral and familiar faces
summary: Roosevelt finds Nicholas Fish and his wife at the lake, and drives with Alice to the town of Como to see its cathedral.

headline: Sunday at Lake Como
summary: The Roosevelts remain at Lake Como; nothing is recorded.

headline: Hiring Lombardino and a three-horse carriage

summary: Roosevelt and Alice cross the Splügen Pass, stopping for a poor lunch at Campodolcino, and spend the night at a decent inn in the village of Splügen. They walk the hills among Swiss cows and sheep.

summary: The couple drive through the dramatic Via Mala, lunch at Thusis, climb to a Rhaetian castle, and follow a gorge to Tiefencastel.

summary: Roosevelt and Alice leave the valley by the treeless Julier Pass, descending into the Upper Engadine and on to Samedan.

summary: At Samedan, Roosevelt takes his wife Alice out riding donkeys.

headline: A Sunday letter to Bamie
summary: From Samedan, Roosevelt writes to his sister Bamie.

headline: Snowbanks on the Bernina
summary: The couple cross the Bernina Pass by carriage, lunching at the hospice amid deep snowdrifts, and continue to Le Prese, where Roosevelt rows Alice on the Lago di Poschiavo after dinner.

summary: Roosevelt travels up the Valtellina to the Baths of Bormio, where he learns that Garfield has been shot and calls it a dreadful blow to the country.

summary: Fresh reports tell Roosevelt that Garfield has survived, and he writes that the crisis means work ahead for every man who wishes his country well.

headline: Turned back on the Stelvio
summary: Roosevelt and Alice cross the snowy Stelvio Pass, but heavy rain washes out the road beyond the summit and they retreat to spend the night at Trafoi.

summary: The couple descend into the Adige valley, lunch at the Haidersee with a curious German landlady, and stop at Hoch-Finstermünz above a deep gorge. Roosevelt interprets for their driver. It is his mother Mittie's 46th birthday.

headline: A Tyrolean inn at Imst
summary: Driving down the Inn valley through rain and sun, Roosevelt and Alice stop for the night at a traditional Tyrolean inn in Imst.

headline: On to Innsbruck
summary: The couple follow the Inn valley on to Innsbruck.

headline: Innsbruck sights, then Munich
summary: After sightseeing in Innsbruck, Roosevelt and Alice go on to Munich.

headline: Munich's picture gallery
summary: Roosevelt tours the picture gallery and other sights in Munich.

headline: Munich to Lucerne
summary: Roosevelt and Alice travel on to Lucerne.

headline: A bundle of letters from home
summary: In Lucerne, a refuge from the heat, the couple collect a stack of mail: two letters from Oyster Bay and nine from Chestnut Hill.

summary: Roosevelt and Alice hike up Mount Pilatus from Alpnach and down the other side to Hergiswil, outpacing their guide halfway up. Roosevelt chats with German students along the way.

headline: A dull sermon in Lucerne
summary: Roosevelt attends the English Church in Lucerne and finds the sermon weak.

headline: Sunset from the Rigi
summary: Roosevelt climbs the Rigi Kulm and watches a magnificent sunset.

headline: Up at three for the sunrise
summary: Roosevelt rises at 3 a.m. to see the sunrise from the Rigi, descends to Lucerne, and writes Bamie.

summary: The Roosevelts drive across the Brünig Pass to Interlaken.

summary: Roosevelt and Alice are at Interlaken; nothing is recorded.

summary: The couple drive through the rain to Grindelwald and lodge at the Schwarzer Adler.

headline: An outing above Grindelwald
summary: With Alice riding and Roosevelt walking, they make a round trip to a lookout near Grindelwald.

headline: Setting out for the Jungfrau
summary: Roosevelt leaves Grindelwald at 8:15 a.m. with guides Peter Egger and Hans Baumann, whom he rates highly, and reaches the Bergli hut at 4:45 p.m. to spend the night.

headline: Summit of the Jungfrau
summary: Starting at 3:15 a.m. into wind and cloud, Roosevelt crosses the Mönchjoch and the Jungfraufirn and stands on the Jungfrau's summit at 8:55. He enjoys the descent and is back in Grindelwald by 6 p.m.

headline: Resting in Grindelwald
summary: Roosevelt is at Grindelwald after the climb; no events are recorded.

headline: To the Upper Glacier

headline: Carriage to Kandersteg
summary: The Roosevelts hire a carriage and drive to Kandersteg.

headline: Gemmi Pass and a surprise reunion
summary: The couple cross the Gemmi Pass to Leuk and go on to Visp, where they are astonished to run into Charley Alexander.

headline: On to Zermatt
summary: Alice rides and Roosevelt walks from Visp to Zermatt in the company of Charley Alexander, whom he finds a fine companion.

headline: Glacier walk and dinner for friends
summary: After yet another weak sermon, Roosevelt walks to the glacier with Alexander and hosts a small dinner for friends he has met at Zermatt.

headline: Up the Gornergrat
summary: Roosevelt and Alice, still traveling with Alexander, climb to the Gornergrat and spend the night at the Riffel.

summary: Back in Zermatt, the Roosevelts reluctantly part with Alexander. The Gardiners, the Baylies, and the Kennedys are also in town.

summary: Roosevelt leaves the hut at 3:45 a.m., reaches the Matterhorn's summit at seven, and is back in Zermatt by 3:30 p.m., hard and risky going, but he is in top condition.

summary: Roosevelt and Alice leave Zermatt for Stalden, Alice and the bags on two mules. He writes Bamie and his Maine guide Bill Sewall about the Matterhorn ascent.

summary: Roosevelt finds the Chapmans staying at Chamonix and is unimpressed by the church service.

summary: The Roosevelts ride the stagecoach from Chamonix to Geneva.

summary: Roosevelt hires 25-year-old Joe Ferris to guide him. Buffalo have been hunted hard in the Dakotas lately. They overnight at the Maltese Cross Ranch, which Sylvane Ferris, 24, runs with Bill Merrifield, 28; all three men came from Canada. Roosevelt also writes his mother.

headline: A mare named Nell and the Lang cabin
summary: Roosevelt buys a mare called Nell from Ferris, then rides 45 miles south to the cabin of Scotsman Gregor Lang and his son Lincoln, 16. Lang, sent by an English firm to scout cattle country, talks with Roosevelt past midnight about the region and the cattle trade.

headline: A missed buck in the rain
summary: Up at six on a soaking day, Roosevelt hunts with Joe Ferris. Ferris drops a blacktail buck at long range after Roosevelt misses it, to his own annoyance. That night Roosevelt again talks cattle with Gregor Lang late, while Ferris sleeps.

headline: Mud and an empty game bag
summary: Roosevelt and Ferris hunt the whole day in the rain, bag nothing, and come back caked in mud. While Ferris sleeps, Roosevelt and Gregor Lang talk cattle, America and politics.

headline: More rain, more hunting
summary: Another wet day: Roosevelt hunts from morning to night and then talks late into the evening, just as before.

headline: Cree riders in the rain
summary: Rain again. Roosevelt's party spots a band of wandering Cree, but otherwise the day repeats the last two.

headline: A wounded buffalo and a bloody brow
summary: Roosevelt hits a buffalo too far back and it gets away. In the chase the animal charges, his pony knocks his rifle into his head, and he bleeds from the cut. That night the horses bolt. Ferris hears him exclaim he is having fun.

headline: Rain in his eyes
summary: In cold rain, Roosevelt gets a shot but misses with water streaming into his eyes, and spends another drenched night outdoors.

headline: Hard luck, and a choice to invest
summary: On a hot day Roosevelt tumbles down a cliff, is thrown from his horse, and nearly loses the horse to quicksand. After two days on biscuits and rainwater, he resolves to put money into the Badlands, and talks late with Gregor Lang again.

headline: A $14,000 stake in cattle
summary: With Sylvane Ferris and Bill Merrifield at the Lang cabin, Roosevelt hands them a $14,000 check to run his stock and purchase 450 cattle. The sum tops his entire income for the year, $13,920.

headline: Drawing up a ranch contract
summary: At the Lang cabin Roosevelt writes out a ranch contract. Ferris and Merrifield head to Minnesota to be released by their employers, Wadsworth and Halley, so they can partner with him.

summary: Riding into Montana with Joe Ferris, Roosevelt finally brings down a bison bull. He celebrates with a whooping dance and hands Ferris $100 then and there.
