summary: Cortelyou and Loomis call, and Roosevelt writes Albert Shaw about sending warships toward Beirut and the dispute with Turkey.

headline: Six steps on labor and capital
summary: Roosevelt writes Payne about a Delaware postmistress pushed out by the Addicks machine, congratulates John Finley on the NYU presidency, and sends Lyman Abbott a long letter on trusts, Indian agencies and the coal strike, listing six things he has done on labor and capital.

headline: Night train to Syracuse
summary: After lunch with James R. Garfield, Roosevelt leaves in the evening for Syracuse with Jacob Riis and William Loeb. He tells Florence LaFarge he read Aristophanes and Euripides side by side.

headline: Labor Day at the State Fair
summary: At the state fair in Syracuse, Roosevelt reviews the Labor Day parade at 10:30, gives his Labor Day address, reviews the letter carriers at five, and dines as the guest of F. H. Hiscock.

headline: Back to Oyster Bay; senators bristle
summary: Roosevelt returns to Oyster Bay, speaking at Richmond Hill on the way, and sees Cooley and a Sound Money League group. He writes Harvey Scott about senators angry that he has meddled in appointments they treated as their own.

headline: Archbishop of Manila and two writers
summary: Paul Morton and Francis Leupp call; Gordon Johnston and Will Cowles come to lunch. At three Archbishop Harty of Manila and H. M. Hoyt arrive, and in the evening Grant LaFarge and Owen Wister.

headline: Wary of stirring revolt in Panama
summary: LaFarge, Wister and Hamlin Garland are houseguests. Roosevelt again writes Payne about Miss Todd's removal and tells Jacob Schurman why he cannot say what he thinks about Panama.

headline: Keeping the squadron at Beirut
summary: Roosevelt writes Alford Cooley about how the merit rules apply to fourth-class postmasters and explains to Hay why the Beirut squadron had to go and must stay.

headline: Miss Todd's case may be lost
summary: Roosevelt tells Payne the Delaware postmistress's removal may now be impossible to reverse, and writes Wood about charges meant to sink his promotion.

headline: Ted turns sixteen
summary: Ted's sixteenth birthday at Sagamore Hill.

headline: Nothing on the record
summary: Roosevelt is at Sagamore Hill; no activity is noted.

headline: Wait on Colombia, think Nicaragua
summary: The Storers and Willis Ogden call, and Roosevelt dines with John Bassett Moore, LaFarge, Wister and Albert Bushnell Hart. He tells Hay to do nothing about Colombia for now and writes Taft that the coming winter may bring a start on Nicaragua or a move at Panama.

headline: Inspecting Ellis Island aboard the Sylph
summary: Roosevelt takes the Sylph out to the immigration station, touring it with Commissioner William Williams, to look over the station, meets Senator Platt, and leaves that evening for Antietam.

headline: Honoring New Jersey's dead at Antietam
summary: At Antietam, Roosevelt speaks at the dedication of New Jersey's monument to its soldiers, dines with Governor Franklin Murphy, and heads back to Oyster Bay.

headline: Seawanhaka dinner; at wits' end over the city race
summary: Roosevelt dines at the Seawanhaka Yacht Club at eight. He tells Alford Cooley that fourth-class postmasters fall under the new civil service rules and confides to Seth Low his puzzlement over the New York City election.

headline: Literary lunch with Matthews and White
summary: Roosevelt lunches with Brander Matthews, Stewart Edward White, Captain W. C. Brown and Nicholas Murray Butler, who stays over. He writes LeGrand Cannon about the tariff league's campaign against the Cuba treaty.

headline: Butler stays for Sunday
summary: Nicholas Murray Butler remains a guest at Sagamore Hill.

headline: Pressure on the Alaska tribunal
summary: Roosevelt talks over the special session with Harvey Scott and Senator Redfield Proctor and federal patronage with Representative Curtis. He warns Hay that the Alaska tribunal is under pressure against the United States and writes Clarke Davis about Miller and labor unions.

headline: Philippine commission letter to Taft
summary: Roosevelt writes Governor Taft about filling a seat on the Philippine Commission.

headline: An emptier house, and Archie's overalls
summary: With Ted and Kermit back at Groton, Roosevelt writes Kermit that home feels empty though hardly quiet, thanks to Archie in his faded blue overalls and Quentin. Edith is shutting the house for winter. He also writes Bill Sewall about the burdens of the presidency, and LaFarge and Wister arrive for the night.

headline: Three-hour ride; a Panama plot at the Waldorf
summary: Roosevelt rides three hours with LaFarge and Wister, lunches with Lyman Abbott, chops wood in the afternoon, and hosts Parsons overnight. In New York, Philippe Bunau-Varilla and Dr. Manuel Amador meet at the Waldorf-Astoria hotel and lay plans for a Panamanian revolution.

headline: Riding with Edith, talking game with Grinnell
summary: Roosevelt and Edith ride for four hours. At lunch George Bird Grinnell and Sears discuss Indian reservations and the zoology of big game, and Roosevelt plays tennis in the afternoon.

headline: All day on the water with Edith
summary: Roosevelt and Edith spend the day in a rowboat, picnicking at the big marsh off Lloyd's Neck before a hard pull home into wind and tide. He also writes Henry White about the Alaska boundary.

headline: Corinne's birthday
summary: Roosevelt's sister Corinne turns 42.

headline: Summer ends; back to Washington
summary: Roosevelt leaves for Washington. Writing Corinne, he looks back on a lovely summer, praises her son Stewart, and wryly notes that Alice spent it mostly at Newport among the Four Hundred.

headline: Labor leaders at the White House
summary: Back at work, Roosevelt meets the Cabinet, receives the American Federation of Labor's executive council, and lunches with mine leader John Mitchell. He also takes up the postal inquiry with Payne and the Printing Office probe with Sargent and Garfield.

headline: Reading Lincoln and Plutarch
summary: Roosevelt visits Dr. Harban at eleven and lunches with Bonaparte and Conrad. To Lodge he reports he is reading Lincoln and Plutarch and covers the Printing Office, postal scandals and the Platt-Odell feud. British Ambassador Sir Michael Herbert has died in Switzerland, and London picks Sir Mortimer Durand as his successor.

headline: Delaware attorney talks; first World Series opens
summary: Roosevelt and Delaware's two senators, Allee and Ball, discuss a new district attorney for that state; sees R. P. Skinner and Senator Stewart, lunches with Secretary Wilson, and at three receives Ambassador and Mrs. Charlemagne Tower. In Boston the first World Series begins at the Huntington Avenue Grounds.

headline: "My hand on the lever"
summary: After a Cabinet meeting and talks on Alaska and postal indictments, Roosevelt writes his family: Quentin has started at the Force School, and Kermit should study more and play less. He adds that he enjoys the presidency and is reading about Lincoln.

headline: Drafting the annual message; jumping Bleistein
summary: Roosevelt works on his annual message, lunches with Moody, Shaw and Cortelyou, and receives Justices McKenna and Harlan and a string of officials. Then he rides out to Chevy Chase to jump Bleistein.

headline: Letting Ted play football
summary: Roosevelt writes Ted, now on Groton's second football squad, with some misgivings, and tells headmaster Endicott Peabody he will let the boy play even at some risk of injury.

headline: "Cat-rabbits" warning to Colombia
summary: Roosevelt names J. P. Nields Delaware's U.S. attorney as a grand jury charges Tyner and Barrett over postal fraud. He sits for three photographers, receives Venezuela's minister, and tells Hanna that Colombia must be warned his patience has limits; to Lodge he says Britain has no case on Alaska.

headline: Memorial for Sir Michael Herbert
summary: After the Cabinet meets, Roosevelt attends a noon memorial for the late Sir Michael Herbert at St. John's Episcopal Church, then sees a druggists' committee and lunches with George Becker.

headline: Langley's aircraft falls into the Potomac
summary: Roosevelt confers with Cromwell on the canal, Knox on judgeships and Payne at the Post Office, and goes to St. Thomas Church for the marriage of General Young's daughter. On the Potomac, Charles Manly tries to fly Samuel Langley's Smithsonian aircraft and fails.

headline: Postal probe, rivers and extradition
summary: Roosevelt meets Payne, Moody and C. E. Smith on the postal investigations, Representative Theodore Burton on rivers and harbors, and Joseph Folk on extradition with Canada and Mexico. He asks J. P. Morgan to talk finance.

headline: Cabinet day and lunch with McClure
summary: Roosevelt meets his Cabinet and lunches with magazine publisher S. S. McClure.

headline: Bunau-Varilla at the White House
summary: At 11:30 Roosevelt and Assistant Secretary Loomis meet Philippe Bunau-Varilla of Paris. He talks Ohio with Senator Foraker, lunches with Will Cowles and visiting English traffic commissioners, and sees Lincoln Steffens. To Albert Shaw he writes that an independent Panama would delight him. It is Kermit's fourteenth birthday.

headline: Evening tea with Hay and reformers
summary: At 7:30 Roosevelt takes tea with Arthur von Briesen, John Hay and William Dudley Foulke. He writes Ted that he belongs on Groton's third football team, not the second. His niece Eleanor turns 19.

headline: Praise for Uncle Remus, a quarrel with Long
summary: Atha Cunningham photographs Roosevelt at nine. He meets Moody and Congressmen Grosvenor, Dalzell and Olmsted, receives the Supreme Court, and lunches with Lloyd Lowndes. He praises Joel Chandler Harris and protests John D. Long's Outlook article suggesting he wanted Spanish ships sunk before war began in 1898.

headline: Game wardens for Yosemite
summary: After the Cabinet meets, Roosevelt shares lunch with the Corbins, Clarke Davis and a visiting English lord and lady. He tells Taft he needs him home by late January for help on labor and trusts, and suggests to Roger Baldwin that Yosemite's forest rangers double as game wardens.

headline: Boston wins the first World Series
summary: Roosevelt confers with Knox and receives Henry Clay Frick, Regis Post, Simon Wolf and Senator McComas, then has Generals Bell and Crozier to dinner. Boston beats Pittsburgh in game eight to take the first World Series, and Amador and Bunau-Varilla meet again at the Waldorf.

headline: Sherman statue speech; word of a Panama revolt
summary: Roosevelt speaks at 2:30 at the unveiling of General Sherman's statue in Washington. Navy Commander John Hubbard tells him a rising in Panama is coming. Postal investigators confer with him, General Dodge and the Thorndikes stay overnight, and he orders Payne to look into Perry Heath.

headline: Army officers predict a Panama uprising
summary: After the Cabinet meets and he talks with Representatives Payne and Dalzell about a special session, two Army officers tell Roosevelt that Panama is close to rising against Colombia. Arthur Sage and Albert Shaw stay the night.

headline: Alaska tribunal sides with America
summary: The Alaska boundary tribunal decides in favor of the United States. Roosevelt sees Hay and Senators Scott and Hansbrough, lunches with Generals Oliver and Brooke, John Logan and John C. Black, meets A. Maurice Low, and has Joe Bishop to dinner and overnight.

headline: Pillow ambush and Uncle Remus
summary: Roosevelt meets Hay and, at 2:30, Ambassador von Sternberg, and enjoys Washington's autumn color. Once he is home, the two youngest boys, Archie and Quentin, ambush him with pillows, and once they are bathed he reads aloud from Uncle Remus. Nephew Sheffield Cowles turns five.

headline: Warships ordered toward the isthmus
summary: Roosevelt sends the Boston to Nicaragua and the Atlanta to Guantanamo. He discusses land laws with Senator Hansbrough, has Paul Morton and General Black to lunch, and tells Kermit that a car spooked Renown on a family ride.

headline: "I rose like a rocket"
summary: Roosevelt summons Congress to meet November 9 on the Cuban treaty. The Alaska tribunal's ruling, with Lord Alverstone siding with the Americans, gives Canada nothing; the two Canadians refuse to sign. He writes Ted about his own fast rise, and writes Holmes on the boundary.

headline: Claiming credit for the Alaska win
summary: Roosevelt meets a group of senators including Quay, Clark, Mitchell and Fulton, lunches with Wayne MacVeagh and Bishop William Lawrence, and hosts Henry Lee Higginson overnight. He tells Ted his warnings over Alaska were decisive and praises Ray Stannard Baker's article on union bosses.

headline: Public Lands Commission created
summary: Roosevelt sets up the Public Lands Commission to study how the nation's land laws work. He reviews the postal prosecutions with Bonaparte, Conrad and Knox, lunches with James R. Garfield, and writes Shaw about a Boston business meeting.

headline: Laid low by Cuban fever
summary: After the Cabinet and callers including Senator Cullom and Charles Walcott of the Geological Survey, Roosevelt comes down with Cuban fever. He spends the afternoon still on the sofa while Edith knits beside him in a rocker.

headline: Stiff joints and good grades
summary: Several hundred Universalist convention delegates call. Roosevelt cheers Ted's grades but confesses he is slipping physically, stiff with what may be rheumatism or gout. He tells Kermit that Quentin fell off the pony unhurt and the family has gone to Dr. Rixey's farm, while he works on his annual message.

headline: Bishops and a talk at Mount St. Alban
summary: Roosevelt receives a delegation of American bishops and speaks at Mount St. Alban on Christian virtues.

headline: Inquiry into the New York Post Office
summary: A probe of the post office in New York City gets under way. Roosevelt sees Senator Scott, meets Secretary Moody and the West Indies archbishop, and entertains the Satterlees, the Rixeys and Chief Justice Fuller.

headline: Forty-five, with greetings from Hungarian Republicans
summary: Roosevelt turns 45. A Hungarian-American Republican club from New York stops by that morning with good wishes; he also meets the Cabinet, talks the glove contract case with Littauer, and sees Baldwin and Burgess.

headline: Glove case talks and a crowded lunch table
summary: Roosevelt meets Littauer and John G. Milburn, sees Senators Cullom and Cockrell and Representative Dixon, and lunches with Silas McBee, General Joseph Wheeler, Bishop Talbot, the Dudleys and others.

headline: Admiring Joseph Conrad
summary: Roosevelt confers with Interior Secretary Hitchcock on public lands and lunches with Dean Worcester and Alexander Agassiz. He tells Lincoln Steffens he likes Joseph Conrad's work and writes Lyman Abbott about the Caribbean islands and about his policies toward Black Americans.

headline: Nashville ordered to Colon
summary: The Cabinet works over the annual message, and Roosevelt confers with Long and Darling. The gunboat Nashville is sent to Colon on the isthmus.

headline: Carter named governor of Hawaii
summary: Roosevelt appoints George R. Carter territorial governor of Hawaii, receives the Portuguese minister, sees Mr. Emerson of the New York Herald, and writes Hanna about Ohio patronage.

headline: A quiet Sunday in Washington
summary: Roosevelt is in Washington; nothing else is recorded.

headline: Waiting on the Nashville
summary: Roosevelt talks with Representatives Cannon and Mondell, greets the sailors of the Sylph and Mayflower, lunches with John W. Foster, and leaves that night for Oyster Bay. The Panama rising planned for this day is held back until U.S. warships take station; the Nashville reaches Colon by 5:30.

headline: Panama declares independence
summary: Roosevelt votes at Oyster Bay on Election Day, sees Jacob Riis, and heads back to Washington that evening. In Panama City, Colombian troops are bought off with $50 apiece in gold, railroad workers and firemen seize the city, U.S. ships keep Colombian forces from landing, and Panama proclaims independence with Dr. Amador as president.

headline: Marines ashore at Colon
summary: American Marines come ashore at Colon. Roosevelt writes Nicholas Murray Butler about the elections, including a lengthy rundown of his reading since 1900, and writes Hanna on the canal and Gilder on the coal strike.

headline: War council on the Panama rising
summary: Roosevelt meets Hay, Moody, Loomis and Admirals Taylor and Walker on events in Panama, sees the immigration commissioners, and has Senator and Mrs. George Turner overnight. He writes General Francis Greene on the elections and Lyman Abbott about Hanna's place in the presidential picture.

headline: America recognizes the Republic of Panama
summary: The United States recognizes Panama, and the Cabinet agrees to open canal treaty talks with the new republic at once. Roosevelt sees Congressmen Grosvenor and Hepburn, dines with Governor Franklin Murphy, and insists to Albert Shaw there was no conspiracy with the rebels.

headline: Senate leaders and the Cuba treaty
summary: On a crowded day Roosevelt meets Senators Spooner, Aldrich, Cullom, Allison, Hale and Orville Platt about changes to the Cuban treaty, lunches with John Sleicher, and dines with General Francis Greene. He writes Hay on Congress's role in foreign affairs.

headline: Late-night talks with Root and Aldrich
summary: Roosevelt meets Elihu Root at nine about Panama and Senator Aldrich at ten about finance.

headline: Congress meets in special session
summary: Congress gathers in extra session to act on Cuban reciprocity. Roosevelt discusses the Republican National Committee chairmanship with Hanna, dines with Lodge, and spends the evening with a roomful of party leaders over his Cuba message. He presses for Spring-Rice's posting to Washington.

headline: Cuba message goes to Congress; Booker T. Washington calls
summary: Roosevelt sends Congress his special message on Cuban reciprocity after a Cabinet session on Panama. He meets a joint committee including Hanna, Lodge and Cannon at 10:30, lunches with Baroness von Sternberg, sees Booker T. Washington at 2:30, and dines with House leaders.

headline: Dinner with Root
summary: Roosevelt dines with Secretary Root.

headline: "We did not know"
summary: Roosevelt breakfasts with Senator Beveridge and holds an evening dinner conference on Panama with Hay, Wilson and a group of senators. He assures Jacob Schurman and Lawrence Abbott that he and Hay had no advance knowledge of the Panama revolution.

headline: Receiving Panama's minister
summary: At 9:30 Roosevelt receives Philippe Bunau-Varilla as Panama's minister. After Cabinet and talks with Senators Fairbanks, Hoar, Allison and McComas, he lunches with Knox and dines with Lodge and Hay. To James Wilson he recalls urging McKinley in 1898 to treat Spanish torpedo boats' sailing as an act of war.

headline: A scramble up Rock Creek
summary: After meeting Hanna and Puerto Rican delegates, Roosevelt leads Ethel, Archie, Quentin and three Garfield boys on a scramble through Rock Creek Park. That evening he dines with members of the Ellis Island investigating commission.

headline: Acting as "vice-mother"
summary: Roosevelt has dinner with Lodge and his sister Bamie and her husband. With Edith away nine days, he tells Kermit he spends 45 minutes every evening reading aloud to the two little boys, from Algonquin legends and Scott to Macaulay, Jim Bludso and the Bible. Ted has broken his nose at football.

headline: Speech on Lincoln at New York Avenue church
summary: At Congressman Hitt's request, the House receives the Panama documents. Roosevelt sees Beveridge, Fairbanks, Moody, Cortelyou, Cannon and Governor Durbin, lunches with Hughitt, Hendricks and Low, and at 7:45 gives an address on Lincoln at New York Avenue Presbyterian Church. He sends Harvard's football team a rousing letter.

headline: Senators to dinner as the treaty takes shape
summary: After the Cabinet meets, Roosevelt lunches with Governor Durbin, Justice Harlan and others while Bunau-Varilla and Hay draft a canal treaty. He dines with Lodge, Root, Knox and a table of senators, and writes on labor unions and the canal.

headline: Hay-Bunau-Varilla Treaty signed
summary: At 6:40 in the evening John Hay and Philippe Bunau-Varilla sign the canal treaty between the United States and Panama, on the same $10 million terms Colombia had refused. Earlier Roosevelt sees Simon Wolf and lunches with Moody, Ream and Wayne MacVeagh.

headline: Quentin's birthday cake in the nursery
summary: Quentin turns six, nursing a cold; his birthday cake is brought up to the nursery, where Edith, Aunt Emily, Ethel, Archie, his father, Mame and Georgette join him. The House passes the Cuban reciprocity bill, Roosevelt addresses Washington's German societies, and he wires Alice forbidding her to pour tea at a charity show.

headline: Alice pours tea anyway
summary: Roosevelt meets the Cabinet and at 2:30 the Panama commission with Bunau-Varilla. In New York, Alice ignores his wishes and serves tea at $5 a cup at the Charity Portrait Show with Ethel Barrymore and Maude Adams.

headline: Caruso's Met debut
summary: Roosevelt lunches with W. D. Murphy, goes over the Bristow report with Payne and Bristow, sees Tawney and, at 2:30, the Russian ambassador, and dines with Joe Bishop. In New York, Enrico Caruso makes his Metropolitan Opera debut in Rigoletto.

headline: Sunday with nothing recorded
summary: Roosevelt is in Washington; no activity is noted.

headline: Opening the German-American fair by button
summary: Roosevelt lunches with Senator Platt and G. W. Dunn, sees Foraker and Fairbanks, and at seven touches an electric button that starts the German-American fair at Convention Hall before meeting Hanna at 8:30. He writes Philip Stewart about Colorado politics and bear hunting.

headline: Peacemaking between Platt and Odell
summary: After the Cabinet takes up Panama, Roosevelt brings Governor Odell, Senator Platt and Dunn together to settle their New York feud. He lunches with Montana labor leaders, Cortelyou, MacVeagh and Carroll Wright, meets the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, and keeps Odell overnight.

headline: Bamie's anniversary, a full calendar
summary: Bamie marks eight years of marriage. On a packed day Roosevelt lunches with Slicer and Shaw and meets Austria's ambassador.

headline: Thanksgiving, then north for Uncle Jimmie
summary: On Thanksgiving evening Roosevelt leaves for New York after the death of his uncle James K. Gracie and stays at Corinne's, where Eleanor is also a guest; everyone but Eleanor goes out to play. He answers Packard's charge that he is anti-labor and tells G. H. Putnam of a Collier's deal for his collected works.

headline: Uncle Jimmie Gracie's funeral
summary: Roosevelt attends the funeral of his uncle James K. Gracie in New York and returns to Washington.

headline: A crank at the funeral
summary: Roosevelt sees S. Fred Nixon at ten, meets Ball, Quay and Fairbanks, and lunches with Eugene Philbin. He tells Kermit that 500 police ringed the church at Uncle Jimmie's funeral, yet a crank slipped in with a petition about curing the Kaiser's cancer. Ted has sprained an ankle and is urged to read Trevelyan's American Revolution.

headline: His Bristow report comments go public
summary: Roosevelt's comments on the Bristow report on postal frauds are published.

headline: Was Panama like the Confederacy?
summary: Roosevelt receives Cannon with an Illinois delegation and dines with Senators Spooner and Orville Platt. To Otto Gresham he explains why Panama's break from Colombia is no parallel to Southern secession: the Panamanians have right on their side.

headline: Lunch with Captain Pershing
summary: After the Cabinet meets, Roosevelt lunches with Captain John J. Pershing, Monsignor O'Connell and Major and Mrs. Howze, confers with Senator Penrose, and writes Joe Bishop about press guesswork over his talk with Platt and Odell.

headline: Panama ratifies the canal treaty
summary: As he and Edith mark 17 years of marriage, Panama's government ratifies the Hay-Bunau-Varilla treaty. Roosevelt talks Panama and Illinois with Cullom, lunches with John R. Proctor and Garfield, sees Foraker, Fairbanks and the British ambassador, and writes Arthur von Briesen on immigration tests.

headline: Alaska result "satisfactory in every way"
summary: Roosevelt confers with Root, Moody and Hay, lunches with Ray Stannard Baker, and sends Congress a message on the Alaska boundary award.

headline: Hanna at night on canal and Wood
summary: Roosevelt sees Hill of the Tribune at ten, meets the Cabinet, takes up New York appointments with Senator Platt and confers with Hay. At 9:15 p.m. he and Hanna go over canal legislation, the Wood case and the national committee chairmanship.

headline: Breakfast with Putnam
summary: Roosevelt breakfasts with Putnam and writes Hanna about rumors swirling around his meeting with Platt and Odell.

headline: Evening with Bristow and Leupp
summary: Roosevelt confers in the evening with Joseph Bristow and Francis Leupp.

headline: Annual message: building the canal is a duty
summary: Congress opens its regular session and hears Roosevelt's annual message, which calls building the Panama canal a national duty. He confers with Senator Warren on Alaska and lunches with Gordon and Peck. To Arthur Lee he praises the Alaska settlement and teases that Britain did well to face such reasonable jurors.

headline: Langley's machine fails again
summary: Charles Manly makes a second try at flying Professor Langley's aircraft off the Potomac, and fails again. Roosevelt meets the Cabinet, lunches with Andrew Carnegie, Henry Pritchett, Moody and others, and dines at Root's at eight.

headline: Panama tops his worries
summary: Roosevelt confers with Representative Foss on the Navy, visits Root in the evening and sees Senator Aldrich at 8:30. He tells Charles Osborn that Panama concerns him more than anything else right now.

headline: Commander Winslow joins as aide
summary: Roosevelt meets Republican National Committee members, takes Commander Winslow on as an aide, has Hugh Bond and Congressman Dayton to lunch, and sees H. H. Kohlsaat at 9:30.

headline: Sternberg calls; party committee meets
summary: After the Cabinet, Roosevelt lunches with Root, Mott, Stewart and Brooke, receives Ambassador von Sternberg at 2:30, and meets the Republican National Committee.

headline: Praising Trevelyan's Revolution
summary: Roosevelt names W. I. Buchanan U.S. minister to Panama, discusses Oklahoma statehood with Bird McGuire, and meets National Republican League leaders. He tells George Otto Trevelyan his book is the best history of the Revolution, defends Wood to Root, and answers Abbott on the postal frauds.

headline: Pinchot and Reynolds at nine
summary: Roosevelt sees Elihu Root in the afternoon and, at nine that night, Gifford Pinchot and James B. Reynolds.

headline: Riis at the White House
summary: Roosevelt talks statehood with Delegate Wilson, sees Root, Moody, Proctor, Cockrell and Foraker, and meets Shaw and von Sternberg about exports to Germany. Jacob Riis is his guest. He writes Austin Wadsworth about New York business jitters over his financial course.

headline: Funeral for a civil service commissioner
summary: At 10:30 Roosevelt attends the funeral of Civil Service Commissioner John R. Proctor, then lunches with Shaw and Speaker Cannon and discusses German export duties. Beveridge calls at nine and Riis stays over. He names John Black to Proctor's seat.

headline: Senate passes Cuban reciprocity
summary: The Senate passes the Cuban reciprocity bill. Roosevelt breakfasts with Albert Shaw, meets the Cabinet, reviews with Bonaparte and Conrad the report upholding Tulloch's postal fraud charges, and lunches with G. H. Putnam.

headline: Signs Cuban reciprocity as the Wrights fly
summary: Roosevelt signs the Cuban reciprocity bill, lunches with Root, Cortelyou, Lodge and Massachusetts Governor Crane, gives a Cabinet dinner at eight, and hosts Governor Odell overnight. At Kitty Hawk, Orville and Wilbur Wright make the first powered flights; the longest, Wilbur's fourth, lasts 59 seconds over 852 feet.

headline: Backing Peary's polar bid
summary: After a Cabinet session on Panama, Roosevelt discusses New York politics with Governor Odell and has Kennedy, Jones, Crane, Root, Cortelyou and Lodge to lunch. He writes Daniel Coit Gilman in support of Robert Peary's North Pole expedition.

headline: Western land frauds and a jab at Bryce
summary: Roosevelt calls in Knox, Lodge, Root, Moody, Hitchcock and Cortelyou to deal with land frauds in the West, lunches with Judge Grosscup, and dines with Joe Bishop, Professor Lounsbury and Nicholas Murray Butler, who stays over. He objects to James Bryce's portrait of Godkin and lays out his Panama policy for critic George Harvey.

headline: Mrs. Trescott's camera
summary: At 9:15 in the morning Mrs. Trescott arrives to photograph the President and Edith.

headline: "Dead sure that Columbia fires first"
summary: Roosevelt calls on John Hay and orders Navy Secretary Moody to keep forces in Panama from shooting unless fired on.

headline: Talks with Colombia's General Reyes
summary: After the Cabinet, Roosevelt lunches with Spring, Moore, Garrison and MacVeagh. He writes Hay about negotiations with Colombia's General Reyes and David Thompson about comparisons between Panama and the Civil War.

headline: Friars' lands and a question about Yaviza
summary: Roosevelt breakfasts with Paul Morton, takes up the Philippine friars' lands with Root and Shaw, lunches with Pennsylvania Governor Pennypacker, and sees H. G. Squiers. He telephones Senator Warren about Wood instead of sending a letter, rebukes George Carter for airing MacArthur's slurs on German-Americans, and asks Admiral Walker whether the Navy should take Yaviza.

headline: On the rights of citizenship
summary: Roosevelt meets the Spanish minister and Root, attends Miss Locke's funeral at St. Paul's at two, and visits Bamie that evening. He writes Shaw twice on Philippine bonds, urges Governor Hunt to hire Puerto Ricans, and tells Carl Schurz why he would not abet stripping Black Southerners of their basic rights.

headline: Stockings on the President's bed
summary: At seven on Christmas morning the children pile onto Roosevelt's bed to open their stockings, while Allan, Kermit's terrier, sits in the thick of it and Bob Ferguson and Aunt Emily looking on. After breakfast the bigger gifts wait in the library on separate tables. The Lodges, the Cowleses, Brooks Adams and Ferguson come to dinner.

headline: A Christmas like the old days
summary: Senator Elkins calls at 9:45 and Secretary Shaw at three. Roosevelt tells Corinne the family's Christmas recalled the ones their parents gave them decades before.

headline: Trouble with Ambassador Storer
summary: Roosevelt writes Bellamy Storer about his indiscreet remarks on getting Archbishop Ireland a cardinal's hat and on removing an American diplomat named Hurst in Vienna.

headline: Lunch with W. B. Yeats
summary: Roosevelt lunches with the Irish poet William Butler Yeats, Maurice Francis Egan and William Dudley Foulke, then confers at three with Moody, Root and Quay.

headline: Hay hosts the Roosevelts
summary: At four the Cabinet takes up Colombia. Roosevelt sees Simon Wolf, and the Hays give a dinner for him and Edith. He writes John Byrne about New York bankers and honest money, and Samuel Small on Southern opposition to the canal.

headline: Reprimanding Storer
summary: Roosevelt receives the Spanish Treaty Claims Commission, Simon Wolf and Congressmen Dixon and Loomis. He rebukes Bellamy Storer over Archbishop Ireland and Hurst, and writes about the postal frauds and three letter carriers fired without cause.

headline: Year-end conferences; Santo Domingo seeks protection
summary: Roosevelt ends the year meeting Root, Garfield, Knapp, Cortelyou and Librarian of Congress Herbert Putnam. Santo Domingo asks the United States to make it a protectorate to keep European powers out.

headline: New Year's reception
summary: Roosevelt confers with Secretary Shaw, then greets the public at the White House New Year's reception from eleven to 1:30.

headline: Lunch with Spooner
summary: Roosevelt lunches with Senator John Spooner.

headline: Sunday, nothing recorded
summary: Roosevelt is in Washington; no activity is noted.

headline: Urging the Senate to ratify
summary: As Congress returns, Roosevelt sends the Senate a special message asking it to approve the canal treaty with Panama. He sees Senator Hansbrough and Whitelaw Reid and lunches with David Starr Jordan, Moody, George Kennan, Merriam and Higgins. He tells Charles Lummis he may not have gone far enough with Colombia.

headline: War clouds over Korea
summary: Russian troops move into Korea, and the Cabinet discusses the Far East. Roosevelt takes a long-distance call from Governor Odell, meets Senator Platt at 12:30, lunches with Baldwin, sees Booker T. Washington at 2:30, and with Edith dines at Secretary Root's.

headline: Lodge carries the treaty fight
summary: Roosevelt asks Senator Quarles how the public is taking his canal policy and receives a stream of callers, among them Smoot, Beveridge, Burrows, Ball, Burton, Humphrey and Baldwin of the Outlook. At noon he attends Isabel McKenna's wedding to Mr. Duffield. He thanks John Bigelow and John Bassett Moore for help and praise on his canal message and writes Lodge, who is leading the Senate fight.

headline: Henry Adams frowns at the court
summary: Roosevelt confers with Quay and sees Allison, Hopkins, Boutell and Mondell. At the evening diplomatic reception Henry Adams is struck by what he considers royal trappings and imperial airs, and judges the presidency changed for the worse. Roosevelt writes Douglas Robinson on family money and Burlingame a comic verse about Panama.

headline: Senators all day, music at night
summary: Roosevelt confers with Representative Hinshaw and Senators Foraker, Aldrich, Fairbanks and Orville Platt, then with John Sleicher and Maurice Low, before a White House dinner and a ten o'clock musicale.

headline: "I ought to be dead"
summary: Roosevelt meets Arthur von Briesen's Ellis Island commission at nine, confers with Congressmen Bartholdt and Burton, Senators Allison and Dolliver, and at 2:30 Ambassador von Sternberg. He tells Jacob Riis his biography is so kind it embarrasses him.

headline: Two Scotts at 9:30
summary: Two evening callers, Captain Charles H. Scott and John Winfield Scott, see the President.

headline: Steering Ted away from West Point
summary: Roosevelt is photographed at nine, confers with Kearns and Aldrich, sees Governor Durbin and others, and lunches with Root, Knox, Beveridge and MacVeagh. He writes Ted weighing military against civilian careers and hoping he will skip West Point and Annapolis.

headline: Persian minister and a Knox dinner
summary: After the Cabinet, Roosevelt meets Senator Elkins, sees Representative Champ Clark, receives Ambassador von Sternberg at 12:30 and the Persian minister at 2:30, and dines with Edith at the Knoxes'.

headline: Naval Academy appointments
summary: Roosevelt confers with Lucius Littauer and sees Penrose, Governor Murray Crane, and Moody, who comes to review Naval Academy appointments.

headline: Snowy ride; Hanna told who the nominee is
summary: After a day of callers, the Roosevelts take their horses through deep snow along Rock Creek, and the White House holds its diplomatic dinner at eight. He writes Hanna, after press talk of a Hanna candidacy, leaving no doubt that he himself will be the nominee.

headline: Ida Tarbell calls
summary: Roosevelt meets the Cabinet, talks New York politics with Woodruff and confers with Beveridge, sees Senator Long at ten and Sternberg at 12:30, lunches with Norman and Alderman, and receives Ida Tarbell at three. He and Edith ride again through the snow before a 10 p.m. musicale.

headline: Callers and canal talks
summary: Among a crowd of callers are Quay, Governor Hill and Senator Beveridge. Roosevelt confers with Hay and Representative Hitt.

headline: Writing Morley about Gladstone
summary: Roosevelt writes John Morley about his life of Gladstone; Morley plans to visit Washington in December.

headline: Michigan Republicans and a juggler
summary: On Bamie's 49th birthday Roosevelt receives a Michigan Republican delegation led by Senators Alger and Burrows, sees Rockhill and Amos Pinchot among others, and sits for Hewitt at 2:30. He tells Kermit the family went to see Kellar the magician, and Ted that he relaxes with riding and broadsword bouts.

headline: Hanna won't fight, he thinks
summary: Hewitt photographs the President at nine and Edith at 2:30. The Cabinet takes up the canal treaty, and Roosevelt confers with Senators Cullom and Allison about it. He and Edith dine at the Paynes', and he tells Joe Bishop he doubts Hanna will contest the nomination.

headline: Springy is engaged
summary: Hewitt photographs the President again at nine. Roosevelt confers with Aldrich on the canal treaty while the House debates the Hepburn pure food bill. Spring-Rice writes Edith from St. Petersburg that he is to marry Florence Lascelles, whom he has known eight years.

headline: Jusserand and the judicial reception
summary: Senators Cullom, Frye and Hopkins and the Board of Indian Commissioners call. Roosevelt receives French Ambassador Jusserand at 2:30 and hosts the judicial reception that evening.

headline: Miles likened to Wilkinson
summary: After the Cabinet, Roosevelt discusses Ohio with Foraker, sees former Governor Merriam and Millard, lunches with Knox and Gates, and hosts a 10 p.m. musicale. Japanese troops land in Korea. He praises Alfred Henry Lewis's The Boss and tells George Harvey that General Miles resembles the early republic's James Wilkinson.

headline: Boone and Crockett dinner
summary: Roosevelt talks canal treaty with Fairbanks, sees Cannon, Grosvenor, Chief Justice Fuller and Justice Harlan, confers with Root, and lunches with Caspar Whitney and Lodge. At eight he goes to the Metropolitan Club to dine with his fellow Boone and Crockett members. He tells Kermit that Ethel is wonderful with the little boys and reports on Loretta the parrot.

headline: A blank Sunday
summary: Roosevelt is in Washington; no activity is recorded.

headline: On writing history
summary: Roosevelt confers with Heyburn, Shaw and Beveridge and sees Dalzell and Lodge. He writes Trevelyan about the craft of history and asks Cortelyou to let Quan Yick Nam, a merchant from China, enter the country.

headline: Good roads from St. Louis
summary: After a Cabinet session on Panama, Roosevelt meets St. Louis's good roads committee, sees Delaware's two senators and Representative Smith, and dines at Moody's. He sends Cullom State Department papers on Panama and Root and Moody memos on Wood and on Army and Navy actions on the isthmus.

headline: Honoring Root at Alger's
summary: Heyburn, George Perkins and Metcalf call, and Sternberg comes at 2:30. From nine to midnight Roosevelt attends a reception for Elihu Root at Russell Alger's home. He tells Hay he opposes the Philippine inter-island shipping bills.

headline: Supreme Court dinner
summary: Roosevelt talks Nebraska politics with Millard, lunches with Root, Taft and Bonaparte, confers with Chauncey Depew, sees the Spanish Treaty Claims Commission, and at eight gives the Supreme Court dinner.

headline: "I doubt if they can prevent my nomination"
summary: After the Cabinet and callers including Aldrich and Beveridge, Roosevelt lunches with Governor Crane, joins a reception for William Howard Taft, and closes with a White House dinner and musicale. He tells Ted that Hanna and Wall Street worry him a little but cannot likely stop him.

headline: Gridiron dinner; nomination "assured"
summary: Roosevelt confers with Crane and Kohlsaat and on Ohio with Foraker, lunches with Alice French, Mrs. Oliver Wendell Holmes, Pinchot and Taft, and goes to the Gridiron Club's dinner; Butler is his overnight guest. He thanks Albert Shaw for friendly editorials and says his nomination is now certain.

headline: Root, Taft, Moody and Archbishop Ireland
summary: After a dinner for Elihu Root, Roosevelt sees Governor Taft at nine, Secretary Moody at 9:30 and Archbishop Ireland at ten. Critics are attacking the Roosevelts' style of living and what they call an imperial presidency.

headline: Root steps down as Secretary of War
summary: Roosevelt learns that Elihu Root, a frequent sparring partner on policy, is leaving the War Department for private practice. Word also comes that rebels at Santo Domingo have shot at the U.S. cruiser Yankee. Senators and Taft fill the day's call list.

headline: Taft becomes Secretary of War
summary: William Howard Taft takes charge of the War Department as Root's term ends. Roosevelt holds a Cabinet session, talks over the Panama treaty with Cullom and railroad regulation with Elkins, then dines at Secretary Hitchcock's home.

headline: Canal money talks with Platt and Shaw
summary: Roosevelt works through the financing of the Panama canal with Senator Orville Platt and Treasury Secretary Shaw, and reviews upcoming bills with Allison. In the evening he hosts a dinner that includes Chapin, Saltonstall, Winsor and Robert Bacon.

headline: Evening reception for Congress
summary: After meetings with Senators Depew, Hopkins and Scott and a noon visit from the German ambassador, Roosevelt hosts the evening reception for members of Congress. His uncle Robert Roosevelt stays over. He writes to novelist Alice Hegan Rice about his love of books.

headline: Filling Taft's seat on the Philippine Commission
summary: The Cabinet takes up who should replace Taft on the Philippine Commission. Roosevelt sees George Perkins, Moody and others and goes to visit Senator Mark Hanna, while reports arrive that rebels near Santo Domingo City are menacing American property.

headline: The Kaiser's letter and Dominican affairs
summary: Roosevelt meets Moody, Loomis and Ambassador Speck von Sternberg, who hands him a letter from Kaiser Wilhelm, to talk over the Dominican crisis. Illinois politicians come in about their state, and Justice Holmes is among the dinner guests. He writes Ted that he regrets losing Root.

headline: Russia and Japan cut ties
summary: Russia and Japan break off diplomatic relations, bringing war in the Far East close. That Sunday evening Roosevelt sees Treasury Secretary Shaw.

headline: Ready to send troops to Santo Domingo
summary: Roosevelt resolves that American troops will go to Santo Domingo to restore order if it comes to that. At noon he goes to St. John's Church to see Justice Brewer's daughter married. He thanks Ambassador Jusserand for sending him the medieval Song of Roland.

headline: Japan strikes Port Arthur
summary: That evening Japanese torpedo boats strike Russia's ships at Port Arthur and the Russo-Japanese War begins. Roosevelt's Cabinet meets on the Far East. He tells Oscar Straus that Japan turned down his offer to mediate, and writes about help for fire-ravaged Baltimore.

headline: Russia declares war on Japan
summary: Russia formally declares war. Roosevelt goes over canal financing again with Secretary Shaw, and the Shoshone reclamation project in Wyoming is established. He tells Ted that winter has left him with little exercise beyond walking.

headline: America declares neutrality
summary: With Japan now formally at war with Russia, Roosevelt issues a proclamation of American neutrality. He talks pensions with Cannon, lunches with Taft and hosts the White House reception for the Army and Navy.

headline: Alice turns twenty
summary: It is Alice's 20th birthday, and the family marks it with a dinner at the White House. Earlier Roosevelt meets his Cabinet, calls on the ailing Senator Hanna and receives Uruguay's new minister. He tells Maryland's governor he will not send troops to Baltimore.

headline: Jamieson told to mind his oath
summary: On a crowded Saturday Roosevelt calls on Mark Hanna and lunches with Harvey, General Greene, Seth Low and Taft. He warns T. N. Jamieson, his embattled pick for Chicago's port, to be scrupulous, and suggests to Moody that the Cabinet consider more ships for Asia.

headline: Mark Hanna dies
summary: Senator Mark Hanna, the Ohio power broker, dies of typhoid fever. Roosevelt's callers that day range from Governor Herrick and Ambassador Sternberg to Buffalo Bill Cody and a group of cotton mill owners, and Ambassador Jusserand comes at midday.

headline: Remembering Hanna
summary: Roosevelt sees H. M. Hanna and talks with Speaker Cannon, then has Lincoln Steffens in that night. He thanks Root for a Union League Club speech that is winning him Wall Street support, and pays warm tribute to Hanna.

headline: Senate funeral for Hanna
summary: Roosevelt attends the Senate's funeral service for Mark Hanna. To Henry White he writes candidly that resistance to his nomination had already crumbled before Hanna fell ill.

headline: Lunch with the Sternbergs
summary: Roosevelt confers with Senator Kean, Taft and Beveridge and receives Senator Millard and others. At lunch he entertains the German ambassador and his wife along with Captain Fournier and the Folgers.

headline: Syracuse delegation calls
summary: After the Cabinet meets, Roosevelt confers with Representative Landis and Senator Thomas Platt and in the afternoon receives Francis Hendricks with a group from Syracuse. He writes Ted about Hanna's death and Buffalo Bill's recent lunch visit.

headline: Dewey sent to look into Santo Domingo
summary: Roosevelt meets a run of senators, including Lodge and Thomas Platt, and lunches with Hendricks and Hiscock. He picks Admiral Dewey, joined by Loomis and Admiral Taylor, to look into the troubles in Santo Domingo.

headline: A quiet Sunday note to Corinne
summary: Roosevelt sends his sister Corinne a brief thank-you. In the evening Admiral Walker and Loomis come to the White House.

headline: Root defends the Panama policy
summary: Roosevelt confers with Senators Perkins and Bard about the canal commission and with railroad man A. J. Cassatt, Thomas Platt and Admiral Walker. In Chicago that day Elihu Root tells the Union League Club that the President's course on Panama was right.

headline: Senate ratifies the Panama treaty
summary: The Senate approves the canal treaty with Panama. Roosevelt's Cabinet meets on Dominican affairs, and his dinner table holds Gifford and Amos Pinchot, Leupp, Moody and the Rev. Rainsford, who stays over. He tells Bishop he has no wish to meddle in Santo Domingo.

headline: Canal Zone health on his mind
summary: Roosevelt talks New York politics with Depew and lunches with Kohlsaat. Benjamin Ide Wheeler spends the night after dinner with the Garfields, Cooley and Librarian of Congress Putnam. Roosevelt writes Admiral Walker about sanitation on the isthmus.

headline: Roosevelt approves the canal treaty
summary: Roosevelt gives his own approval to the Panama Canal Treaty. He lunches with the Jusserands, Walter Berry, Benjamin Wheeler, and the young poet George Cabot Lodge with his wife, and dines that night with Senator Lodge. He writes Bonaparte about support for Indian mission schools.

headline: Proclaiming the Panama canal treaty
summary: Roosevelt formally proclaims the treaty with the Republic of Panama that clears the way for an American-built canal. Earlier he hears from Dr. Rixey on health conditions on the isthmus and the Cabinet takes up the Philippine Commission. He tells William Hale he hopes to keep involvement in Santo Domingo small.

headline: Quentin's candy riot
summary: Panama's minister Philippe Bunau-Varilla calls in the afternoon. Roosevelt writes Kermit a lively family bulletin: Quentin and his nurse Mame are both laid up, Edith is home from three days in New York, and Ethel has been a big help with the younger boys.

headline: Sunday evening with Knox and Bacon
summary: Roosevelt spends Sunday evening with two callers: Attorney General Knox at 8:30 and his old friend Robert Bacon an hour later.

headline: Leap-day essay on the party's mission
summary: The Critic prints a Roosevelt essay on what the Republican Party is for. He sees Knox and Lodge during the day and has Speaker Cannon and Senator Allison in that night.

headline: Cabinet on the canal contract
summary: The Cabinet works on the Panama canal contract. Roosevelt then confers with a long line of lawmakers and officials, among them Fairbanks, Aldrich, Beveridge and Thomas Platt, and lunches with Navy Secretary Moody.

headline: An Arizona nominee withdraws
summary: Roosevelt confers with Lodge and shares lunch with Taft, Jessup and Truman Newberry. He tells Senator Thomas Platt that Isaac Stoddard, nephew of a Platt friend, has pulled out of the running for Secretary of Arizona Territory.

headline: Dinner at Justice Holmes's
summary: Roosevelt and Edith are Justice Oliver Wendell Holmes's dinner guests. During the day he talks New York politics with Littauer, receives Japan's minister Takahira and lunches with Stranahan.

headline: Talking about a Pacific cable
summary: The Cabinet discusses a proposed cable across the Pacific. Roosevelt confers with Admiral Walker, Foraker and Thomas Platt, visits with Japanese minister Takahira and lunches with Bonaparte and Hitchcock.

headline: Wrestling Japanese style
summary: Admiral Dewey's commission reaches Santo Domingo. Roosevelt fills a big dinner table with Cabinet members, senators, Pinchot, Lodge and Holmes; Admiral Frothingham and historian A. B. Hart stay over. He tells Kermit he wrestles two Japanese wrestlers three times a week and has a sore throat from being choked.

headline: Bible Society centennial at St. John's
summary: Roosevelt and Edith go to St. John's Church in the afternoon for the hundredth anniversary of the Bible Society. Secretary Shaw calls that evening.

headline: Public lands report arrives
summary: Roosevelt gets the first findings of his commission on public lands, and the Bonaparte-Woodruff findings on Indian Territory go to Congress. He lunches with Governor Crane, works on canal talks with Knox and Walker, sees Lincoln Steffens among his callers and dines at Secretary Moody's.

headline: Chief Joseph's fare home
summary: The Cabinet meets on canal negotiations without the ailing Agriculture Secretary Wilson. Roosevelt charges the new Isthmian Canal Commission and tells Interior Secretary Hitchcock that the government must pay for Chief Joseph's trip home from Washington.

headline: Henry Adams sizes him up
summary: Roosevelt rides out to Arlington, Virginia, in the afternoon to see the ailing Postmaster General Payne. Henry Adams dines at the White House and afterward writes that the President now talks of nothing but the election.

headline: Post Office report under review
summary: Roosevelt talks with Hay about enforcing neutrality, and with Cannon, Overstreet and Bristow about Payne's report on the Post Office scandals.

headline: Albert Shaw and LaFarge stay over
summary: After the Cabinet meets, Roosevelt discusses civil service pensions with Sulloway and Gibson. Editor Albert Shaw and architect Grant LaFarge come to dinner with Taft and Chandler, and both stay the night.

headline: Sitting for Mr. Handy
summary: Photographer Handy comes at 9 a.m. to take Roosevelt's picture. He lunches with Harvey, Moody, Taft, Knox and MacKay, and Joseph Bishop stays the night. He tells Charles Mellen he cannot predict how the Northern Securities case will end.

headline: Supper at Bamie's
summary: Roosevelt spends Sunday evening at supper with his sister Bamie.

headline: Northern Securities broken up
summary: By a 5-4 vote the Supreme Court rules that the Northern Securities Company broke the Sherman Antitrust Act and must be dissolved, a landmark win for Roosevelt's trust policy. He shares lunch with Cardinal Gibbons, Secretary Hay, Moody and his sister Bamie and defends his White House spending to Lawrence Abbott.

headline: Cabinet weighs the court ruling
summary: The Cabinet discusses the Northern Securities decision. Roosevelt sees Senator Hopkins and congratulates Andrew Draper on becoming New York's first state Commissioner of Education.

headline: Lunch with Mrs. Lodge and Taft
summary: Roosevelt confers with Senator Foraker and has Taft, Bowers and three ladies, Mrs. Lodge among them, to lunch. He writes James Roche about American neutrality in the war in Asia.

headline: Explaining White House expenses
summary: Roosevelt lunches with AP chief Melville Stone and John Wise. He tells Illinois Governor Richard Yates he will not stand in the way of his renomination and sends editor St. Clair McKelway a detailed account of White House spending.

headline: Lunch with Bliss
summary: A quieter day: Roosevelt receives Allison, Foraker, Beveridge, Kean, Millard and Leupp, and lunches with Bliss.

headline: Wood confirmed as major general
summary: Roosevelt lunches with illustrator Howard Pyle and sees Booker T. Washington in the afternoon. He tells Leonard Wood the Senate has unexpectedly confirmed him as major general, and assures Spring-Rice that he means to keep America neutral in the Russo-Japanese War.

headline: Root brokers a Platt-Odell truce
summary: Roosevelt breakfasts with James Sheffield. That day Elihu Root sits down with Depew, Thomas Platt, Governor Odell and Dunn and makes peace in New York's Republican ranks: Odell will chair the state party while Platt stays its leader.

headline: Congratulations all around
summary: Roosevelt sends warm notes to Thomas Platt, Governor Odell and Root on the New York peace settlement. He receives the Isthmian Canal Commission, lunches with Sheffield, Knox and Adams, and hosts a dinner that includes Justice Day, the Aldriches, Forakers and Mrs. Leonard Wood.

headline: Lunch with the canal commissioners
summary: After the Cabinet meets, Roosevelt lunches with the Canal Commission and Secretary Taft, talks Alaska with Kearns and sees Hendricks in the afternoon.

headline: Ohio and Missouri politics
summary: Roosevelt goes over Ohio politics with Senator Dick and Missouri politics with Representative Bartholdt, receives Elkins and Redfield Proctor, and lunches with Noyes and James.

headline: Platt and Odell as Jungle Book wolves
summary: Roosevelt talks Illinois politics with Representative Rodenberg and receives Depew, Penrose and Hill of the Tribune. Writing to Root, he says the two New York chieftains remind him of Kipling's Jungle Book wolves, and sends Knox two letters on labor planks for the convention.

headline: No canal job for his friend Bishop
summary: After the Cabinet meets, Roosevelt sees Admiral Walker about the Canal Commission. He explains to Joseph Bishop, who hopes to become the commission's secretary, that their close friendship makes the appointment awkward.

headline: Telling the public about the Beef Trust
summary: Roosevelt plans for the Republican convention with Senator Scott and meets the Canal Commission. Among his callers are Japan's envoy Kaneko, Richard Olney and Lodge. He urges Knox to publicize what has been done against the Beef Trust.

headline: Sunday call from cousin Emlen
summary: Roosevelt's cousin Emlen Roosevelt visits him on Sunday morning.

headline: A senator convicted of fraud
summary: Senator Joseph Burton of Kansas is found guilty in a postal fraud case. Roosevelt goes over money bills with Aldrich and Cannon, lunches with the Chinese-born physician Dr. Yamei Kin, and writes Knox about the verdict.

headline: Praise for Lounsbury on language
summary: The Cabinet meets, and Roosevelt goes over canal finances with Knox and lunches with Father Vattman. He compliments Yale scholar Thomas Lounsbury on an article about language.

headline: A fitting with the tailor
summary: At 9 a.m. tailor Rock arrives to fit Roosevelt for new clothes. He goes over spending bills with Hemenway and tells Senator Foraker that the island possessions should be run by the Secretary of War.

headline: Canal money, campaign plans, dinner with Holmes
summary: Roosevelt goes over canal finances with Attorney General Knox and the coming Republican campaign with Senator Quay, then dines with Justice Oliver Wendell Holmes. Across the Atlantic, Britain and France are closing in on the Entente Cordiale, trading a free French hand in Morocco for British control in Egypt.

headline: Sims and better naval gunnery
summary: The Cabinet takes up canal finances. Roosevelt writes Moody about Lieutenant Sims's push for better naval gunnery and new gun sights, and writes his brother-in-law Will Cowles about the inquiry into the collision of Cowles's Missouri with the Illinois.

headline: Dinner with the Roots and Lodges
summary: Roosevelt lunches with Elihu Root, receives the Countess Cassini in the afternoon, and at 8 p.m. dines with the Roots, the Lodges, the Wadsworths and Taft.

headline: Correcting the press on the Cowles inquiry
summary: On Sunday Roosevelt writes Navy Secretary Moody about the findings of the Cowles inquiry and the made-up newspaper accounts of them.

headline: An unsent letter to Eliot
summary: Roosevelt sees Moody and a group of steel executives from Pittsburgh and dines with Mr. and Mrs. Parsons. He drafts but holds back a letter to Harvard's Charles Eliot arguing that the Philippines are not yet ready for independence.

headline: Root says no to the national chairmanship
summary: The Cabinet discusses a strike on the Panama Railroad. Roosevelt dines with the Leupps, Garfields, Foulkes, Egans and Wares, and tells Charles Emory Smith that Root cannot chair the Republican National Committee and asks him to draft the platform.

headline: Who will chair the convention
summary: On a packed day Roosevelt discusses the convention chairmanship with Depew and Thomas Platt and New York politics with J. A. Stewart. He lunches with Knox, Grey and Dodge.

headline: Speaking to the magazine publishers
summary: Roosevelt addresses the Periodical Publishers Association dinner. Earlier he sees Knox, receives his Dakota friend Seth Bullock among other callers and lunches with L. Clarke Davis. Jacob Riis stays the night.

headline: Quentin gets a spanking
summary: The Cabinet discusses Chinese exclusion. Roosevelt's lunch table holds Jacob Riis, Seth Bullock, William Allen White, Moody, editor Norman Hapgood and publisher Robert Collier. At home he has to spank young Quentin for stealing.

headline: Archie turns ten
summary: It is Archie's tenth birthday: he gets a cake and a tool chest. Roosevelt lunches aboard the Mayflower and dines with Bamie, Bob Ferguson and David Gray. He tells Ted his Japanese wrestling has left him bruised but taught him three new throws, and tells Kermit, down with mumps, about press lies.

headline: Sunday lunch with conservation allies
summary: Roosevelt has Sunday lunch with Gifford Pinchot, James Garfield and William Dudley Foulke.

headline: Lunch with Bishop Spalding
summary: Roosevelt lunches with Bishop Spalding, George Meyer and Rawle.

headline: Shaws host the Roosevelts
summary: The Cabinet meets on the Chinese exclusion laws. Roosevelt confers with Fulton, receives tariff advocates from the American Protective Tariff League and others, and he and Edith dine with Secretary and Mrs. Shaw.

headline: Deadly blast on the Missouri
summary: An explosion during target practice aboard the battleship Missouri kills 33 men. Roosevelt confers on a proposed Senate probe of the Post Office Department and on Canal Zone bills, and sees George Perkins at night.

headline: Pushing the canal bill
summary: Roosevelt continues talks on the Post Office investigation with Penrose, Aldrich and Spooner and greets members of the Knights of Columbus at a reception. He asks Representative Hepburn to get the canal bill through.

headline: More on Chinese exclusion
summary: Roosevelt confers with Spooner, receives Warren, Fairbanks and Quarles, and holds another Cabinet session on the Chinese exclusion laws.

headline: Standing by Crum
summary: On a busy Saturday Roosevelt discusses Chinese exclusion with Knox, sees a delegation from Alaska and several senators, and tells Senator Aldrich that Congress must confirm William Crum. He sets up a meeting with Cornelius Bliss about the national chairmanship.

headline: Breakfast with Owen Wister
summary: Roosevelt breakfasts at the Shaws' with novelist Owen Wister. Former Senator William Chandler calls late in the evening.

headline: An afternoon at the theater
summary: Roosevelt discusses Indian affairs with Penrose, Fulton and Philip Stewart and West Virginia's party squabbles with Senator Scott, lunches with Taft and attends a benefit show at the Lafayette Theater.

headline: Wister and Stewart Edward White as houseguests
summary: The Cabinet discusses wireless telegraphy. Roosevelt confers with Senator Orville Platt, and writers Owen Wister and Stewart Edward White are overnight guests.

headline: Veterans and senators
summary: On a heavy day Roosevelt confers with former Puerto Rico Governor Hunt and Knox, receives Spooner, Beveridge, Akins and a party of Union veterans from the Grand Army, and lunches with Ambassador Sternberg.

headline: Food for Indian schoolchildren
summary: Roosevelt signs a bill allowing rations for children at Indian mission schools. He writes George Bowers about California's golden trout and Moody about naval marksmanship, among a full day of conferences and letters.

headline: Meeting Hugo Münsterberg
summary: After the Cabinet meets, Roosevelt confers with Harvard psychologist Hugo Münsterberg, with Wadsworth, and with Lacey about public land bills.

headline: Winthrop to govern Puerto Rico
summary: Roosevelt appoints Beekman Winthrop governor of Puerto Rico, and the Minidoka reclamation project in Idaho is established. He dines with Nicholas Murray Butler and Joseph Bishop and writes his Harvard-era friend Kentaro Kaneko praising the Japanese people.

headline: Sunday dinner with Cameron
summary: Roosevelt dines on Sunday with Cameron.

headline: Odell comes to talk New York
summary: Governor Odell confers with Roosevelt on New York politics and stays for lunch with Littauer, Warren and Sherman. A musicale is held at four, and Roosevelt writes a memorandum on Senator Proctor's talk with him about appointments.

headline: Lunch at Hay's, dinner at Cortelyou's
summary: The Cabinet meets on canal affairs. Roosevelt and Edith lunch at Secretary Hay's and dine at Secretary Cortelyou's. He tells Cardinal Gibbons that Dominic Murphy will join the Canal Commission staff.

headline: Sullys Hill set aside
summary: Sullys Hill National Park in North Dakota is established. Roosevelt discusses the homestead laws with Representatives Dietrich and Kinkaid and lunches with Governor Murray Crane.

headline: Congress creates the Canal Zone government
summary: An act of Congress provides for governing the Panama Canal Zone, and Congress adjourns. Roosevelt names Thomas Dawson minister to Santo Domingo and writes Nicholas Murray Butler about the ICC and the coal walkout.

headline: Richard Strauss at the White House
summary: On Corinne's 22nd wedding anniversary, Roosevelt talks Kansas politics with Senator Long and the state's governor, Willis Bailey and lunches with Civil War General Osterhaus and others. Composer Richard Strauss is among his callers. He tells Butler why Bishop did not get the canal post.

headline: The St. Louis World's Fair opens
summary: The Louisiana Purchase Exposition opens in St. Louis. Roosevelt hosts a large lunch for visiting royalty with Bamie, Lodge, Hay, Whitelaw Reid and the German ambassador, then watches a drill at Fort Myer with Edith. His article on the merit system appears in Cosmopolitan.

headline: Sunday-night platform session
summary: On Sunday evening Roosevelt gathers the Republican leadership, including Aldrich, Allison, Spooner, Lodge, Cannon and Cortelyou, to shape the party's campaign platform.

headline: Choosing a chairman and a running mate
summary: After breakfast with Von Briesen, Roosevelt and senior senators weigh who should run the national committee and who should share the ticket. He also talks New York politics with Thomas Platt and tells Senator Proctor that letters clear Secretary Shaw of Proctor's charges.

headline: Alice's rivalry over Nick Longworth
summary: Roosevelt meets the Cabinet, Postmaster General Payne and Admiral Walker. In her diary Alice writes of her rivalry with Marguerite Cassini, the Russian ambassador's daughter, over Ohio congressman Nicholas Longworth, who had proposed to Marguerite and been refused.

headline: Platform work and a conservation lunch
summary: Roosevelt works on the Republican platform with Cortelyou and Senators Spooner, Cullom and Allison, then lunches with Cornelius Bliss, Gifford Pinchot and James Garfield.

headline: A day of callers
summary: Roosevelt's visitors include Lodge, Burrows, Fulton, Ball and Senator Redfield Proctor.

headline: Asking Bliss to run the campaign
summary: The Cabinet discusses the canal, and Roosevelt talks with Representative Adams about a proposed immigration bill before lunching with Taft. He writes Cornelius Bliss that he wants him as Republican national chairman.

headline: Labor delegation from Baltimore
summary: Roosevelt confers with Admiral Walker on the canal and receives a delegation from the Baltimore branch of the American Federation of Labor.

headline: Evening callers Fish and Sternberg
summary: Roosevelt receives Hamilton Fish at nine on Sunday evening and Ambassador Speck von Sternberg half an hour later.

headline: A charter for the Canal Zone
summary: Formal instructions go out to the Isthmian Canal Commission, and Roosevelt sends Taft an official letter laying out the treaty terms, including a six-mile-wide zone, that serve as the Canal Zone's founding charter. He also talks with mine union leader John Mitchell about the Colorado strike.

headline: Three reclamation projects launched
summary: The Yuma, Belle Fourche and Lower Yellowstone reclamation projects are created, the last reaching into North Dakota. The Cabinet takes up canal finances, and Roosevelt asks Payne whether a Black delegate should second his nomination at the convention.

headline: Talking tariff with Lodge
summary: Roosevelt confers with Taft and sees Hitt and Dr. Rixey. He writes Benjamin Ide Wheeler about a French study of the Phoenicians and the Odyssey, and Lodge about the protective tariff in the platform.

headline: Bliss turns down the chairmanship
summary: Roosevelt writes Root about politics and learns that Cornelius Bliss will not take the national chairmanship. He tells Bliss he will likely press for George Cortelyou instead.

headline: Will Fairbanks run?
summary: After the Cabinet meets, Roosevelt receives the Spanish minister. Robb's findings about the post office in New York are published. He asks Senator Beveridge whether Fairbanks will accept the vice-presidential slot, since Fairbanks keeps telling reporters he will not.

headline: Saving the old elm in Lafayette Park
summary: Roosevelt receives Archbishop Riordan and the German ambassador and attends Miss Young's musicale. He tells Ted about scrambles in Rock Creek Park and his preference for Robert Hitt over Fairbanks as running mate, and forbids the felling of an old elm in Lafayette Park.

headline: A blank Sunday
summary: The record for this Sunday in Washington is empty.

headline: The Riises stay over
summary: Photographer Oscar Marshall takes Roosevelt's picture in the morning. He confers with labor statistician Carroll D. Wright, dines with Herbert Smith and Richard Watson Gilder, and has Jacob Riis and his wife as overnight guests.

headline: Cortelyou to run the campaign
summary: George Cortelyou is picked to lead the Republican campaign as national chairman. Elihu Root comes to stay, and Roosevelt writes Butler about politicians who fight party machines.

headline: Drafting the platform with Root and Lodge
summary: Mr. Prince photographs Roosevelt in the morning. After dinner with the Lodges he goes over the proposed party platform line by line with Root, Lodge and Black. Whitridge and Hunt are overnight guests.

headline: Perdicaris kidnapped in Morocco
summary: From Tangier, Consul General Gummere wires that Ion Perdicaris, an American, and his English stepson Cromwell Varley have been seized by the bandit chief Raisuli. Roosevelt orders four warships of the South Atlantic Squadron to Morocco. At home he works on campaign plans with Elmer Dover.

headline: The Roosevelt Corollary
summary: At a dinner marking two years of Cuban independence, Root reads a Roosevelt letter that lays out the policy later called the Roosevelt Corollary. Roosevelt also confers with William Cromwell on the canal and dines with the Lodges and Moody.

headline: White River National Forest
summary: The White River National Forest in Colorado is established. Roosevelt hosts the Republican National Editorial Association at lunch and tells Root he has picked Frank Black to place his name in nomination.

headline: Raisuli names his price
summary: Roosevelt sees Judge Blanchard on Sunday evening. In Morocco, a go-between, the Sherif of Wazan, delivers Raisuli's terms: troops withdrawn, the Bashaw of Tangier dismissed, his partisans freed, a $70,000 payment, and governorship of two districts.

headline: Off to Groton
summary: Roosevelt sees Admiral Evans, Secretary Shaw and others, has Hale, Bacon, Dalzell and Elkins to lunch, and leaves at 5:35 p.m. for Groton, Massachusetts. Admiral Chadwick's squadron steams toward Morocco, with the European Squadron sent to back it up.

headline: Feet on the ground at Groton
summary: Roosevelt speaks to the boys of Groton School, urging them to pair high ideals with practical sense, then heads back to Washington that evening. He offers his good offices to Japan and Russia.

headline: Dinner with Harriman
summary: Back in Washington, Roosevelt receives Shaw, Hale and Alger, lunches with Monsignor O'Connell, Roberto Centaro and his kinsman Captain Harry Roosevelt, and dines with railroad magnate E. H. Harriman. He explains to Senator Orville Platt why he chose Cortelyou.

headline: Gompers in the evening
summary: Landscape gardener Scott Brown calls first thing. Roosevelt confers with Taft, Spooner and others, including Harper's Weekly art editor H. T. Clinton, lunches with the Jusserands and Russian ambassador Cassini, and sees labor leader Samuel Gompers at night.

headline: Peter Rabbit's funeral
summary: Roosevelt rides up Rock Creek after a day of Cabinet and diplomatic business. At home, the children's pet Peter Rabbit dies and gets a funeral: Archie pulls the little coffin in a wagon and Edith is chief mourner. Quentin and Archie, playing in the sandbox, can't wait to get back to Sagamore Hill.

headline: Matthew Quay dies
summary: Senator Matthew Quay of Pennsylvania dies. Roosevelt describes his White House routine to Ted: breakfast with Edith on the South Portico, a garden stroll, work until late afternoon, official guests at lunch, then a ride, walk or tennis. He tells Kermit about a Mount Vernon outing with the children.

headline: Raisuli threatens his captives
summary: Word arrives that Raisuli will kill Perdicaris and Varley unless his demands are met within two days. Roosevelt sees Elliott Woods that night and leaves at 10:30 for Gettysburg.

headline: Memorial Day at Gettysburg
summary: Roosevelt gives a Memorial Day address at Gettysburg and returns to Washington. At Tangier, the Brooklyn and Admiral Chadwick's squadron drop anchor at dawn, and Moroccan Foreign Minister Mohammed Torres comes aboard but refuses Raisuli's terms.

headline: La Follette men come calling
summary: Roosevelt receives a delegation of Wisconsin Republicans loyal to Robert La Follette, and Mr. Prince photographs him in the East Room. Alice is off seeing the St. Louis fair.

headline: Is Perdicaris even American?
summary: A North Carolina man, A. H. Slocomb, privately tells the State Department that Perdicaris is a Greek citizen, not an American, and Roosevelt huddles with Hay, Moody and Admiral Evans over it. He and Edith have a late-afternoon lunch at the Library of Congress as guests of Librarian Herbert Putnam.

headline: A record for Root's convention speech
summary: Roosevelt sees Senator Foraker and talks Alaska with Knox. For Root's convention speech he sends a list of his administration's achievements, and he confides to Lodge that he is unsure how the election will turn out.

headline: A three-hour scramble with Crozier
summary: Roosevelt has General Crozier and two admirals, Evans and Taylor, to lunch, then takes Crozier on a three-hour cross-country scramble. He sends Butler a very long letter on falsehoods in Collier's and other magazines.

headline: Praise for Wood among the Moros
summary: Washington asks its envoy in Greece to verify whether Perdicaris is a Greek national. Roosevelt lunches with Warner Miller and Paul Morton, and writes Leonard Wood praising his work with the Moros and noting Wood has been hurt at singlestick.

headline: Planning a point-to-point walk
summary: On Sunday Roosevelt writes Ted that the horse Renown has died, that the family is puzzling over Kermit's going to St. Louis, and that once home he will lead a point-to-point hike through the pond and marsh. He and Edith have just ridden on the Virginia side.

headline: Talking peace with Takahira and Kaneko
summary: Roosevelt lunches with Japan's Takahira and Kaneko, Pinchot and Bromwell, a talk he later recounts at length to Spring-Rice. He discusses a board for the planned Great Lakes naval training school with Moody and hosts a reception for Ambassador Jusserand.

headline: Perdicaris turns out to be Greek
summary: Word comes from Athens that Perdicaris became a Greek citizen in 1862. Seven American warships now lie off Tangier, a British warship arrives and France asks what America intends in Morocco. Roosevelt writes Root about the outcry over his Monroe Doctrine letter.

headline: Strike war at Cripple Creek
summary: Violence breaks out in the Cripple Creek mining district of Colorado, beginning a long strike. Roosevelt confers with Taft and Hitt and holds a public reception. He explains to Leonard Wood why he will not be named governor general of the Philippines.

headline: Knox to take Quay's Senate seat
summary: Word comes that Attorney General Knox will succeed the late Matthew Quay in the Senate. Roosevelt confers with Hay, Taft, Shaw and Hitchcock, lunches with Speaker Cannon and others, and he and Edith dine with the Hays.

headline: Welcoming the Philippine commissioners
summary: The Cabinet discusses Cortelyou's tour inspecting immigration in the U.S. and Canada. Roosevelt entertains the commissioners from the Philippines at a luncheon and reception and dines with Taft, Moody, Cortelyou and Lyman Abbott.

headline: An owl in the mail
summary: Roosevelt watches a monument to Richard Rush unveiled at the Naval Museum, lunches with Hawaii's Governor Carter and Beekman Winthrop, and has Lyman Abbott and Joseph Bishop as guests. He writes Quentin a bird-picture note about feeding a young elk at the zoo, and tells Archie an owl came in the mail.

headline: Butler for the night
summary: Roosevelt talks New York politics with Littauer and Philippine affairs with Taft. Nicholas Murray Butler comes to dinner and stays the night. He writes Spring-Rice a full account of his June 6 talk with Takahira and Kaneko about the war.

headline: Praise for Root's speech
summary: After the Cabinet meets, Roosevelt talks West Virginia politics with Representatives Dayton and Hughes and lunches with George Gould and Butler. He sends Root two letters praising his speech and discussing Cabinet changes. Edith writes Kermit about her own struggles learning languages as a girl.

headline: The General Slocum burns
summary: The excursion steamer General Slocum catches fire in New York's East River, killing many women and children. Raisuli raises his demands, and Roosevelt tells Hay the government has gone as far as it can for Perdicaris, while exploring joint action with Britain and France if the captive is harmed.

headline: Ordering a Slocum inquiry
summary: Roosevelt orders an investigation into the General Slocum disaster. He receives Paul Morton and Lincoln Steffens, lunches with Benjamin Ide Wheeler and Frank Travers, and names Victor Metcalf Secretary of Commerce and Labor.

headline: Standing by Cortelyou
summary: After a Cabinet session on naval and judicial business, Roosevelt leaves for Hyde Park. He wires that he will tolerate no opposition to Cortelyou as party chairman, telling Cortelyou that disloyalty to him is disloyalty to the party.

headline: A family wedding at Hyde Park
summary: At Hyde Park, Roosevelt sees his nephew Theodore Douglas Robinson married to Helen Rebecca Roosevelt, whose father is James "Rosy" Roosevelt, then heads to Philadelphia.

headline: Unplanned remarks at Valley Forge
summary: Roosevelt spends Sunday at Attorney General Knox's home at Valley Forge and gives an impromptu talk in a church there. Gummere cables that Raisuli's demands have all been met and Perdicaris should go free on June 21. Roosevelt leaves for Washington that evening.

headline: Raisuli backs out
summary: Roosevelt confers with Cortelyou about the Slocum investigation and sees Ambassadors Cassini and Jusserand. Raisuli calls off the release; Gummere and Chadwick believe Moroccan officials are plotting against him.

headline: Convention opens in Chicago
summary: Republicans gather in Chicago for their national convention while Roosevelt stays in Washington for Cabinet talks on the Slocum disaster. Gummere warns that America's position in Morocco is becoming humiliating and urges landing Marines. Roosevelt sends letters, some with pictures, to his children at Sagamore Hill.

headline: Perdicaris alive or Raisuli dead
summary: As the convention continues, Hay sends his blunt cable to Morocco demanding Perdicaris be saved or his captor killed, while forbidding a Marine landing. Unknown to Washington, Raisuli is already escorting Perdicaris and Varley to Tangier, and they are freed that evening.

headline: Nominated for President
summary: The Republican convention in Chicago nominates Roosevelt for President, with Senator Charles Fairbanks of Indiana as his running mate. Just after lunch, as he and Edith sit on the White House's South Portico, his secretary William Loeb arrives with word of the vote.

headline: Edith heads to Oyster Bay
summary: Japan loses some 1,200 men in a battle with Russia. The Cabinet discusses tariffs for the Canal Zone, and the coming Cabinet shuffle is announced. Edith leaves for the summer at Oyster Bay, and Seth Low dines and stays the night. Roosevelt congratulates Fairbanks.

headline: Morton takes the Navy
summary: Roosevelt sees Admiral Dewey, Shaw and General Chaffee among others, lunches with S. M. Ferris and the Tafts, and welcomes Panama's minister De Obaldía. He charges Paul Morton, his new Navy Secretary, to carry on Moody's good work.

headline: A quiet Sunday
summary: Nothing is recorded for this Sunday in Washington.

headline: Lunch with Hay and Sternberg
summary: Roosevelt receives Cortelyou, Elmer Dover and Boutell, confers with Payne, and lunches with Hay, Ambassador Sternberg, Simpson, who stays over, and Captain Rutgers. He dines with General Oliver and the Cortelyous.

headline: Cripple Creek on his mind
