headline: Camp moves to a salt marsh
summary: The safari packs up and moves camp to a salt marsh.

headline: A big Grant's buck and a rhino
summary: On the Fourth of July Roosevelt takes a large Grant's gazelle buck and a rhino, measuring its two horns.

headline: Wildebeest at 280 yards
summary: Roosevelt drops a wildebeest buck on the run, along with a sow and a Thomson's gazelle.

headline: Back to the Guaso Nyero camp
summary: The party returns to its earlier campsite on the Guaso Nyero.

headline: A writing day
summary: Roosevelt spends the day at his writing.

headline: Return to the Nyarok
summary: The safari marches to the Nyarok; Roosevelt shoots a Thomson's gazelle at 230 yards.

headline: Recrossing the thirst
summary: The party reaches the camp it used after crossing the thirst on the way south.

headline: Leaving the ox wagons behind
summary: Roosevelt parts from the ox wagons and heads for Lake Naivasha, making camp after dark at the base of the Mau.

headline: Water at last, then Naivasha
summary: The marchers find water by mid-morning and make Naivasha by nightfall.

headline: Edith settles on the Italian Riviera
summary: Roosevelt moves to Attenborough's place at Naivasha. Congress sends the income tax amendment to the states. In Italy, Edith and the children are met at Genoa and settle into the little Villa Magna Quies near Porto Maurizio, with a Secret Service man on guard; the children take up bicycles and lessons with Franciscan friars.

headline: Kermit kills a hippo
summary: Out on the lake in a launch, Kermit shoots a hippopotamus.

headline: Rowing the marshes
summary: Roosevelt works the lakeside marsh from a rowboat. In Washington, Alice is late to a Bastille Day dinner, and Butt records Taft's mixed view of her: disapproving, yet charmed by her quick tongue.

headline: Charged by a hippo
summary: A hippopotamus charges Roosevelt on Lake Naivasha.

headline: Writing through a fever
summary: Roosevelt keeps writing despite a bout of fever, and sends Oscar Straus congratulations on his appointment as ambassador to Turkey.

headline: Praise for Kermit's photographs
summary: Still feverish, Roosevelt writes on. He tells Robert Bridges that Kermit's photos are good and will run with the Scribner's pieces, and The Outlook prints his essay on poverty and riches.

headline: On the mend
summary: Roosevelt notes that the fever is lifting.

headline: Hudson tubes open back home
summary: While Roosevelt stays by Lake Naivasha, the Hudson tubes open under the river linking Manhattan with Jersey City.

headline: Five hippos
summary: Roosevelt records five hippos in his diary, with sketches.

headline: Upset over Henry White's removal
summary: Roosevelt works in camp and writes Henry White, whom Taft has replaced as ambassador in Paris despite assurances; he calls it a tragedy. Edith tells Kermit of walks on donkey paths and a pebbly Italian beach.

headline: Ibis by the lake
summary: Roosevelt rides to Naivasha and shoots two ibis, one in flight. Archie Butt dines with the Longworths, where Alice mentions keeping a diary through her first two White House years.

headline: Funding secured for the safari
summary: Heading back toward Nairobi, Roosevelt shoots a pelican from a boat. He tells Charles Walcott of the Smithsonian that $70,000 is now in the bank for the expedition, and reports on specimens collected.

headline: Back in Nairobi for race week
summary: After a long trek the party is back in Nairobi, staying again with the McMillans. Roosevelt sees Selous, and Kermit rides in the race week events.

headline: Sunday at Juja Farm
summary: Roosevelt goes to church from the McMillans' Juja Farm.

headline: Catching up with Lodge
summary: Roosevelt dines with Edwards. He writes Lodge, missing their contact, about Root, Platt, White's ouster, the tariff, his specimens and a charging hippo, and thanks Carnegie for the money.

headline: Blissfully ignorant of politics
summary: Roosevelt dines at the Wards'. He tells Bamie he is refitting at the McMillans' and has eight Scribner's articles done, and writes Corinne about Carnegie's generosity and his happy distance from American politics.

headline: Dinner with Hobley
summary: Roosevelt is a dinner guest of C. W. Hobley.

headline: Turf Club dinner at the Norfolk
summary: Roosevelt attends the races and an 8 p.m. Turf Club dinner at the Norfolk Hotel in Nairobi.

headline: Time with Governor Jackson
summary: Roosevelt's diary notes Governor Frederick Jackson for the day.

headline: An aviator at the races
summary: Roosevelt sees an aviator and the races. In France, Ethel and Archie tour Provence with Ambassador Lloyd Griscom and his wife.

headline: Presbyterian service in Nairobi
summary: Roosevelt worships at the Scotch Presbyterian church.

headline: A dance at the Nairobi Club
summary: Roosevelt goes to a dance at the Nairobi Club. A letter from Edith says she is glad of the extra room with Ethel and Archie off traveling.

headline: Speaking on education in Africa
summary: In Nairobi, Roosevelt gives an address on education in Africa, then goes out to dinner.

headline: Cornerstone at Kijabe, springhaas by lantern
summary: Roosevelt lays the cornerstone for a new building at the Kijabe mission and travels on to Naivasha. That night Mearns and Loring take him hunting springhaas, dazzling them with a lantern.

headline: Rain, then an afternoon hunt
summary: A wet morning at Lake Naivasha gives way to an afternoon of hunting. Edith and Quentin, with a Swiss maid, head for Avignon.

headline: Edith's birthday in Provence
summary: Edith turns 48. She and Quentin see the Papal Palace in Avignon and a play in the Roman theater at Orange, then rejoin Archie and Ethel at Lyon. Taft puts his name to the Payne-Aldrich tariff and a Philippine free-trade bill.

headline: Bad misses, one good shot
summary: Roosevelt grumbles about his misses but notes a fine shot at a stork at 180 yards.

headline: Bound for the Aberdares
summary: Roosevelt and Kermit leave Nairobi for the Mount Kenya country, starting toward the Aberdare Range. Edith writes her Aunt Lizzie that she is growing more sure of managing on her own.

headline: At the base of the Aberdares
summary: The safari reaches the foot of the Aberdare Range.

headline: Cold on the Aberdare crest
summary: Roosevelt crosses the top of the Aberdares and finds it bitterly cold.

headline: Edith in Paris with old friends
summary: The safari pushes on toward Nyeri. In Paris, Edith and the children take an apartment on the Avenue Gabriel, share lunch with the Jusserands and Sturgis Bigelow, and dine with Henry Adams.

headline: A Kikuyu dance at Nyeri
summary: At Nyeri Roosevelt watches a Kikuyu dance, and the day is captured on film.

headline: Kermit heads north with Tarlton
summary: Kermit and Leslie Tarlton strike off northward on their own. In France it is Ethel's birthday.

headline: Fever on the road to Kenya
summary: Roosevelt moves toward Mount Kenya with a fever.

headline: Feeling better in the foothills
summary: Camped in the Kenya foothills, Roosevelt reports he is improving.

headline: A slight relapse
summary: Roosevelt stays in camp with a mild return of fever. At Beverly, Massachusetts, where he is vacationing with Taft, Archie Butt gets a Roosevelt letter written June 27.

headline: News from Archie Butt
summary: A rainy day on the mountain. Butt writes Roosevelt about life under Taft, Alice and Nick, the tariff battle, Mrs. Taft's poor health and the public's endless fascination with TR.

headline: Off after elephants
summary: Roosevelt sets out on an elephant hunt with light Whymper tents.

headline: First bull elephant
summary: Roosevelt kills a bull elephant on the slopes of Mount Kenya.

headline: Walking back to base
summary: Roosevelt hikes back to the main camp, leaving Cunninghame and Heller behind with the elephant.

headline: Writing at Mount Kenya
summary: Roosevelt spends the day writing.

headline: March to Nyeri
summary: The party marches to Nyeri.

headline: Another writing day
summary: Roosevelt writes in camp near Mount Kenya.

headline: Homesick, he tells Ethel
summary: Roosevelt prepares a new safari with Maxwell and Kikuyu porters. Writing Ethel, he admits he is homesick, talks of money and her mother's thrift, and says Kermit sometimes worries him.

headline: Camp in a forest glade
summary: In the afternoon the safari marches and pitches camp in a glade in the forest.

headline: Eighteen miles on foot
summary: Roosevelt covers 18 miles and shoots a steinbuck along the way.

headline: Thunder on the march
summary: After a ten-mile march to camp, a heavy thunderstorm rolls in during the afternoon. Film shot around Roosevelt's camp this month survives.

headline: All-day hunt in the rain
summary: Roosevelt hunts from morning to evening, with heavy rain after midday, and takes a steinbuck.

headline: A bull eland
summary: Roosevelt shoots a bull eland at 280 yards.

headline: Oryx at 450 yards
summary: Roosevelt brings down a cow oryx at long range and a marabou stork.

headline: The Ballinger-Pinchot fight begins
summary: Roosevelt misses a waterbuck and wounds an oryx that gets away. Alice has surgery to remove bone from her troublesome jaw. At home, Interior Secretary Ballinger and Gifford Pinchot start their feud.

headline: Cook claims the North Pole
summary: Roosevelt wounds an oryx and shoots a crane. From the Shetland Islands, Frederick Cook wires the world's newspapers that he stood at the North Pole in April 1908.

headline: A fine oryx
summary: Roosevelt kills a handsome oryx at 125 yards.

headline: Cunninghame and Heller return
summary: R. J. Cunninghame and Edmund Heller rejoin Roosevelt in the afternoon.

headline: Heading for Meru
summary: The safari turns toward Meru.

headline: Frost on the equator
summary: Marching along the equator, the party wakes to frost after a cold night.

headline: Peary nails the flag to the Pole
summary: Roosevelt reaches Meru Boma on Mount Kenya's northeast slopes and finds Kermit and Tarlton there. The press receives Robert Peary's telegram announcing he stood at the Pole on April 6, launching his long quarrel with Cook.

headline: An elephant charges
summary: At 11 a.m. three elephants are spotted three miles off in rough jungle. One charges, and Roosevelt brings down a bull at 50 yards; the specimen later goes to the University of California.

headline: Writing at Meru
summary: Roosevelt writes in camp.

headline: Kermit gets his elephant
summary: Kermit kills a bull elephant.

headline: Discovering Shakespeare in the bush
summary: Cunninghame and Heller come in and another bull elephant falls. Roosevelt writes Lawrence Abbott, the Lodges and George Otto Trevelyan: he is reading Shakespeare with real pleasure for once in his life, faults Eliot's reading list, and favors an inheritance tax over an income tax.

headline: Ten shots for one elephant
summary: Roosevelt kills a bull elephant at 70 yards; his sketch shows ten hits. Archie and Quentin sail home with an adult escort to start at Groton, Quentin's first year there, while Edith and Ethel remain in Europe.

headline: Cables about the Pole
summary: A quiet day by Roosevelt's diary. He writes William Foran about three cables concerning the rival Cook and Peary claims.

headline: Ted turns 22
summary: Roosevelt shoots a cow elephant. Ted marks his 22nd birthday, still at work for the Hartford Carpet Company in Connecticut.

headline: Into Meru
summary: Roosevelt goes to Meru.

headline: To Lake Ingunga
summary: The safari moves on to Lake Ingunga.

headline: Rhino and elephant
summary: Roosevelt and Kermit kill a rhino and an elephant.

headline: A blank page
summary: Roosevelt leaves his diary blank for the day.

headline: Back to Meru
summary: Roosevelt returns to Meru.

headline: Sunday writing
summary: Roosevelt writes at Meru Boma.

headline: Outfitting the next safari
summary: Roosevelt spends the day organizing the safari for the next leg.

headline: The party splits up
summary: Kermit and Tarlton head southwest for Lake Hannington while Roosevelt and Cunninghame make for the Guaso Nyero. An ailing Heller takes skins to Nairobi by donkey. Roosevelt shoots a crane in flight, and camp sits by a palm-lined brook full of monkeys.

headline: Congratulations for Peary
summary: Roosevelt and Cunninghame reach a branch of the Guaso Nyero and settle in for several days of hunting on the plains. He shoots a big oryx and writes Herbert Bridgman to pass his congratulations to Peary.

headline: A dreadful miss
summary: Roosevelt flubs a shot at an ostrich and spends a beltful of cartridges on one distant oryx, plus two gazelles.

headline: Ostrich, oryx and zebra
summary: Roosevelt gets a hen ostrich, a bull oryx and a big zebra, and writes notes on the ostrich.

headline: The cock ostrich escapes again
summary: Roosevelt misses a cock ostrich a second time, but takes an oryx and a zebra and runs down another zebra on horseback.

headline: The ostrich at last
summary: Roosevelt finally gets his cock ostrich, and a giraffe after a gallop.

headline: Guinea fowl, impala and oryx
summary: The bag includes two guinea fowl, an impala buck and a bull oryx, at the cost of another beltful of cartridges.

headline: Camp by an abandoned boma
summary: The party moves to the Guaso Nyero close to the empty boma of Nyama Yango; Roosevelt shoots a waterbuck bull in the evening.

headline: A serumik
summary: Roosevelt shoots a serumik at 90 yards.

headline: African Game Trails goes to press
summary: Roosevelt kills another serumik and a buffalo cow, while Kermit hunts sable antelope alone. Roosevelt's African Game Trails begins appearing in serial form.

headline: Nothing shot, pages written
summary: Roosevelt comes back empty-handed from a hunt and spends time writing.

headline: Trekking the Guaso Nyero
summary: The safari travels along the river, and Roosevelt shoots a young impala ram.

headline: Upriver, a waterbuck
summary: Moving farther up the river, Roosevelt drops a waterbuck at 120 yards.

headline: A buffalo lost
summary: Roosevelt scolds himself for losing a wounded buffalo bull, but takes two gazelle bucks.

headline: On to Mamba camp
summary: The party pushes upriver to Mamba camp, and Roosevelt shoots two kongoni.

headline: "An elderly man," he tells Arthur Lee
summary: Roosevelt shoots five zebra to feed the porters. He writes Arthur Lee that the African settlers recall America's Western pioneers and that he has ideas on colonial rule to share, and tells Cecil Spring-Rice he hopes to see him in May.

headline: Gazelle, oryx and giraffe
summary: Roosevelt's bag runs to two gazelle, an oryx and a giraffe bull.

headline: Edith witnesses a deed in Italy
summary: Roosevelt writes in camp. Edith and Ethel come back to Porto Maurizio from a tour of Switzerland and northern Italy and serve as official witnesses when Edith's sister Emily Carow signs the deeds to her villa.

headline: Lions in the morning
summary: After lions in the morning, camp moves three hours farther up the Guaso Nyero; Roosevelt notes a monkey.

headline: Kermit turns 20
summary: Roosevelt marches to a waterhole in a gorge and shoots a bull oryx. Kermit, hunting antelope on his own elsewhere, celebrates his 20th birthday.

headline: A crescent moon at sunrise
summary: Roosevelt takes a big gazelle buck, then hits a running oryx too far back, and notes a crescent moon hanging over the sunrise. In America, Eleanor Roosevelt turns 25.

headline: Waterbuck and eland
summary: Among the day's game are a waterbuck and an eland, which Roosevelt sketches in his diary.

headline: Cowboy memories on the downs
summary: A long trek over high rolling downs brings the party back to the marsh where Roosevelt killed an eland in August. Cutting an eland from the herd puts him in mind of his ranching days.

headline: Toward Nyeri
summary: The safari turns toward Nyeri.

headline: Chapters for Scribner's
summary: Reaching Nyeri on the way to Nairobi, Roosevelt mails Robert Bridges chapters nine and ten of African Game Trails and discusses plans for the series and the book.

headline: Comforting Corinne
summary: At Nyeri, Roosevelt tells Charles Walcott that Carnegie has sent $20,000 more, thanks Carnegie and weighs his idea of getting the Kaiser into a world peace council, and writes to console Corinne, traveling the world with Douglas after their son Stewart's death.

headline: "Cook...is a fake"
summary: At the foot of the Aberdares, with a month's mail just in and his ink and paper used up, Roosevelt writes Bamie. He is stunned by the death of Lodge's son Bay, yet holds that death should not be mourned, and weighs in on the polar dispute.

headline: Across the plateau
summary: The safari reaches the middle of the plateau. Back home, Sheffield Cowles turns 11.

headline: Down the escarpment
summary: The party camps an hour past the bottom of the Aberdare escarpment.

headline: Back at Naivasha
summary: The safari arrives at Lake Naivasha.

headline: Reunited in Nairobi
summary: The whole expedition, Kermit included, regroups in Nairobi. Roosevelt writes Lawrence Abbott about Eliot's list of best books, Russia, and Tolstoy, whom he condemns.

headline: Dinner at the Hobleys'
summary: Roosevelt dines with the Hobleys in Nairobi.

headline: Dinner at Nanderman's
summary: Roosevelt is a dinner guest at Nanderman's.

headline: Lunch with Loran, dinner with Jackson
summary: Roosevelt lunches with Loran and dines with Frederick Jackson.

headline: Off to the Uasin Gishu
summary: Roosevelt, Tarlton, Kermit and Heller leave the Londiani railhead, aiming for the Nzoia River on the Uasin Gishu plateau.

headline: First camp out of Londiani
summary: The safari makes camp five miles beyond Londiani.

headline: A 51st birthday on the march
summary: Roosevelt turns 51 marching hard across rolling hills, with no time to hunt. The party crosses the equator again into cold nights, and he likens the country to Oregon and northern California.

headline: Twelve miles past the ravine
summary: Camp is twelve miles beyond the ravine.

headline: A Defassa waterbuck
summary: Roosevelt hunts and gets a young Defassa waterbuck bull at 125 yards.

headline: A blank day
summary: Nothing noted in Roosevelt's diary.

headline: A ten-hour march
summary: Roosevelt marches ten hours and shoots a duiker. Edith and Ethel travel on to Florence, Siena and Rome, and another installment of African Game Trails comes out.

headline: Death of a Roosevelt baby
summary: After a seven-hour march Roosevelt shoots two Jackson's hartebeest bulls but runs short of ammunition while after oribi. In the United States, Franklin and Eleanor's infant son Franklin Jr. dies at seven months.

headline: Hunting through Election Day
summary: As Americans vote, Roosevelt hunts all day and brings in three oribi and a reedbuck.

headline: To Sergoi Lake
summary: The party reaches Sergoi Lake, where Roosevelt records notes on animals.

headline: A running hyena
summary: Camp moves again, and Roosevelt shoots a hyena on the run at 70 yards.

headline: Kermit's giraffe
summary: Kermit gets a bull giraffe and Roosevelt a kongoni at 150 yards.

headline: Rumors of his death
summary: Roosevelt drops a running oribi but misses kongoni after kongoni. In Rome a false report spreads that he has been killed; friends in Nairobi cable a denial, but Edith is shaken.

headline: Hartebeest, oribi and hyena
summary: A day's hunting yields two hartebeest, an oribi and a hyena.

headline: Camp at a swamp spring
summary: The safari marches to a spring in a swamp, and Roosevelt shoots a running warthog.

headline: At the Nzoia River
summary: Reaching the Nzoia River, Roosevelt shoots two kob.

headline: Waterbuck, hartebeest, kob
summary: Roosevelt brings in a waterbuck bull, a big hartebeest bull and a young kob.

headline: Kob in the tall grass
summary: Roosevelt shoots two kob in very high grass.

headline: "Sweetest of all sweet girls"
summary: Roosevelt shoots two bushbuck and Kermit a leopard, as Edith and Ethel sail for New York. He sends Christmas letters to Loeb, boasting that Kermit now outshoots him, and to Ethel and the boys, and writes Edith of a dream.

headline: Meat for the porters
summary: The safari halts so the men can eat well, and Roosevelt shoots a dozen antelope for them.

headline: Carl Akeley arrives
summary: Camped beside the swamps, the party is joined by naturalist Carl Akeley.

headline: Elephants with Akeley
summary: Out with Akeley, Roosevelt kills three elephants, and Kermit one more.

headline: Back to the swamp camp
summary: The hunters return to the swamp camp; Roosevelt writes up the animals.

headline: Everyone hunts for the pot
summary: Camp moves to a valley, and all hands shoot meat for the safari: topi, kongoni and oribi.

headline: Return to Sergoi Lake
summary: The safari goes back to Sergoi Lake.

headline: Lion hunting with the Nandi
summary: Roosevelt joins Nandi warriors on a lion hunt that comes up empty. Quentin turns 12 at school in Groton.

headline: Nandi spearmen kill a lion
summary: The Nandi warriors kill a lion.

headline: To Impey's
summary: The safari marches to Impey's place.

headline: Into Nandi country
summary: Roosevelt reaches a government post in Nandi country and writes Oscar Straus hoping to meet near Turkey or Greece in March. In Washington, Alice turns up to watch a house fire on H Street.

headline: Edith home in New York
summary: Roosevelt and the porters beat a swamp; he misses a lion but gets a hyena and reedbuck. Edith and Ethel land in New York, and Archie Butt sends Edith a White House bloom.

headline: Another swamp drive
summary: A second drive through the swamp turns up nothing but meat for the porters.

headline: Thanksgiving on the plateau
summary: Roosevelt moves camp and shoots a reedbuck on Thanksgiving, which is also Bamie's 14th wedding anniversary.

headline: By the juniper forest
summary: The party returns to its former camp on the Londiani road, on the fringe of the juniper forest.

headline: Bound for Lord Delamere's
summary: Roosevelt marches to a stream in the juniper belt, now heading for Lord Delamere's ranch.

headline: "Back from Elba"
summary: Roosevelt reaches Little Lake and shoots three roan antelope. Edith writes Kermit that America is wild about his father, that Taft is having a hard time, and that New York newspapermen have formed a club toasting TR's return.

headline: Through the rain to Kongoni
summary: The safari slogs through rain to Kongoni camp.

headline: Farewell to the safari
summary: Roosevelt reaches Londiani and goes on to Delamere's, bidding the safari goodbye. Another African Game Trails installment appears.

headline: Guest of Lord Delamere
summary: Roosevelt settles in with Lord Delamere at his Soysambu ranch, farmland where the Mau escarpment begins, and camps in the forested foothills.

headline: An anniversary far from Edith
summary: Roosevelt and Edith's 23rd wedding anniversary passes with a bongo hunt that finds nothing and an evening of stories. He writes Lawrence Abbott about the dispute over his role at San Juan Hill.

headline: Colobus monkeys in the treetops
summary: Roosevelt shoots two colobus monkeys. He reports on Smithsonian specimens to Charles Walcott, and tells Ethel he is sorry Edith heard the death rumors and that Kermit is after bongo with Lady Delamere's brother.

headline: Back to Delamere's
summary: Roosevelt returns to Lord Delamere's.

headline: Corinne's daughter marries Joseph Alsop
summary: Roosevelt shoots two more colobus. At home his niece Corinne Robinson weds Joseph Alsop; the couple will farm tobacco in the Connecticut Valley and raise sons who become columnists.

headline: Edith worries about Quentin
summary: Roosevelt camps in the forest. Edith writes Kermit that Quentin is a handful, always busy and on first-name terms with every tough in town.

headline: Empty-handed
summary: Roosevelt hunts without result.

headline: Sagamore Hill reopens
summary: Another fruitless hunt. At home, Sagamore Hill's guest book records the house opened up again.

headline: Harriman dies
summary: Roosevelt shoots a colobus. William Phillips signs the Sagamore Hill guest book, and railroad magnate E. H. Harriman dies.

headline: Praise for William Allen White's novel
summary: Roosevelt returns to Delamere's and writes William Allen White that he enjoyed his first novel.

headline: Packing up for Uganda
summary: Back in Nairobi, the naturalists, Cunninghame and Tarlton ready the Uganda leg and start shipping specimens home. New books arrive for the Pigskin Library. Warrington Dawson and Eleanor Alexander, Ted's future wife, visit Sagamore Hill.

headline: Moving up the Khartoum reunion
summary: Roosevelt dines with the governor. Worried that Edith is fretting over him, he tells Ethel he will reach Khartoum, and Edith, earlier, by March 15.

headline: Dinner with Watts
summary: Roosevelt dines with Watts in Nairobi.

headline: Thinking about home and Taft
summary: Roosevelt dines with Milne. He writes Carnegie again about a peace league with the Kaiser's help, and tells Henry Beach Needham his thoughts on returning home and on Taft's presidency.

headline: Lunch with Sanderson, dinner with Tarlton
summary: Roosevelt lunches with Sanderson and dines with Leslie Tarlton.

headline: A Badelu lunch
summary: Roosevelt's diary notes a lunch with Badelu.

headline: Nairobi says goodbye
summary: A farewell lunch and dinner close Roosevelt's time in Nairobi. He writes Bamie about the Alsop wedding and his longing to see everyone, and Bridges about a photo of a hyena inside an elephant and Helen Sanderson's African stories.

headline: Leaving for Uganda
summary: Roosevelt sets off for Lake Victoria and Uganda, and members of Nairobi's American mission come to the station to see the party off.

headline: Steaming across Lake Victoria
summary: From Port Florence in Kavirondo country, the party boards a lake steamer for Entebbe, recrossing the equator. Sagamore Hill's guest book fills with visitors including Hamilton Fish Jr.

headline: Arrival at Entebbe
summary: After a day on the water the party lands at Entebbe, near an outbreak of sleeping sickness. They stay with Acting Governor Boyle, and Roosevelt tours missions.

headline: Meeting the boy king of Buganda
summary: In Kampala Roosevelt stays with District Commissioner Knowles, is welcomed by Bishop Alfred Tucker at the Anglican mission, calls on King Daudi Chwa and visits King Mutesa's grave.

headline: Kermit's sitatunga
summary: On a sitatunga hunt near Kampala, Kermit gets one.

headline: Missing home
summary: Roosevelt hunts leopard as the safari moves out, and writes Ethel that he misses home, above all her and her mother.

headline: Catching up with the safari
summary: Roosevelt overtakes the safari on the trail into Uganda. At Sagamore Hill, his November letters arrive, and Helen Leigh Hunt and Alice and Nick Longworth sign the guest book.

headline: Christmas on the march
summary: Roosevelt spends Christmas Day marching with the safari and sends Helen Sanderson holiday greetings and news of the trip.

headline: Remington dies
summary: Roosevelt marches on and shoots a bushbuck. In the United States, artist Frederic Remington dies after his appendix ruptures.

headline: Three reedbuck
summary: Another day's march, with three reedbuck among the animals Roosevelt shoots.

headline: A giant bull elephant
summary: Rain delays the start, but the party makes a long march and camps by mid-afternoon. Afterward Roosevelt and Kermit bring down a huge bull elephant standing 10 feet 9 inches.

headline: Taking the tusks
summary: The tusks are cut from the elephant, and Roosevelt writes in camp.

headline: A Uganda hartebeest
summary: On the march, Roosevelt kills a Uganda hartebeest bull at 80 yards.

headline: Guinea fowl to close the year
summary: Roosevelt ends 1909 marching and shooting two guinea fowl. Isabella Hagner is a guest at Sagamore Hill, and African Game Trails continues as a serial.

headline: Nineteen miles on New Year's Day
summary: Roosevelt opens 1910 with a 19-mile march through Uganda.

headline: On to Hoima
summary: The safari heads for Hoima.

headline: A day at Hoima
summary: Roosevelt stays at Hoima. Barclay H. Farr signs the Sagamore Hill guest book.

headline: Receiving the King of Bunyoro
summary: At Hoima, Roosevelt receives the king of Bunyoro before the safari moves on.

headline: Camp on Lake Albert's beach
summary: By midday the party is at Butiaba on Lake Albert, about 160 miles from Lake Victoria, and pitches camp on the sand. From here boats run down toward the Nile.

headline: Waiting at Butiaba
summary: Roosevelt spends the day at Butiaba. Warrington Dawson is again a guest at Sagamore Hill.

headline: Taft fires Pinchot
summary: Roosevelt travels by boat to Koba. In Washington, President Taft dismisses Gifford Pinchot, and Edith writes Kermit that the Ballinger-Pinchot inquiry leaves Taft in a hard spot and that she pities him.

headline: Down the Nile past Wadelai
summary: The boat carries Roosevelt past Wadelai. Five visitors sign the Sagamore Hill guest book, among them Evelyn Irving and Helene Coster.

headline: Into the Lado
summary: The party makes camp in the Lado Enclave.

headline: White rhino cow and calf
summary: Roosevelt shoots a white rhino cow and calf at 60 yards, sketching where each bullet struck.

headline: Fighting a grass fire
summary: Roosevelt shoots two oribi, then helps battle a fire in the evening.

headline: Women smoke at the White House
summary: Rhino skins are carried into camp. In Washington, women light up at a public White House event for the first time, and Archie Butt shares stories about Alice.

headline: Kermit's bull rhino
summary: Kermit kills a bull rhino and Roosevelt a waterbuck bull.

headline: Two kob
summary: Roosevelt shoots two kob at 90 and 180 yards.

headline: Nothing to show
summary: A hunt turns up nothing. Woodrow Creen, David Paton and Cornelia Landon visit Sagamore Hill.

headline: A pair of white rhinos
summary: Roosevelt shoots a white rhino bull and cow, and a hippo nearly blunders into camp.

headline: "I cannot believe it"
summary: A runner brings word that Gifford Pinchot has been removed, and Roosevelt writes him in disbelief, praising his public service. He tells Lodge about the hunt, evening mosquitoes and Kermit's skill, hoping the Pinchot news is false.

headline: Bamie turns 55
summary: Roosevelt shoots oribi, hartebeest, kob and a guinea hen. Bamie marks her 55th birthday, and Warrington Dawson visits Sagamore Hill again.

headline: Kermit's cow rhino
summary: Kermit kills a cow rhino. Teresa Richardson is a guest at Sagamore Hill.

headline: A crocodile and more
summary: Roosevelt's bag includes a crocodile, a kob, a hartebeest, a bustard and a bushbuck ram. Binks signs the Sagamore Hill guest book.

headline: "A complete success"
summary: Roosevelt shoots two oribi. He writes Bamie that the United Press reports Pinchot's dismissal, which he still can't credit, and tells Corinne the expedition has been everything he hoped.

headline: Rhino meat is good
summary: Roosevelt writes, notes that the local bushbuck differ from East African ones, and approves of rhino meat.

headline: Midday heat in the tropics
summary: The party marches to Sukuni village in the scorching January noon, two to three degrees from the equator.

headline: Lily pond camp
summary: At a camp beside a lily pond, Roosevelt shoots two waterbuck.

headline: Nine rhinos in a day
summary: Roosevelt sees nine rhinos and shoots a duiker. In New York, panic hits Wall Street.

headline: Back to the village
summary: The party returns to the village.

headline: A buffalo bull
summary: Roosevelt shoots a buffalo bull at 80 yards.

headline: Ethel visits Washington
summary: Camp moves to the river, and Roosevelt shoots a cow rhino. Ethel arrives in Washington to stay with the McLeans.

headline: Writing day
summary: Roosevelt writes in camp.

headline: Boating with Loring
summary: Roosevelt goes out in a boat with J. Alden Loring.

headline: Writing as the serial runs
summary: Roosevelt spends the day writing while African Game Trails continues in serial form.

headline: A young bushbuck from the boat
summary: Roosevelt hunts from a boat in the Lado Enclave and brings down a young bushbuck at about sixty yards, sketching the shot in his diary.

headline: Bushbuck, hartebeest and kob
summary: A full day of shooting in the Lado Enclave: Roosevelt logs a bushbuck ram, several hartebeest and a kob, with the range of each shot and sketches beside them.

headline: Setting out for Nimule
summary: Roosevelt's party begins the trip to Nimule. Back home in Washington, Archie Butt gives a luncheon at the house of Roosevelt's daughter Alice.

headline: Arrival at Nimule
summary: The safari reaches Nimule on the upper Nile.

headline: Writing Lodge from Nimule
summary: Halted at Nimule, Roosevelt writes Henry Cabot Lodge, admiring the late poetry of Lodge's son Bay, reporting illness among the men, and worrying over Justice William Moody's health.

headline: A day at Nimule
summary: Roosevelt stays put at Nimule.

headline: First march toward Gondokoro
summary: The overland march to Gondokoro begins. That night the party camps beside a shallow, palm-lined river.

headline: Camp beside an anthill
summary: Walking rather than riding, Roosevelt marches on and camps beneath two leafy trees by an anthill, with water a mile away among the bamboos.

headline: Camp near an old smithy
summary: Another day's march ends in camp beneath three big trees, close to the remains of a native blacksmith's forge.

headline: Up at 2:45 for the march
summary: The whistle sounds before three in the morning. After the march the party camps past a dry riverbed, near a pool.

headline: Early camp by a creek
summary: The safari stops early, pitching camp beside a creek among trees.

headline: Rest day hunt on the march
summary: The column halts for a day and Roosevelt hunts, taking an oribi, a reedbuck and a red baboon. At home, his daughter Alice turns 26.

headline: Camp under a big tree
summary: An early start, and camp that night beneath one large tree.

headline: Camp near a rocky hill
summary: The party marches early and camps near a village and a rocky hill. Roosevelt shoots an oribi at 100 yards.

headline: Eighteen miles at 112 degrees
summary: A brutal eighteen-mile march in shade temperatures of 112 degrees leaves the porters spent. Roosevelt kills a hartebeest at 80 yards.

headline: Hoping for elephant
summary: Roosevelt expects elephant, but none turn up.

headline: The safari reaches Gondokoro
summary: The march ends at Gondokoro. At home, Alice and Nick Longworth mark four years of marriage.

headline: Toward Redjaf in the heat
summary: From Gondokoro the party heads for Redjaf, moving at night and in the early hours and shooting game to eat in the dry country. Roosevelt writes Andrew Carnegie about Europe, the Kaiser, and his longing for Edith and Sagamore Hill.

headline: After the giant eland
summary: Roosevelt and Kermit go from Redjaf on an eight-day side trip into the Congo after giant eland, heading for the Kabo River.

headline: Camp near the Koda River
summary: The eland hunters camp about two hours short of the Koda River, near a hill.

headline: Fourteen hours in the field
summary: Roosevelt spends fourteen hours out hunting and takes one hartebeest.

headline: Roan, but still no eland
summary: Another thirteen-hour day. Roosevelt finds roan antelope and records one shot the day before.

headline: The giant eland bull at last
summary: After eleven hours out, Roosevelt brings down a bull giant eland at 120 yards, the trophy he came for, and records its measurements.

headline: Curing the eland skins
summary: The day goes to preparing the skins. Roosevelt also shoots an oribi at 60 yards.

headline: Seventeen miles back toward Redjaf
summary: The hunters turn back, covering seventeen miles toward Redjaf with an afternoon march along the dry Kabo River.

headline: Back to Gondokoro
summary: Roosevelt passes through Redjaf and returns to Gondokoro.

headline: The Sirdar's boat arrives
summary: At Gondokoro, Roosevelt meets the steamer that General Reginald Wingate has sent to carry the party down the Nile to Khartoum, and writes Archie about it. A Scottish engineer, Captain Middleton, commands.

headline: Downriver on the Dal
summary: The party boards the steamer Dal and starts down the Nile. Roosevelt notices the swift current and the walls of reeds, marsh grass and papyrus, passing Lado and Mongalla.

headline: The safari by the numbers
summary: A tally of the African year: Roosevelt has taken 296 animals and Kermit more than 200, including nine lions and eight elephants for Roosevelt. He was ill only five days. Ted is now engaged to Eleanor Alexander, and Americans are starting to look ahead to Roosevelt's homecoming.

headline: Stunned by news of Pinchot
summary: Steaming down the Nile to Bor, Roosevelt writes Gifford Pinchot of his shock at Pinchot's dismissal, and tells Lodge about it along with his European plans and the giant eland hunt.

headline: Dinner at Mongalla, then the Sudd
summary: The steamer stops at Lado, and at Mongalla the party has dinner with Colonel Owen, who runs the southern Sudan, before pushing into the great Sudd swamps toward Lake No.

headline: A tramp on the shores of Lake No
summary: While the boat creeps along Lake No, Roosevelt walks five hours with Cuninghame and spots kob. He tells Lodge he will stay silent on politics at home, and touches on Bay Lodge and Taft's renomination.

headline: Waterfowl in the great marsh
summary: Near the mouth of the Bahr el Ghazal, Roosevelt shoots a white-eared kob and takes in the vast marshes and their crowds of water birds.

headline: On the Bahr el Ghazal
summary: The steamer travels the Bahr el Ghazal.

headline: A shoebill on the White Nile
summary: From the Bahr el Ghazal and Lake No the boat moves on toward the Bahr el Zeraf and the White Nile. Roosevelt shoots a shoebill stork and more kob.

headline: Three kob on the Zeraf
summary: On the Bahr el Zeraf, Roosevelt shoots three kob at long range, between 230 and 280 yards.

headline: Meat for the mission at Taufikia
summary: The boat reaches a mission where the Sobat joins the Nile, near Taufikia, where Roosevelt shoots a waterbuck cow to feed the local people.

headline: Letters while passing Kodok
summary: Passing Kodok, Roosevelt catches up on mail: praise for William Loeb's customs work, a blessing on the match of Joe Alsop and his niece Corinne, the Standard Oil breakup case for Frank Kellogg, and English plans for Arthur Lee.

headline: Reporters come up the river
summary: Newspapermen have hired boats to meet Roosevelt upstream, and he gives his first press interview in a year. He talks freely about the expedition but refuses every question on politics at home.

headline: Heading north
summary: The steamer keeps on downstream.

headline: Still northward
summary: Another day on the river.

headline: Reunion with Edith at Khartoum
summary: At Khartoum, Slatin Pasha greets the party and Governor General Wingate hosts them. Edith and Ethel are waiting for Roosevelt and Kermit after a year apart. Lawrence Abbott arrives too and offers to serve as secretary in Europe.

headline: Speaking at Gordon College
summary: Roosevelt drafts the foreword and appendices for African Game Trails, tours the old battlefield at Kerreri, speaks at Gordon Memorial College, and dines at the Sirdar's palace.

headline: Two speeches in Khartoum
summary: The family tours Khartoum and Omdurman. Roosevelt speaks at the Government School and then at the American mission, where he talks about fairness and order under Sudanese rule, before dinner at the Sudan Club.

headline: Night train out of Khartoum
summary: After lunch at the palace, a mission visit, a hotel reception and a talk to Egyptian officers, the family boards the night train north. Roosevelt welcomes Eleanor Alexander into the family in a warm letter.

headline: Boarding the Ibis at Wadi Halfa
summary: The train reaches Wadi Halfa at nine at night, and the party transfers to the steamer Ibis for the Nile run toward Cairo. Roosevelt and Edith send Corinne the news.

headline: The temples at Abu Simbel
summary: The party stops to see Rameses II's temples at Abu Simbel. Swamped with mail despite two volunteer secretaries, Roosevelt writes Bamie, who is ill, and William Loeb about his New York homecoming.

headline: Philae and the Aswan Dam
summary: From Shellal the party explores ruined Philae, inspects the Aswan Dam, and visits the hillside tombs at Mount Grenfell.

headline: Karnak by night
summary: Leaving Aswan, the party reaches Luxor for a welcome at the Winter Palace Hotel and an evening at Karnak. Roosevelt writes Ted a glowing letter about Eleanor. At home, Alice's grandfather George Cabot Lee dies.

headline: Tombs of Thebes
summary: Roosevelt tours the temples and tombs of Thebes, speaks at the American Mission, and lunches with Weigall.

headline: Luxor and Karnak temples
summary: A day among the ancient temples at Luxor and Karnak, with a call at the United Presbyterian mission.

headline: Moonlight at the pyramids
summary: Arriving in Cairo, Roosevelt is greeted by Major Stack and the U.S. consul-general and exchanges calls with the Khedive. That night he sleeps out by the pyramids at the Mena House. He insists by letter that Edith be with him in Berlin.

headline: No strings on a papal audience
summary: After touring the tombs at Sakkara, Roosevelt catches up with Oscar Straus, who has traveled from Constantinople to see him. He cables Ambassador Leishman that he will accept no conditions on whom he visits in Rome, after the Vatican objected to his planned Methodist call.

headline: At Al-Azhar University
summary: Roosevelt visits Al-Azhar University and that evening dines at the American Agency, where a reception follows. He writes Selous to arrange a visit in London.

headline: Easter in Cairo
summary: On Easter Sunday Roosevelt receives a delegation of Coptic, Muslim and Egyptian journalists, and dines with Wingate.

headline: A Cairo speech stirs protest
summary: Roosevelt addresses Cairo's National University on keeping order under the law in Egypt, and students march against what he said. He also receives Syrian visitors, calls at the American mission, and promises Lodge to stay apart from politics when he returns.

headline: The papal audience falls through
summary: Students protest again. Roosevelt lunches with Hatzfeldt and cables Leishman that, given the Vatican's condition that he skip the Methodists, an audience with the Pope is now out of the question.

headline: Sailing for Naples
summary: The Roosevelts leave Cairo for Alexandria and sail for Naples aboard the Prinz Heinrich, a ship they find dirty and uncomfortable.

headline: Crossing the Mediterranean
summary: At sea. The European tour party is Roosevelt, Edith, Kermit and Ethel, with a valet and a maid, plus three secretaries, Frank Harper, Lawrence Abbott and John Callan O'Laughlin.

headline: At sea toward Italy
summary: A quiet day aboard ship on the way to Naples.

headline: Mobbed with welcome in Naples
summary: Roosevelt lands at Naples to a reception so huge it embarrasses him. The family spends the evening at the opera, and he writes Henry White about British rule in Egypt.

headline: Explaining the Vatican affair
summary: Roosevelt arrives in Rome and dines at the embassy, and Edith's sister Emily Carow joins the family. He writes Lyman Abbott a letter, later printed in The Outlook, explaining his stand with the Vatican and denying any hostility to Catholics.

headline: Received by the King of Italy
summary: King Victor Emmanuel III receives Roosevelt. He sees the Pantheon, lunches with Ambassador Leishman, receives the Methodist B. M. Tipple among other callers, and attends a state dinner at the Quirinal.

headline: The day meant for the Pope
summary: Roosevelt's diary still marks the papal audience that was canceled. Instead he rides out with the King to see the Royal Bodyguard of Cuirassiers, goes sightseeing, and dines with Edith at the British Embassy while the young people visit Pisa.

headline: A second honeymoon begins
summary: After calls on Professor Boni and lunch with Ferrero, and a city dinner at the Capitoline, Roosevelt and Edith slip away toward Spezia by carriage, just as they traveled on their honeymoon 23 years earlier. He writes Lodge about the papal muddle.

headline: Waves under the balcony
summary: Roosevelt and Edith take a carriage over the mountains from Spezia to Sestri Levante, lodging in an old hotel where they lie listening to the sea against the walls below.

headline: Serenaded at Sestri Levante
summary: Town officials call, and a band plays for the couple, badly. Then they drive on to Chiavari past crowds lining the road.

headline: Rejoining the family in Genoa
summary: Roosevelt sees Chiavari and meets Catholic students, then he and Edith meet up with the rest of the family in Genoa. Archie turns 16 at Groton. The Outlook prints Roosevelt's statement on the papal audience.

headline: Flowers at Porto Maurizio
summary: Porto Maurizio makes Roosevelt an honorary citizen, names a boulevard for him, and pelts his carriage with flowers. He and Edith settle into a house near Emily's and lunch with the novelist Fogazzaro.

headline: Pinchot brings his side
summary: Gifford Pinchot spends nearly the whole day with Roosevelt, recounting his fight with Ballinger and his firing by Taft and showing a stack of anti-Taft letters. Roosevelt writes Lodge that the Taft leadership has misread the country.

headline: Resting at Porto Maurizio
summary: Roosevelt stays on at Porto Maurizio.

headline: The family splits up
summary: After meeting with Phelan, Roosevelt leaves Genoa with Kermit for a fast swing through Vienna and Budapest, while Edith and Ethel head to Paris to stay with Ambassador Robert Bacon.

headline: A day in Venice
summary: Roosevelt and Kermit see the sights of Venice and take an evening train for Vienna.

headline: Audience with Emperor Franz Joseph
summary: Roosevelt arrives in Vienna, calls on Henry White, Count Aehrenthal and Archduke Franz Ferdinand, and is received by Emperor Franz Joseph. He tours the famous riding school and the Hussar barracks and dines with Aehrenthal.

headline: Kreuzenstein Castle
summary: Roosevelt and Kermit visit Count Wilczek at Kreuzenstein Castle. Roosevelt receives the papal nuncio and attends an official dinner at Schönbrunn. The Outlook runs his Sudan speech.

headline: On to Hungary
summary: Bound for Budapest, Roosevelt stops to visit Count Apponyi at Eberhart.

headline: Budapest's welcome
summary: In Budapest Roosevelt pays a call at the Royal Palace, gets a formal welcome at Parliament, visits Kossuth, lunches with Archduke Joseph, and dines with Baron Hengelmüller. In Paris, Edith tells Corinne she dislikes the political picture at home more each day.

headline: Horses at Bábolna
summary: Roosevelt tours the government stud farm at Bábolna and attends a Foreign Office dinner and reception before a midnight train out of Budapest.

headline: Overnight to Paris
summary: Roosevelt and Kermit board the train in Budapest at one in the morning and travel to Paris.

headline: Paris and the family again
summary: Arriving at 7:30 a.m., Roosevelt and Kermit rejoin Edith and Ethel. He calls on President Fallières and former President Loubet, and the family goes to the Comédie-Française.

headline: At Napoleon's tomb
summary: Roosevelt visits Napoleon's tomb with French generals, Ambassador Bacon and Jusserand, lunches with Baron de Coubertin, and dines with the family at the Élysée as President Fallières's guest.

headline: Citizenship in a Republic
summary: At the Sorbonne, Roosevelt gives his address on citizenship in a republic, urging character over cleverness or wealth and taking aim at the Socialists. Earlier he takes part in a meeting of the moral and political sciences academy of the Institut. Film catches him leaving.

headline: Château at Saint-Germain
summary: Roosevelt visits the château at Saint-Germain and lunches with Jusserand, who crossed to France to greet him. A film camera records the day.

headline: Paris City Hall and Edith Wharton
summary: The city of Paris welcomes Roosevelt at the Hôtel de Ville. He calls on Edith Wharton and has dinner with Rochambeau Mission officers at the Military Club. At home, Taft picks Governor Charles Evans Hughes for a Supreme Court seat.

headline: Delegations and the Bacons
summary: More sightseeing. Roosevelt receives two delegations, one from France's Interparliamentary Union and one a Franco-American committee, then dines with Ambassador and Mrs. Bacon.

headline: Rodin's studio and Versailles
summary: A full day: the Vincennes garrison, the Salon, Rodin's studio and Versailles, then dinner at the Foreign Ministry. Roosevelt asks Root for his view of Taft and writes Lodge about his future.

headline: A night at Laeken Palace
summary: Leaving Paris for Brussels, the Roosevelts lunch at the American legation, are welcomed at the town hall, and dine with the King and Queen of the Belgians at Laeken, where the family spends the night.

headline: An unloved queen at Het Loo
summary: The family lunches with Queen Wilhelmina at Het Loo, and neither Roosevelt nor Edith warms to her. In Amsterdam the burgomaster welcomes them, Roosevelt attends a meeting at the Free Church, and the city gives a dinner. Corinne's wedding anniversary falls today.

headline: Delft and the House in the Woods
summary: In Holland, Roosevelt visits the royal House in the Woods, is received by Queen Mother Emma, tours Delft, and attends an embassy dinner. The Outlook prints his Sorbonne speech and "The Pigskin Library." Halley's Comet is in the sky.

headline: Tulips at Haarlem
summary: The Roosevelts leave The Hague for the national tulip show and art gallery at Haarlem. In Amsterdam the burgomaster greets them at the Rijksmuseum, and with their luggage astray they turn up in travel clothes.

headline: Royal guests in Copenhagen
summary: The family reaches Copenhagen in the afternoon and stays at the palace of Denmark's crown prince and princess, Christian and Alexandrine, with a palace dinner and a legation reception. Roosevelt tells Whitelaw Reid he would rather be home at Sagamore Hill.

headline: Hamlet's castle at Elsinore
summary: The family tours Elsinore Castle, caught on film, before a city dinner in Copenhagen. Roosevelt confesses himself puzzled by the crowds that greet him everywhere. That evening they set out for Norway.

headline: Romping with Prince Olav
summary: King Haakon and Queen Maud welcome the Roosevelts to Christiania and put them up at the Royal Palace, where Roosevelt plays happily with little Prince Olav before the state dinner.

headline: The Nobel lecture
summary: Roosevelt finally gives his Nobel address on international peace, proposing that peace-minded powers band together in a league ready to stop others from breaking the peace, by force if need be. Nansen calls. He tells Lodge the party held power only because he kept it moving forward.

headline: A cowboy, not a statue of me
summary: The University in Christiania awards Roosevelt an honorary doctorate, and word comes that Britain's King Edward VII has died. Roosevelt asks Louis Hanna to make North Dakota's planned statue an ordinary cowboy rather than himself, then leaves for Stockholm.

headline: Guests of Sweden's crown prince
summary: In Stockholm the Roosevelts stay with Crown Prince Gustaf Adolf and Crown Princess Margaret, see the city, and attend a dinner given by its citizens. The Outlook prints the Nobel address.

headline: Lunch with Sven Hedin
summary: Roosevelt lunches with Ambassador Graves and the explorer Sven Hedin, receives the crown prince and a delegation of Swedish parliamentarians, and leaves Stockholm in the afternoon.

headline: Into Berlin
summary: The Roosevelts travel south and reach Berlin in the afternoon.

headline: Lunch with the Kaiser at Sanssouci
summary: Staying with the American ambassador, the Roosevelts go to Potsdam for a midday meal with Wilhelm II and the Empress at Sanssouci, where Wilhelm shows Edith the paintings. Roosevelt writes Reid about the King's funeral.

headline: Reviewing troops beside the Kaiser
summary: Though down with bronchitis, Roosevelt rides out with Wilhelm II to review the German army in mock battle at Döberitz. The Kaiser later sends him photos with joking captions his ministers wish he had not. Glacier National Park is created back home.

headline: Lecturing at the University of Berlin
summary: Roosevelt delivers "The World Movement" at the University of Berlin with the Kaiser and Kaiserin in the audience, and accepts an honorary doctorate. He dines with Bethmann-Hollweg. In America, an animated cartoon spoofs his European welcome.

headline: Embassies and parliamentarians
summary: Lunch at the American Embassy, a visit from the German Interparliamentary Union, and dinner at the French Embassy.

headline: The zoo and a cool German welcome
summary: The Roosevelts visit the Berlin zoo, and the wildlife writer Schillings calls. Roosevelt later judged that the Germans liked neither him nor America. The Outlook publishes his Berlin lecture.

headline: Bound for London
summary: Leaving Berlin early, Roosevelt writes Lodge on the trip about the progressive-conservative split in the Republican party, Taft's alliance with the conservatives, Cannon's loss of power, and the public's appetite for real reform.

headline: London in mourning
summary: The Roosevelts reach London and stay with Ambassador Whitelaw Reid. the new King, George V, and his queen receive them, and they pay respects at Edward VII's bier. Visiting royals call, and Alice arrives from America.

headline: A possible Oxford trip
summary: Roosevelt's diary notes a question mark beside a trip to Oxford.

headline: Three kings in one day
summary: Roosevelt has audiences with the Kings of Denmark, Norway and Greece. His old Dakota friend Seth Bullock comes calling.

headline: A banquet of eight monarchs
summary: Roosevelt lunches with Lewis Harcourt, calls on the Kaiser, and sits down at a Buckingham Palace state banquet with eight kings. He found the mourning there brief before the merriment resumed.

headline: America's envoy at the King's funeral
summary: As special ambassador of the United States, Roosevelt attends Edward VII's funeral at St. George's Chapel, Windsor, on a gray, heavy day, amused by the squabbles over precedence and livery. He lunches at Windsor Castle and drives back for an embassy dinner.

headline: Weekend at Wrest Park
summary: The family goes to Wrest Park in Bedfordshire to stay with Whitelaw Reid and his wife.

headline: Family day with the Reids
summary: A family gathering with the Reids at Wrest Park.

headline: Back in London with Arthur Lee
summary: The Roosevelts return to London and settle in at Arthur Lee's Chesterfield Street house. Roosevelt lunches with Lord Lansdowne and sees Andrew Carnegie, and writes Robert Bridges about his book chapters and a bogus safari book.

headline: With the widowed Queen Alexandra
summary: Roosevelt calls on the widowed Queen Alexandra and her sister Marie, Russia's dowager empress; Edith has her own audience. At lunch he joins Owen Seaman, Maxse and Arthur Conan Doyle, and writes Lodge about Calhoun and Manchuria.

headline: Breakfast with Grey, a call from Kipling
summary: Roosevelt breakfasts with Foreign Secretary Sir Edward Grey, tours the zoo with his safari friend Leslie Tarlton and Seth Bullock, and receives Rudyard Kipling and the British Interparliamentary Union.

headline: A teddy bear at Cambridge
summary: Speaking to Cambridge undergraduates, Roosevelt defines success as an honest life that leaves others better off, while students dangle a teddy bear above him. He takes an honorary degree, tours the colleges, and goes on to Arthur Lee's Chequers with Balfour and Lord Roberts among the guests.

headline: Talking with Balfour
summary: At Chequers, Roosevelt and Arthur Balfour hit it off at once and spend the day in lively conversation.

headline: Kitchener comes to lunch
summary: Lord Kitchener joins the Chequers party for lunch. Neither Roosevelt nor Edith cares for him, finding him overbearing and forever striking a strongman's pose.

headline: Back to town
summary: The Roosevelts return from Chequers to London, where Buxton calls. Alice slips over to France and wins enough at the races to pay for the trip.

headline: Root carries word from Taft
summary: Called to the American Embassy, Roosevelt sees Elihu Root, who carries word from President Taft and advises him to say nothing political for sixty days or more after he gets home. He lunches with the Royal Geographical Society and dines with Lord Beresford.

headline: Telling Britain to govern Egypt or leave
summary: Given the freedom of the City of London, Roosevelt uses his Guildhall speech to tell Britain bluntly that it must keep order in Egypt or get out. Spring-Rice and Arthur Lee had looked over the text beforehand. He lunches with the Lord Mayor.

headline: A night with Selous
summary: Roosevelt tours the National Gallery and lunches with Irish Nationalist members of Parliament, then the family goes down to Worplesdon in Surrey to stay with his hunting friend Frederick Selous.

headline: Dinner with Strachey
summary: The Roosevelts come back to London from Worplesdon, and Roosevelt dines with the editor John St. Loe Strachey.

headline: Calling on the Duke of Connaught
summary: Roosevelt pays a visit to the Duke of Connaught and lunches with W. N. McMillan, his host in East Africa. The day ends at Chequers.

headline: Stratford with the Trevelyans
summary: The family stays with the historian George Otto Trevelyan at Stratford-upon-Avon. Roosevelt tells Lodge he has met every leading Briton except Winston Churchill, whom he chose to avoid. The Outlook runs his piece on Black Americans.

headline: At Shakespeare's birthplace
summary: The Roosevelts visit the house where Shakespeare was born. Alice, back from the Derby, spends time at the John Wards' country place. Roosevelt wires Owen Seaman a joking reply to a Punch story about his Latin outburst at Frith's "Derby Day."

headline: Lunch at the palace
summary: Back in London, the Roosevelts are the King and Queen's lunch guests. Roosevelt tells Spring-Rice how much he enjoyed seeing him and his wife.

headline: The Romanes lecture at Oxford
summary: In the Sheldonian Theatre Roosevelt delivers the Romanes lecture, "Biological Analogies in History," and is made an honorary Doctor of Civil Law. The Archbishop of York grades the talk a B-minus and the speaker an A-plus. The family sees Magdalen and spends the night at Lewis Harcourt's Nuneham Park.

headline: Saying nothing to Taft
summary: After a reception at Dorchester House and a farewell dinner, Roosevelt writes President Taft that he is troubled by some of what he hears but has chosen to keep silent. He carries the letter home himself and gives it to Archie Butt.

headline: Birding the Itchen with Edward Grey
summary: Roosevelt and Foreign Secretary Grey meet at Waterloo Station and spend the day walking the Itchen valley and the edge of the New Forest, listening for birds. Reaching Brockenhurst around sundown, they tally 41 species heard in song and 23 more seen.

headline: Homeward from Southampton
summary: The family, with Alice along, sails from Southampton for New York on the Kaiserin Auguste Victoria.

headline: Romanes lecture in print
summary: At sea. The Outlook publishes his Oxford lecture.

headline: Crossing the Atlantic
summary: A day at sea on the voyage home.

headline: Another day at sea
summary: The ship steams west toward New York.

headline: Letters from mid-ocean
summary: Roosevelt writes Governor Hughes asking to talk over the primary fight, and Robert Bridges about a book appendix in which he takes apart theories of protective coloration in animals.

headline: Nearing home
summary: Still at sea.

headline: An invitation from the White House
summary: A letter from President Taft, carried by Archie Butt, waits for Roosevelt: a warm welcome back and a request that he visit the White House, with a matching note from Helen Taft to Edith.

headline: Archie Butt sees Corinne
summary: While the ship is at sea, Archie Butt calls on Roosevelt's sister Corinne and finds her deep in grief.

headline: A hero's welcome in New York
summary: Roosevelt sails into New York to a roaring reception. After a short speech at the Battery he rides in a huge parade up Broadway and Fifth Avenue with 500 Rough Riders, then heads home to Sagamore Hill. A press boat teases his spelling reform with a "Pres Bot" sign.

headline: Forty-two birds at home
summary: From his piazza rocker and then on a walk, Roosevelt counts 42 bird species at Sagamore Hill, one more than on his English walk. In the evening the family goes into the city to stay at Corinne's, where he talks politics with Nick Longworth, Meyer and Lodge.

headline: Ted marries Eleanor Alexander
summary: On a sweltering day, Ted and Eleanor Butler Alexander are married in Fifth Avenue's Presbyterian church, with a Baptist and a Methodist minister reading the Episcopal service. Roosevelt writes Taft that a trip to Washington must wait, and that being invited would not be proper.

headline: Ted and Eleanor go west
summary: The Cowleses and General Wright come by, and the Bishops and LaFarges are guests. The newlyweds set out for San Francisco, where Ted will work for the Hartford Carpet Company.

headline: Mobbed outside Scribner's
summary: A big crowd gathers on Fifth Avenue while Roosevelt meets Scribner's about African Game Trails, and the crush unsettles him. He addresses the Camp Fire Club over lunch, sees visitors including Booker T. Washington at the Outlook office, and dines with Robert Collier.

headline: The Ananias Club has room
summary: Garfield and Pinchot visit Sagamore Hill. In the New York Times, Roosevelt says any New Yorker against direct primaries qualifies for his Ananias Club of liars.

headline: Tennis with Garfield and Pinchot
summary: Roosevelt confers with Garfield and Pinchot and then takes them on at tennis. McCormick calls, and the Heneys, Tarlton, Tritton and Greenaway sign the guest book.

headline: Lunch with Merriam and Stimson
summary: Roosevelt's lunch guests are the naturalist C. Hart Merriam, Henry Stimson and Archbishop Spalding.

headline: Sunday at home
summary: A quiet day at Sagamore Hill.

headline: La Follette comes to talk
summary: Roosevelt confers with Senator La Follette. He tells Governor Hughes he cannot openly side with him against the bosses Barnes and Wadsworth on primaries, and turns down a trade group presidency offered by C. W. Post.

headline: "Taft has passed his nadir"
summary: Roosevelt goes to Cambridge to speak to Harvard Law School alumni. He writes Pinchot that Taft is a man shaped by those around him, who did well under Roosevelt.

headline: Back in the fight for primaries
summary: At Harvard Commencement, Roosevelt and Governor Hughes are so deep in talk they miss the start of the procession. Hughes asks for help with his direct primary bill; Roosevelt agrees, introduces him at lunch, and wires Lloyd Griscom his support, his first public political stand since leaving office. He spends the night with Lodge at Nahant.

headline: A scotch and soda with Taft
summary: Roosevelt and Lodge call on President Taft at his summer place in Beverly. Over a scotch and soda Roosevelt talks about Europe and New York politics, and afterward tells reporters the visit was friendly. He signs on as an Outlook editor at $12,000 a year.

headline: A call on Justice Moody
summary: In Boston, Roosevelt visits his ailing friend William Moody, then heads home to Sagamore Hill. In Albany, the direct primary bill goes down to defeat.

headline: Insurgents at Sagamore
summary: Roosevelt meets with Griscom and the insurgent congressmen Bristow, Murdock and Madison. Three of his pieces run in The Outlook, including one on Hughes and primary reform.

headline: Quiet Sunday
summary: No events recorded at Sagamore Hill.

headline: A full house for the Fourth
summary: Independence Day brings a crowd of guests to Sagamore Hill, among them John Burroughs, the publisher Henry Holt, Lucius Swift and William Dudley Foulke.

headline: Poindexter and the Ballinger fight
summary: Roosevelt meets Representative Miles Poindexter of Washington, and newspapers report he has promised to help fight Ballinger. Bacon and Gardner also call.

headline: Office day and old friends
summary: At The Outlook Roosevelt sees William Loeb and other visitors. Back at Sagamore Hill he talks with John Burroughs, Lucius Swift and William Dudley Foulke.

headline: Beveridge and the Basses
summary: A stream of visitors: Senator Beveridge, Carter, Churchill, the Bass brothers of New Hampshire, Fish, Sheffield, Bacon and Burroughs.

headline: Setting the record straight
summary: Roosevelt denies that he and Miles Poindexter see eye to eye on everything, a claim that had embarrassed Taft. He explains the meeting to Lodge and tells William Barnes Jr. that a New York World interview was fake.

headline: Johnson beats Jeffries
summary: At Reno, Jack Johnson beats Jim Jeffries to keep boxing's heavyweight crown. Roosevelt is at Sagamore Hill.

headline: Sunday guests
summary: Five guests sign the Sagamore Hill book, among them Hamilton Fish Jr. and F. W. Whitridge.

headline: Writing Nick about the tariff
summary: Roosevelt writes his son-in-law Nick Longworth about the Payne-Aldrich tariff, Taft, and the political picture. Marion Oliver is a guest.

headline: Hughes comes to Sagamore
summary: At The Outlook Roosevelt sees Pinchot, Wadsworth, Stimson and others and shares lunch with Reverend Cranston, the Kansas City editor W. R. Nelson and his nephew Douglas Robinson. That evening Governor Hughes confers with him at Sagamore Hill.

headline: Riis among the callers
summary: Jacob Riis, Charles N. Fowler and others call at Sagamore Hill, and Roosevelt's nephew Theodore Douglas Robinson is a guest.

headline: At home
summary: Nothing is recorded for the day at Sagamore Hill.

headline: Back at the Natural History Museum
summary: Roosevelt confers with Herbert Parsons and Wainwright at The Outlook, sees other callers, and stops in at the natural history museum on Central Park West.

headline: Writing on the big fight
summary: The Outlook publishes Roosevelt's piece on the Johnson-Jeffries prize fight.

headline: Edith writes Kermit
summary: A Sunday at home. Edith sends Kermit the family news.

headline: Wood becomes Army chief of staff
summary: Leonard Wood takes up his post as Chief of Staff of the United States Army, a job he will hold until April 1914.

headline: A divided party
summary: Roosevelt writes Lodge about the trouble of standing behind a split Republican party, and tells Arthur Lee how he feels about Taft.

headline: Dr. Lambert visits
summary: Roosevelt's physician and friend Dr. Alexander Lambert is a guest.

headline: Thinking about Africa policy
summary: Roosevelt writes Sir Percy Girouard about African affairs. Three guests sign in, including James L. Breese Jr.

headline: Promising to stump for Beveridge
summary: Roosevelt agrees to speak in Indiana for Senator Beveridge's campaign and writes Nick Longworth about Ohio politics. Joseph Burden and Eliot Cross are guests.

headline: English songbirds in print
summary: The Outlook carries Roosevelt's account of English songbirds.

headline: Sunday at Sagamore
summary: A quiet day at home.

headline: Will Cowles visits
summary: Bamie's husband, Admiral William S. Cowles, is among three guests.

headline: At home
summary: Nothing recorded at Sagamore Hill.

headline: Safari naturalists come calling
summary: Edmund Heller and Edgar Mearns, naturalists from the African expedition, visit along with the Lamberts and Constance Leupp.

headline: Another day home
summary: No entries for the day.

headline: Visitors at The Outlook
summary: Roosevelt lunches with Neill and Kellogg, and sees Beveridge, Joseph Bishop and others at his Outlook office.

headline: A tribute to Leonard Wood
summary: The Outlook prints Roosevelt's article on his old friend Leonard Wood.

headline: Archie leaves Groton
summary: Archie, thrown out of Groton for a letter mocking the headmaster, is briefly home before being sent to school in Arizona. Richard C. Paine is a guest.

headline: Off to coal country
summary: Roosevelt leaves Sagamore Hill for the Lackawanna Valley in Pennsylvania's anthracite region.

headline: Touring mine towns with John Mitchell
summary: With mine union leader John Mitchell, Roosevelt visits coal villages in the Lackawanna Valley, then travels to Scranton in Bishop Hoban's company and to Wilkes-Barre in Father Curran's.

headline: Wyoming Valley mining villages
summary: Roosevelt's coal-country tour continues through the mining towns of the Wyoming Valley.

headline: Home to Oyster Bay
summary: Roosevelt returns to Oyster Bay. Eliot Cross and Joseph Burden are guests.

headline: Lunch with Newberry
summary: In the city, Roosevelt lunches with his former Navy Secretary Truman Newberry and sees Youngs, Betts and Morrisey.

headline: Edith turns 49
summary: On Edith's birthday, The Outlook prints Roosevelt's article on selfish legislation. He writes Edward Vreeland on state politics and currency, and tells Nick about the coal towns and his coming tour, joking his throat may not hold out.

headline: Alice in the papers
summary: Alice and Nick reach Beverly, Massachusetts, to stay with the Bryce Allens, while Alice takes heavy criticism for smoking cigarettes in public.

headline: At Sagamore Hill
summary: No events recorded.

headline: Proud of Nick
summary: Roosevelt tells Alice he admires how Nick is carrying himself, and writes William Allen White about John Brown and his upcoming Osawatomie speech. Senator Bourne calls at The Outlook; William Loeb stays at Sagamore.

headline: Too much mail
summary: Roosevelt confers with Garfield and Pinchot. He complains to Bamie that his correspondence is crushing and says young Franklin should enter politics on his own terms, and writes Ted about quietly backing Hiram Johnson in California. Most afternoons he rides with Edith.

headline: Experimental farms on Long Island
summary: Roosevelt inspects a pair of experimental farms on Long Island, one at Medford and one at Wading River.

headline: Lunch with Griscom
summary: Roosevelt lunches with Lloyd Griscom, leader of the fight against boss William Barnes Jr., and sees Pinchot and others at The Outlook. Bishop Charles Brent is a guest.

headline: Ethel's birthday
summary: Ethel turns 19. Roosevelt confers with Pinchot.

headline: Pinchot stays over
summary: Gifford Pinchot is a guest at Sagamore Hill.

headline: Griscom again
summary: Roosevelt confers with Lloyd Griscom.

headline: Sherman gets the nod
summary: Roosevelt meets with Griscom, Ward and Barnes. As he expected, the Republican State Committee, with Taft's blessing, backs Vice President Sherman as temporary chairman of the state convention. He calls himself a genuine radical in a letter to Arthur Lee and writes Archie, who is in the Badlands.

headline: A party split wide open
summary: Roosevelt tells Lodge the Republican break is as deep as it could be, and that Taft can neither mend it nor let anyone else try. He also writes Pinchot about the Osawatomie speech.

headline: Planning with Loeb and Griscom
summary: Roosevelt confers with Loeb, Griscom and Cocks, and writes the San Francisco editor Fremont Older about California politics.

headline: A cornerstone in Garden City
summary: Roosevelt lays the cornerstone for Doubleday, Page and Company's new building in Garden City, then speaks to the Negro Business Men's League in New York. He apologizes to Vice President Sherman over a letter that went astray.

headline: Nick drops by
summary: Nick Longworth calls at Sagamore Hill.

headline: Sunday
summary: Nothing recorded at home.

headline: Into the convention fight
summary: Roosevelt announces he will seek the temporary chairmanship of the state Republican convention, a direct challenge to the Old Guard. He assures William Allen White he has no wish to head a faction in the state.

headline: The western tour begins
summary: Roosevelt sets out on a sixteen-state speaking trip to Kansas in a private car lent by The Outlook. He writes Ted that Taft is helpless as a leader and that the old Oyster Bay summers of the children's youth are over.

headline: Ten thousand at a Grange picnic
summary: At Utica, Roosevelt talks about farming and country life to a Grange picnic crowd of about 10,000.

headline: Across the Great Lakes
summary: Roosevelt talks railroads at Dunkirk, speaks to 250 Buffalo businessmen at breakfast about cleaning up the lake waters, and gives speeches in Ohio towns from Conneaut to Toledo before a Press Club talk in Chicago.

headline: Twins in Iowa, Archie in Omaha
summary: Crossing Iowa, Roosevelt is shown a pair of twins at Ogden and speaks about children, then speaks at Carroll and Council Bluffs, where Walter Smith drives him around town. At Omaha, Archie and James Garfield join him.

headline: Conservation talk in Cheyenne
summary: In Cheyenne, Roosevelt speaks on conservation, is entertained by Governor Brooks, and watches a pony race and rodeo.

headline: Thirty miles on horseback
summary: Roosevelt rides 30 miles on a bronco with Senator Francis Warren to Warren's ranch, eats dinner there, and returns to Cheyenne.

headline: Taking on the Supreme Court in Colorado
summary: In Colorado, Roosevelt reviews a parade in his honor, eats a chuck wagon lunch, and tells the state livestock association that democracy must be progressive, criticizing recent Supreme Court rulings. He also addresses the legislature and Spanish-American War veterans. Edith is at Corinne's Henderson House.

headline: Colorado Springs and Pueblo
summary: Roosevelt speaks in Colorado Springs and Pueblo, conferring with Pinchot and Garfield as they travel, and meets General Bell's four-year-old daughter.

headline: The New Nationalism at Osawatomie
summary: At the dedication of a John Brown memorial in Osawatomie, Kansas, Roosevelt delivers "The New Nationalism," the most important speech of his post-presidency. He calls for a living wage, decent hours, and conservation that uses resources without robbing future generations, laying out the program he will carry to 1912.

headline: Two Kansas Citys
summary: Roosevelt speaks on both sides of the state line, in the Kansas City of Missouri and the Kansas City of Kansas. Edith comes home to Sagamore Hill from Herkimer County.

headline: Omaha speeches
summary: Roosevelt speaks in Omaha.

headline: Thanking Dakota at Sioux Falls
summary: After a stop in Sioux City, Roosevelt tells a Sioux Falls crowd that his years on a Dakota ranch were the most important part of his education. The Outlook prints two of his articles.

headline: Preaching in Willmar
summary: Roosevelt gives a Sunday sermon at Willmar, Minnesota, and travels through parts of Minnesota and the Dakotas.

headline: Fargo's library cornerstone
summary: Roosevelt spends the day in Fargo, North Dakota, giving speeches and setting the cornerstone for Fargo College's new Carnegie-funded library.

headline: St. Paul
summary: Roosevelt gives speeches in St. Paul, Minnesota.

headline: Public men mirror the public
summary: In Milwaukee Roosevelt tells his audience that in a democracy the quality of leaders depends on the quality of ordinary citizens.

headline: No dinner with Lorimer
summary: Roosevelt speaks at Freeport, Illinois, then addresses Chicago's Hamilton Club, having agreed to come only once Senator William Lorimer, who had bought his Senate seat, was out of the club.

headline: Fairness for capital and labor
summary: Roosevelt addresses the crowds at Cincinnati's Ohio Valley Exposition, then visits the Columbus scene of recent rioting in a streetcar strike and calls for justice from both companies and workers.

headline: Pittsburgh
summary: Roosevelt makes speeches in Pittsburgh. The Outlook runs his article on the pioneer spirit, and James Derby signs the Sagamore guest book.

headline: Home from the West
summary: The tour over, Roosevelt comes back through New York City to Sagamore Hill.

headline: Explaining Osawatomie to Lodge
summary: Roosevelt confers with Griscom and sees Parsons and Prendergast; Alice is a guest. He writes Lodge that his labor-over-capital line was borrowed from Lincoln, admits his remarks on courts have alarmed people, and discusses Lodge's reelection and Dolliver.

headline: Ted turns 23
summary: Ted marks his 23rd birthday in San Francisco.

headline: Quiet day
summary: Nothing is recorded at Sagamore Hill.

headline: The Suffolk County Fair
summary: Roosevelt speaks at the county fair in Riverhead. He writes Benjamin Ide Wheeler about the Earl lectures he will give at Berkeley next spring, and Lodge about New England and the bosses.

headline: Sizing up Taft for Arthur Lee
summary: Roosevelt dines with the New York Press Club. To Arthur Lee he opposes Butler's advice that Britain slow its navy, and predicts Taft will win renomination yet lose the 1912 election, weighing his own strengths and failings too.

headline: Speaking at the State Fair
summary: At the state fair in Syracuse, Roosevelt links the New Nationalism to old-fashioned morality. The Outlook prints his case that the tariff is a moral question.

headline: A good word for LaForce
summary: Roosevelt writes Arthur Baker on behalf of a fired employee named LaForce, father of seven, and Baker gives the man another chance.

headline: Speedboat to New Haven to see Taft
summary: Roosevelt races across Long Island Sound in Dodge's motorboat at 40 miles an hour, nearly swamping, then drives from Stamford to New Haven. At Henry White's house he meets President Taft, with Griscom, Bannard, Norton and Yale's President Hadley present.

headline: Who called the New Haven meeting?
summary: Papers report Roosevelt's denial that he arranged the New Haven meeting, which annoys Taft by making it look like the President's idea. Quentin heads back to Groton for his second year.

headline: Edith misses Quentin
summary: Roosevelt confers with John Dwight and Cocks and writes Governor Hadley, Ted and Lodge about politics ahead of the Saratoga convention. Ethel and Evelyn Irving play tennis, and Edith, sad at Quentin's leaving, goes with Archie to Aunt Lizzie's.

headline: Asking about Harriman's money
summary: Roosevelt meets Griscom, Bannard, Parsons and Prendergast, and asks George Cortelyou for facts on E. H. Harriman's 1904 campaign contributions.

headline: A new grandnephew, Baden-Powell calls
summary: Roosevelt confers with progressive Republicans and sees a long list of callers, among them General Baden-Powell and Ernest Thompson Seton. Franklin and Eleanor's son Elliott is born. In Cincinnati, Taft dines at the Longworth house with Alice and Nick.

headline: Defending the New Nationalism
summary: Roosevelt's Outlook article on criticism of the courts explains the New Nationalism. Willcox and Wainwright call, and he writes Lodge about Taft and the Saratoga convention.

headline: Sunday before Saratoga
summary: A quiet day at home.

headline: Arriving at Saratoga
summary: The state Republican convention opens at Saratoga. Roosevelt huddles with Griscom, Hapgood, Bannard, Parsons and other allies.

headline: Beating the Old Guard at Saratoga
