summary: Roosevelt is at Sagamore Hill; nothing else is recorded.

headline: At home
summary: Roosevelt is at Sagamore Hill; nothing else is recorded.

headline: Press attacks and canal tolls
summary: Roosevelt writes Governor Robert Bass on New Hampshire's Senate race, Governor Hiram Johnson on hostile press coverage, the party and Wilson, and Henry White on Panama Canal tolls.

headline: At home
summary: Roosevelt is at Sagamore Hill; nothing else is recorded.

headline: On Perkins again
summary: Roosevelt writes Walter Strong about George Perkins.

headline: Ethel will marry Richard Derby
summary: Ethel decides to marry Dr. Richard Derby. Chapters from Roosevelt's memoirs begin appearing in print.

headline: A month of home and city
summary: Roosevelt opens February at Sagamore Hill, going into New York City often.

headline: At home
summary: Roosevelt is at Sagamore Hill; nothing else is recorded.

headline: At home
summary: Roosevelt is at Sagamore Hill; nothing else is recorded.

headline: New Hampshire politics
summary: Roosevelt writes Governor Robert Perkins Bass about politics in New Hampshire.

headline: Recalling the moment he was shot
summary: In a letter to his friend William Sturgis Bigelow, Roosevelt describes the Milwaukee shooting: stepping into the car from a bright hotel, telling the crowd not to hurt the gunman, and feeling almost no pain beyond his broken rib.

headline: At home
summary: Roosevelt is at Sagamore Hill; nothing else is recorded.

headline: At home
summary: Roosevelt is at Sagamore Hill; nothing else is recorded.

headline: Concerts for the cause
summary: Roosevelt writes Maud Nathan about benefit concerts to raise money for the Progressive Party.

headline: At home
summary: Roosevelt is at Sagamore Hill; nothing else is recorded.

headline: One six-year presidential term?
summary: Roosevelt writes Joseph Bucklin Bishop about Wilson and a proposed amendment limiting presidents to a single six-year term.

headline: Southern Democrats for the movement
summary: Roosevelt writes Silas McBee, and Thomas Nelson Page in much the same vein, about having Democrats head the Progressive cause in the South.

headline: Claiming Lincoln's legacy
summary: At the Progressive Party's Lincoln Day dinner in New York, Roosevelt speaks on 'The Heirs of Abraham Lincoln.' His daughter Alice turns 29.

headline: In the city
summary: Roosevelt, in New York, writes George Wicker about New Hampshire politics.

headline: Dinner with the Rough Riders
summary: Roosevelt speaks at a Rough Riders dinner in New York and writes Lucius Watkins about Michigan's April local elections.

headline: Press relations and party mergers
summary: Roosevelt writes John Callan O'Laughlin on improving how the Army and Navy deal with the press, and Frank Munsey on talk of merging Republicans and Progressives.

headline: At home
summary: Roosevelt is at Sagamore Hill; nothing else is recorded.

headline: A walk to the office
summary: Roosevelt, Edith and Ethel are staying at the Marquis Hotel on East 31st Street. After a 9 o'clock breakfast he walks down Madison Avenue to his Outlook office, works till 5:30, then returns for tea with Edith. He writes Charles Bonaparte about Munsey's push to merge the parties.

headline: Evening train to Oyster Bay; coup in Mexico
summary: Another day like the last, except Roosevelt leaves the office at 5 to catch the 5:30 home from Pennsylvania Station. In Mexico, Victoriano Huerta seizes power from Francisco Madero.

headline: At home
summary: Roosevelt is at Sagamore Hill; nothing else is recorded.

headline: At home
summary: Roosevelt is at Sagamore Hill; nothing else is recorded.

headline: Two historians and Will Cowles visit
summary: Historians Max Farrand and Archibald Cary Coolidge and Roosevelt's brother-in-law Will Cowles are guests at Sagamore Hill.

headline: Nassau County Progressives come calling
summary: Roosevelt holds a reception at Sagamore Hill for Progressives from Nassau County.

headline: At home
summary: Roosevelt is at Sagamore Hill; nothing else is recorded.

headline: At home
summary: Roosevelt is at Sagamore Hill; nothing else is recorded.

headline: Ex-Republicans working for betterment
summary: Teresa Richardson visits. Roosevelt writes Ernest Harvier that former Republicans in the new party are truly pursuing industrial reform, and sends Walter Clyde Jones his thoughts about the Senate.

headline: At home
summary: Roosevelt is at Sagamore Hill; nothing else is recorded.

headline: Lodge likes the memoirs; African game book
summary: Warrington Dawson visits. Roosevelt is pleased Lodge enjoyed his Outlook reminiscences, and mentions he is writing a natural history of Africa's big game together with Edmund Heller. He warns William Cochran and Beveridge that La Follette is luring Progressives back to the Republicans.

headline: Alice's new life in Cincinnati
summary: Another installment of Roosevelt's memoirs is published. Out in Ohio, Alice now lives in Cincinnati with Nick and his mother and must make big adjustments.

headline: March opens with guests
summary: Roosevelt is at Sagamore Hill with frequent trips to the city. W. R. Cross and three others identified only by first names sign the guest book.

headline: Ethel and a trip to Brazil
summary: Edith writes Kermit that she will not stop Ethel from going to Brazil, though she needs her at home.

headline: Kellor and Abbott visit
summary: Frances Kellor and Lawrence Abbott are guests at Sagamore Hill.

headline: At the Armory Show as Wilson takes office
summary: While Woodrow Wilson is sworn in as the 28th President in Washington, Roosevelt tours the modern art exhibition now known as the Armory Show, plus a housing exhibit. He suggests enlisting South American nations to deal with Mexico's new regime and argues the flood-prone Mississippi must be managed by the government as one system.

headline: A bullet like a pocket watch
summary: Roosevelt writes Charles Washburn about how little real power kings hold, and says the bullet lodged in him troubles him no more than something in his vest pocket.

headline: At home
summary: Roosevelt is at Sagamore Hill; nothing else is recorded.

headline: At home
summary: Roosevelt is at Sagamore Hill; nothing else is recorded.

headline: Richard Derby among the guests
summary: Charles and Edith Lindley and Ethel's fiance Richard Derby are guests at Sagamore Hill.

headline: At home
summary: Roosevelt is at Sagamore Hill; nothing else is recorded.

headline: At home
summary: Roosevelt is at Sagamore Hill; nothing else is recorded.

headline: At home
summary: Roosevelt is at Sagamore Hill; nothing else is recorded.

headline: At home
summary: Roosevelt is at Sagamore Hill; nothing else is recorded.

headline: Philadelphia speech on Progressive service
summary: Roosevelt speaks at the Philadelphia Opera House about the Progressive Service.

headline: Before Pennsylvania's electors
summary: Still in Philadelphia, Roosevelt speaks before the state's Electoral College Association.

headline: Back from Philadelphia
summary: Roosevelt returns through New York City to Sagamore Hill.

headline: At home
summary: Roosevelt is at Sagamore Hill; nothing else is recorded.

headline: Franklin heads to the Navy Department
summary: Roosevelt's cousin Franklin D. Roosevelt wins Senate confirmation as the Navy's assistant secretary.

headline: Congratulations to Franklin and Wilson's cabinet
summary: Roosevelt writes Franklin to wish him well at the Navy Department and sends congratulations to new ambassador James Gerard, Interior Secretary Franklin Lane and Attorney General James McReynolds. He also writes O'Laughlin on organizing Progressive congressmen.

headline: A portrait of Macaulay
summary: Roosevelt thanks George Otto Trevelyan for a portrait of Macaulay and writes William Cochran on Massachusetts local elections.

headline: At home
summary: Roosevelt is at Sagamore Hill; nothing else is recorded.

headline: At home
summary: Roosevelt is at Sagamore Hill; nothing else is recorded.

headline: A Saturday house party
summary: James Breese, Chalmers Wood, Eleanor Greene, Cornelia Landon and H. Osborn Jr. sign the Sagamore Hill guest book.

headline: At home
summary: Roosevelt is at Sagamore Hill; nothing else is recorded.

headline: At home
summary: Roosevelt is at Sagamore Hill; nothing else is recorded.

headline: On the Aldrich Bill
summary: Roosevelt writes Henry Cochems about the Aldrich Bill.

headline: At home
summary: Roosevelt is at Sagamore Hill; nothing else is recorded.

headline: At home
summary: Roosevelt is at Sagamore Hill; nothing else is recorded.

headline: Albany, then on to Detroit
summary: After meeting Congressman William Hinebaugh, Roosevelt goes to Albany to speak to New York Progressives and calls on Governor William Sulzer and Lieutenant Governor Martin Glynn, then leaves for Detroit. He writes Gifford Pinchot on politics and on charges about land reclamation.

headline: Detroit, suffrage, and the Armory Show
summary: In Detroit, Roosevelt meets Gifford Pinchot and Michigan Progressives and speaks in favor of votes for women. His Outlook piece on the Armory Show appears, waving off cubist canvases yet applauding the show's break with the conventional.

headline: Back to Oyster Bay
summary: Roosevelt travels home to Oyster Bay.

headline: Memoirs in print again
summary: A new installment of Roosevelt's autobiography is published.

headline: Who to invite to Ethel's wedding
summary: Roosevelt urges Winthrop Chanler to see that Lodge and George Meyer attend to Ethel's wedding, fearing election wounds might keep them away; he would rather Root, Taft and Nicholas Murray Butler stay away. He also writes Perkins about a memo for his autobiography and the tariff.

headline: A rallying letter to Progressives in Congress
summary: Roosevelt sends the Progressive members of Congress an encouraging letter declaring the party stands for the people's rights.

headline: At home
summary: Roosevelt is at Sagamore Hill; nothing else is recorded.

headline: Ethel marries Richard Derby
summary: Ethel weds Dr. Richard Derby at Christ Church in Oyster Bay before 500 guests. Alice comes but Nick does not; Lodge and George Meyer attend. Roosevelt tells Bamie that Derby is the finest young man he knows.

headline: The morning after the wedding
summary: Worn out, Edith stays in bed until lunch and spends the afternoon roaming the woods. Alice does not spend time with her.

headline: Supper with Lillian Wald and a settlement play

summary: Roosevelt is at Sagamore Hill; nothing else is recorded.

summary: The Progressives fare poorly in spring elections in Michigan and Chicago. In Washington, Wilson addresses both houses of Congress in person, something no president had done since George Washington. Roosevelt writes J. M. Wall about the party.

headline: Archie turns 19
summary: Roosevelt's son Archie celebrates his 19th birthday.

headline: Corinne's anniversary
summary: Roosevelt's sister Corinne marks 31 years of marriage.

summary: Roosevelt wires Johnson again on California, and writes Herbert Drake about Wilson's World's Work article attacking his ideas on regulating corporations. Scribner's brings out a new collection of his essays, and another memoir installment appears.

headline: A picture letter for Ethel
summary: Roosevelt writes Ethel, sending a picture letter and delighting in her happiness with Dick. He notes Kermit is struggling in South America and wishes he were better company for Edith in the evenings.

headline: Suffrage speech; no run for mayor
summary: Roosevelt speaks at a woman suffrage meeting. He tells Henry White that Wilson and Secretary of State Bryan have handled California badly and that he will not run for mayor, and backs Governor Sulzer's direct primary bill.

summary: Governor Hiram Johnson signs California's anti-Japanese land bill, calling it the people's will; it breaks no federal law.

headline: Off to Michigan for the libel trial
summary: Roosevelt leaves for Marquette, Michigan, to press his libel suit against editor George Newett. Edith writes Kermit that Nick's absence from the wedding mattered little to the family but deeply hurt Alice.

headline: Traveling to Marquette
summary: Roosevelt is on his way to Marquette.

headline: On the witness stand
summary: Staying with George Shiras, Roosevelt takes the stand in his suit against George Newett, whose Ishpeming Iron Ore had branded him a liar, a curser and a drunk.

headline: Trial continues in Marquette
summary: Roosevelt remains in Marquette as the libel trial goes on.

headline: Trial continues in Marquette
summary: Roosevelt is still in Marquette for the libel case.

headline: Old friends vouch for him
summary: A parade of witnesses testifies to Roosevelt's character and sobriety, among them Gifford Pinchot, Leonard Wood, George Dewey, Jacob Riis, his doctors Alexander Lambert and Presley Rixey, and cousins Emlen and Philip Roosevelt.

headline: Edith and Spring-Rice
summary: Edith writes Cecil Spring-Rice that politics make a visit unwise just now, though the old friends long to see each other.

headline: Six cents and vindication
summary: Newett gives up, and Roosevelt wins his libel case, taking just six cents in damages. He writes Bamie that the libeler caved. The 17th Amendment takes effect, moving the choice of senators from state legislatures to the voters.

headline: Kermit's news from Brazil, sent from Michigan
summary: From Marquette, Roosevelt writes his daughter Ethel that her brother Kermit has taken a job with the Anglo Brazil Iron Company in the south of Brazil.

headline: Home again, writing about Portsmouth
summary: Roosevelt gets back to New York and Sagamore Hill and writes diplomat Henry White about his autobiography chapter on the Portsmouth peace and the Japanese complaints it drew, along with present-day trouble with Japan.

headline: A picnic with Edith
summary: Roosevelt and his wife Edith head out on a picnic. He also makes clear that Dick Derby, about to join the family through Ethel, will be counted as fully one of his own.

headline: Callers at Sagamore Hill
summary: Roosevelt receives visitors at Sagamore Hill, among them Mitchel and Father York.

headline: Quiet day at Sagamore Hill
summary: Roosevelt is at Sagamore Hill; nothing else is recorded.

headline: Cheering schoolboy athletes in Central Park
summary: Roosevelt travels into the city to watch a field day in Central Park put on by boys of the Public Schools Athletic League.

headline: Argentina's minister visits
summary: Arthur Hill and Romulo Naon, Argentina's minister to the United States, spend time as Roosevelt's guests at Sagamore Hill.

headline: Sunday at Sagamore Hill
summary: Roosevelt is at Sagamore Hill; nothing else is recorded.

headline: Commencement speech at the Hill School
summary: Roosevelt goes to Pottstown, Pennsylvania, and speaks to the graduating class of the Hill School.

headline: Stumping for direct primaries in Buffalo
summary: In Buffalo, Roosevelt addresses the Progressive Club to push for direct primaries in New York, staying with C. J. Hamlin. His wife Edith sails for Europe to be near her sister Emily after emergency appendix surgery.

headline: Lunch with 500 Progressives
summary: In Rochester, Roosevelt sits down to lunch with some five hundred Progressives, and speeches follow.

headline: Heading for Archie's graduation
summary: Roosevelt travels toward Andover, Massachusetts. Ted, his wife Eleanor and little Gracie sign in as guests.

headline: Archie graduates from Phillips Academy
summary: Roosevelt watches his son Archie finish at Phillips Academy in Andover, speaks at the alumni luncheon, and then leaves for Hartford.

headline: Hartford, then home
summary: Roosevelt leaves Hartford, Connecticut, and makes for Oyster Bay.

headline: A full house at Sagamore Hill
summary: Ted and Eleanor bring baby Gracie to Sagamore Hill. Alice Longworth and Eleanor's mother, Mrs. Alexander, are staying too.

headline: A Bunker Hill Day speech on the flag
summary: For Bunker Hill Day, Roosevelt gives a rousing talk on the American flag at a Boston banquet of Charlestown's Hayes Square Outing Club. He dines with W. S. Bigelow, is received by the city's press club, and returns to New York.

headline: Planning a South American journey
summary: Roosevelt lunches at the American Museum of Natural History with Frank Chapman and Father Zahm, a South America traveler, to start arranging his trip to Brazil. He also writes several men about the Underwood tariff.

headline: Conference with Whitman
summary: Roosevelt meets with Whitman at Sagamore Hill. Alice and Nick are the house guests.

headline: Good news from Lausanne
summary: Herbert K. Smith and his wife visit Sagamore Hill as word comes from Europe: Ethel and Dick have joined Edith at Lausanne's Hotel Mirabeau, and Emily's surgery went well. Roosevelt writes Arthur Hill about his Charlestown speech attacking the red flag.

headline: Ted and Eleanor's anniversary
summary: Ludwig Moorehead visits Sagamore Hill on the third wedding anniversary of Ted and Eleanor.

headline: The boys come home from school
summary: Quentin and Archie arrive back at Sagamore Hill for the summer.

headline: Sunday at Sagamore Hill
summary: Roosevelt is at Sagamore Hill; nothing else is recorded.

headline: A long letter to Kermit
summary: With his sister Corinne and her husband Douglas visiting, Roosevelt writes Kermit in Brazil, backing his work, sketching ideas for their coming South American journey, and reporting that Eleanor is keeping house while Edith is away.

headline: A Brazilian envoy calls
summary: Mrs. Leigh Hunt and Mrs. Kinsolving join Roosevelt for lunch, and Jose DeLima, secretary to Brazil's foreign minister Lauro Muller, calls. Roosevelt writes William Hotchkiss about the race for mayor.

headline: Quiet day at Sagamore Hill
summary: Roosevelt is at Sagamore Hill; nothing else is recorded.

headline: Quiet day at Sagamore Hill
summary: Roosevelt is at Sagamore Hill; nothing else is recorded.

headline: Workers' compensation and Black voters
summary: Roosevelt urges Donald Richberg to have Progressives in Congress press for a workmen's compensation law, and writes Walter Brown about Black voters in the North.

headline: Guests for the weekend
summary: James B. Eustis and his wife visit Sagamore Hill, along with Ted and Eleanor.

headline: Sunday at Sagamore Hill
summary: Roosevelt is at Sagamore Hill; nothing else is recorded.

headline: Autobiography installment; western plans
summary: Another installment of Roosevelt's "Chapters of a Possible Autobiography" appears. Alice and Nick set off for Panama, and the record notes the coming western journey with Archie, Quentin and cousin Nicholas Roosevelt to the Indian lands beyond the Grand Canyon's north side.

headline: Another letter on the tariff
summary: Roosevelt writes William Nelson again about the Underwood tariff bill.

headline: The Progressive Party turns one
summary: At Newport, Roosevelt marks the Progressive Party's first birthday with a speech on the American Navy, then joins party leaders in an open discussion.

headline: Quiet day at Sagamore Hill
summary: Roosevelt is at Sagamore Hill; nothing else is recorded.

headline: Independence Day at Sagamore Hill
summary: Roosevelt is at Sagamore Hill; nothing else is recorded.

summary: Roosevelt is at Sagamore Hill; nothing else is recorded.

headline: Writing Spring-Rice about Japan
summary: Roosevelt writes his old friend Cecil Spring-Rice about friction between the United States and Japan, saying he wants to see him and never mind diplomacy. From Europe, his wife Edith complains to Kermit that Ted's in-laws have crowded into Sagamore Hill.

headline: Off west with Archie and Quentin
summary: Roosevelt sets out on a western trip with his sons Archie and Quentin. He writes Arthur Lee about his libel trial, a peace conference and the coming South American trip, glad to be beyond the Progressives' reach for a while, and admitting he disliked Edith's going abroad though she had to.

headline: Rolling west by train
summary: Roosevelt and the boys are on their way west.

headline: No change on the Southern question
summary: Still traveling west, Roosevelt writes Walter Brown that he will not change the Progressive Party's all-white policy in the South.

headline: With Bob Ferguson in Silver City
summary: Roosevelt and his sons arrive in Silver City, New Mexico, as guests of his old friend Bob Ferguson.

headline: Another day at Silver City
summary: The Roosevelts remain at Silver City with Bob Ferguson.

headline: Bound for the Grand Canyon
summary: From Albuquerque the Roosevelts head for the Grand Canyon, reaching Flagstaff at 9:45 at night, where cousin Nicholas Roosevelt joins them. They resolve to pack in to see Rainbow Natural Bridge while in Arizona, then ride the train on to Williams.

headline: An old professor on the canyon rim
summary: Roosevelt, Quentin and Nicholas reach the Grand Canyon at 8 a.m. and check into the near-empty El Tovar Hotel. After a day of planning and a walk along the rim, they run into Dr. Fisher, once Roosevelt's professor, who joins them for dinner and talk of canyon plants and animals.

headline: Archie reaches the canyon rim
summary: Archie comes in from Flagstaff by train, bringing Jesse Cummings of Mesa to cook, pack and wrangle for the trip. Roosevelt and Quentin spend part of the day on horseback near El Tovar. Edith writes Kermit that the coming Brazil journey worries her.

headline: Down into the Grand Canyon
summary: After an early hotel breakfast, Roosevelt, Archie, Quentin, cousin Nicholas and Jesse Cummings ride mules down the Bright Angel Trail and finish the steepest pitch on foot. Rain turns to a thunderstorm as they ride a hand-pulled cable car over the Colorado. A Bar Z hand named Stevenson lends horses for the climb north, and supper by the river is bacon, flat pancakes and canned peas.

headline: Night climb to the North Rim
summary: Woken at 1:30 a.m. by Mansfield of the Bar Z, the party eats graham meal and canned chicken and sets off up the trail at 2:45 under clouds. By noon they top out on the North Rim and meet game warden "Uncle Jimmy" Owens, then ready the hunt as rain falls.

headline: Trouble with the hired guides
summary: The Mormon guides who were supposed to bring horses down to the river on the 15th never came, so they are let go. Uncle Jimmy Owens and prospector Joe Wilson will guide the hunt instead, and the party meets Forest Supervisor Pelton and his rangers.

headline: Recruiting Joe Wilson
summary: In a drizzle, the party persuades Joe Wilson to come along on the hunt.

headline: Getting ready to hunt
summary: The Roosevelts spend the day preparing for the hunt on the canyon's north side.

headline: Nicholas bags a cougar
summary: After a night of sour beans and rain in Uncle Jim's tent, the party gets moving at 9. The hounds tree a cougar near the canyon rim and Nicholas brings it down. Lunch comes in a thunderstorm at Kanabownits Canyon; later a cold trail, a new camp and more rain.

headline: Empty-handed at Point Sublime
summary: On a clear, cold morning the hunters ride southeast along the rim toward Point Sublime looking for cougars, but find none. Back at camp, a Mormon visitor is waiting for Roosevelt and leaves soon after.

headline: Writing a speech for Brazil in camp
summary: With the horses strayed and a hound's leg broken, Roosevelt sits in the tent drafting the speech he will give in Brazil and tells the boys stories of earlier Roosevelt childhoods. Next morning, after burnt biscuits, he hunts near Cliff Spring without luck and explores ruined pueblos and cliff dwellings.

headline: Two cougars and a supper of cougar meat
summary: Roosevelt and Archie each kill a cougar, as does Uncle Jimmy, and Roosevelt eats the meat with gusto. Over the next days the party washes up at the ranger station, rides Wooley's Trail to camp under a ledge facing the San Francisco Peaks, hears his ghost stories, and returns to see Supervisor Pelton.

headline: Riding to the Bar Z
summary: After a morning at the ranger station, the party rides to the Bar Z Ranch, where Roosevelt questions Al Doyle about the route to Rainbow Natural Bridge. Nicholas finds Doyle a bit of a talker.

headline: Autobiography chapters in print
summary: The month closes with another installment of Roosevelt's "Chapters of a Possible Autobiography" in print.

headline: Sandstorm in House Rock Valley
summary: Leaving the Bar Z before dawn, the party stops at Kane, where Mansfield lets them keep his horses free of charge, then drops down off the Kaibab into House Rock Valley beside the Vermilion Cliffs. A fierce sandstorm drives them into a stone cabin; Roosevelt beheads a rattler he has caught, and all sleep on the ground.

headline: Desert ride to Lees Ferry
summary: Up at first light, the party rides through hot desert country that impresses Roosevelt, to Lees Ferry, where Tom Caffell gives them a chicken lunch. Archie and Nicholas go over to the far bank to meet the men J. L. Hubbell has sent: the Navajo cook Loko, Navajo policeman Choke and Sneeze, and guide Francisco Marquez.

headline: Camp moves across the river
summary: At Roosevelt's suggestion the party shifts its gear and camp to the river's south bank. Joe Wilson and Uncle Jimmy Owens turn back for the Grand Canyon. From Europe, his wife Edith writes Kermit that she had wanted this trip so father and Quentin would come to understand one another.

headline: Forty miles into Navajo country
summary: With two wagons, the party reaches Tanner's Well, 25 miles out, by noon, covers 15 more after lunch, and camps on a ridge. Roosevelt has been watching the Navajo people along the way.

headline: Arriving at Tuba City
summary: On a cool, fast day the party lunches and bathes at Willow Springs, then rides into Tuba City to the Preston trading post. They visit with Mr. Sullivan, who serves as both Indian agent and head of the school; Roosevelt and Quentin sleep in his house, Archie and Nicholas outside.

headline: Hearing out Hopi and Navajo leaders
summary: Mr. Sullivan drives the party to a Hopi village, where the chiefs lay their complaints against the government before Roosevelt; later he hears Navajo chiefs do the same. Quentin and Nicholas ride in Preston's automobile, one of three in town, and dinner is at Preston's. In Italy, Edith turns 52.

headline: Through deep sand toward Marsh Pass
summary: After breakfast the group sets off for Marsh Pass across 25 miles of deep sand, an 8-hour ride, pausing an hour at Red Lake Trading Post and reaching Halfway House at 9 p.m. for the night.

headline: Camp under a half moon at Marsh Pass
summary: The riders cross grassland past Black Mesa, see many pueblo ruins, and camp in lovely Marsh Pass under a bright half moon.

headline: At the Wetherills' post in Kayenta
summary: After 40 miles in the saddle, the party reaches the Kayenta trading post of John and Louisa Wetherill before noon, meets Mr. Colville and Mrs. Peabody, and is shown Navajo sand paintings by Mrs. Wetherill.

headline: Setting out for Rainbow Bridge
summary: The Roosevelts leave Kayenta for Rainbow Natural Bridge, seen by whites only four years before. Guiding them are John Wetherill, Jesse Cummings and a Navajo called Glad Hand, soon joined by Nasja Begay, the Paiute who first led whites there. Traveling light without tents, they pass a cave pueblo and camp by Bubbling Spring.

headline: Camping beneath Rainbow Bridge
summary: After a slow start up Paiute Canyon and a night below Navajo Mountain, the party strips down to essentials, rides rough slickrock, squeezes through a crack in the rock, and walks in for a grand first look at Rainbow Bridge. They wash in a pool and sleep under the arch as a full moon rises.

headline: Back to Navajo Mountain; Sulzer impeached
summary: Making good time on the way back, the party reaches its old camp below Navajo Mountain by evening. It is Ethel's 22nd birthday, and in Albany the legislature votes to impeach Governor William Sulzer.

headline: Paiute Canyon to Bubbling Spring
summary: The party lunches in Paiute Canyon and spends the night at Bubbling Spring.

headline: Return to Kayenta
summary: A five-hour ride brings the party back to Kayenta in time for lunch.

headline: Novels and Navajo lore
summary: Resting at Kayenta, the party reads cheap novels and listens to Mrs. Wetherill on Navajo ways.

headline: Eight hours across the mesa
summary: With a fresh pack outfit and John Wetherill, Dave Miller and two Navajo men, Snake Dance and Hound, the party rides eight hours straight, eating only an evening meal. Back east, granddaughter Gracie turns two.

headline: Onto the Hopi lands
summary: Another long day crossing Black Mesa brings the party to the Hopi reservation. The two Navajo guides shoot, roast and eat a few prairie dogs.

headline: Crowds at Walpi
summary: A short ride brings the party to Walpi, where Lorenzo Hubbell meets them amid a tangle of tourists and film crews who have come to see Roosevelt.

headline: Inside a Hopi kiva
summary: Lorenzo Hubbell takes Roosevelt into a kiva for a quarter hour, introduces him to the Hopi chiefs, and wins permission for the family to see the next day's snake washing. They watch an antelope dance and meet Indian Service officials and Natalie Curtis. Edith, Ethel and Dick reach home from Europe.

headline: The Hopi snake dance
summary: Roosevelt watches a Hopi footrace, joins about 20 men in a kiva for the 40-minute snake washing, and at 5 p.m. sees the snake dance before some 800 whites, most there to see him. Seated with Governor Hunt before Hunt's cameramen, he then motors with Hubbell through the desert night to Ganado.

headline: Horse-trading at Hubbell's
summary: The Roosevelts pull in at Hubbell's place at one in the morning. Hubbell's daughter, Mrs. Goodman, welcomes them after breakfast, and they spend the day bargaining for horses with Hubbell and enjoying his yarns.

headline: Mud, baths and the Chicago train
summary: Roused at 4 a.m., the Roosevelts drive toward Gallup, pushing a stuck car out of the mud near St. Michaels. In Gallup the Cotton and Manning families lend their tubs, and at noon the party boards the California Limited for Chicago before a big crowd. Roosevelt writes George Perkins about the Progressive pledge.

headline: On the train east
summary: Roosevelt, Archie, Quentin and Nicholas are aboard the train from Gallup, crossing the plains toward Chicago.

headline: Sunburned and back in Chicago
summary: Burned red by the desert sun, Roosevelt is met in Chicago by a reception committee and a crowd of photographers. He lunches and speaks at the Progressive Club, talks with party leaders, and within a couple of hours boards the Pennsylvania Limited for home.

headline: Home from the Southwest
summary: The train pulls into New York in the morning. Roosevelt heads straight to the Outlook office to confer with Progressive leaders, meets George McAneny and the fusion candidates at the Harvard Club, and then goes home to Sagamore Hill. He writes Hiram Johnson about California's Progressives, admitting little faith in Wilson, and Frank Dingley about the party in Maine.

headline: Quiet day at Sagamore Hill
summary: Roosevelt is at Sagamore Hill; nothing else is recorded.

headline: Quentin grows up
summary: Edith writes Kermit that Quentin seems more grown-up since coming home from the Southwest.

headline: Another autobiography installment
summary: A further chapter of Roosevelt's "Chapters of a Possible Autobiography" comes out.

headline: Sagamore Hill, with trips to the city
summary: Roosevelt is based at Sagamore Hill this month and goes into New York often.

K. Davis that the South's whites-only approach may need to be dropped.

headline: Spelling out the Progressive creed
summary: Privately, Roosevelt tells Victor Murdock he will not run in 1916 under either party. A Century Magazine article lays out the Progressive aims, arguing neither old party serves ordinary people. In Albany, Governor Sulzer is removed after his impeachment trial.

headline: A Progressive send-off in New York
summary: New York Progressives throw Roosevelt a farewell dinner at a city roof garden. Albert Beveridge speaks, and Roosevelt follows with an attack on two party bosses, Republican William Barnes Jr. and Tammany's Charles Murphy.

headline: Sailing for South America
summary: At 1 p.m. Roosevelt, in a gray suit and hat, sails from Brooklyn on the Vandyck with Edith, cousin Margaret Roosevelt, naturalist George Cherrie, Anthony Fiala and his secretary Frank Harper. Crowds pack the ship, pier and streets; the Progressives send a band, and envoys of three South American republics see him off.

headline: No answer on 1916

headline: Ashore in Barbados
summary: At Bridgetown, Barbados, Roosevelt gives a short speech, tours the town and lunches with the governor. Naturalist Leo Miller joins the expedition. In Brazil, Kermit turns 24.

headline: Eleanor's birthday at sea
summary: The party is at sea. Back home, his niece Eleanor Roosevelt turns 29.

headline: Word of Timothy Woodruff's death
summary: While Roosevelt is at sea, Timothy Woodruff dies in the United States. He had been Roosevelt's lieutenant governor and a Bull Moose backer in 1912.

summary: Roosevelt's party is at sea aboard the Vandyck, bound for South America.

headline: Edith on a lifted burden
summary: At sea, Edith writes Bamie that her husband seems freed of the Progressive Party, like Christian in Pilgrim's Progress shedding his bundle.

headline: Steaming south
summary: Roosevelt's party is at sea aboard the Vandyck, bound for South America.

headline: Brazil's welcome at Bahia
summary: Officials greet Roosevelt at Bahia, where Governor Seabra and Mayor Brandao receive him. After breakfast he meets the city council at City Hall, gives a speech and tours the city. Kermit, building bridges for the Anglo-Brazilian Iron Company, joins the party.

headline: Father and son on film
summary: Back at sea, Roosevelt and Kermit are caught on film aboard the Vandyck. It is the 15th birthday of his nephew Sheffield Cowles.

headline: Steaming south
summary: Roosevelt's party is at sea aboard the Vandyck, bound for South America.

headline: Steaming south
summary: Roosevelt's party is at sea aboard the Vandyck, bound for South America.

headline: Crowds in Rio de Janeiro
summary: Officials greet Roosevelt in Rio, a great public reception fills the Naval Arsenal, and he calls on President Hermes da Fonseca and Foreign Minister Lauro Muller.

headline: Breakfast with Brazil's president
summary: Roosevelt breakfasts with President da Fonseca, tours the Supreme Court and Military College, speaks to the YMCA, and spends the evening at the Russian ballet.

headline: Science and an embassy reception
summary: Roosevelt tours Rio's Bacteriological Institute and is guest of honor at a reception hosted by the American ambassador, Edwin Morgan.

headline: "American Internationalism" in Rio
summary: The party goes up Tijuca Peak and attends the president's garden party in the Botanical Gardens. At the national university, Roosevelt lectures on "American Internationalism."

headline: Birdsong on the bay
summary: On a cruise around the bay, Roosevelt listens to the birds. He visits the Naval School and receives a group of teachers and advanced students. Edith writes a friend that she finds Brazil lovely.

headline: Petropolis, then Sao Paulo
summary: The party visits the mountain town of Petropolis and then leaves for Sao Paulo.

headline: Turning 55 in Sao Paulo
summary: On his 55th birthday, Roosevelt is received by President Alves of Sao Paulo, sees the city and lectures at the university on "Character and Civilization."

headline: Touring Sao Paulo industry
summary: Roosevelt inspects local industry, including the Anglo-Brazilian Iron Company where Kermit works.

headline: Heading south for Montevideo
summary: Roosevelt leaves Sao Paulo, bound for Montevideo.

headline: A cattle ranch in Parana
summary: In Parana, the travelers pause at Morungava to see a ranch run by Brazil Land, Cattle and Packing Company.

headline: Crossing Parana
summary: The party is in Parana. At home, another installment of Roosevelt's "Chapters of a Possible Autobiography" appears.

headline: Through Santa Catarina
summary: The party crosses the Brazilian state of Santa Catarina. In New York, The Outlook prints Roosevelt's "American Internationalism."

headline: Rolling across Rio Grande do Sul
summary: Crossing Rio Grande do Sul, the train pauses at Cruz Alta and again at Santa Maria.

headline: Greeted at the Uruguayan border
summary: Passing through Porto Alegre, Roosevelt is met at the frontier by officials from Uruguay.

headline: Lunch with Uruguay's president
summary: In Montevideo, Roosevelt lunches with President Batlle y Ordonez and attends a state dinner before leaving for Buenos Aires. Back home it is election day. He writes Frank Chapman about the trip and a cougar skull from the West.

headline: Welcome to Buenos Aires
summary: U.S. Minister John Garrett and Argentine officials greet the party in Buenos Aires. The American community holds a reception, the Roosevelts are guests of President Saenz Pena, and Roosevelt calls on acting President de la Plaza.

headline: In Buenos Aires
summary: Roosevelt is in Buenos Aires; nothing else is recorded.

headline: "Democratic Ideals" at the Colon
summary: Roosevelt sits in on a session of the Argentine Congress, is received by Foreign Minister Bosch, and speaks at the Colon Theater to the Museo Social Argentino on "Democratic Ideals."

headline: Visiting schoolchildren
summary: Roosevelt visits schoolchildren in Buenos Aires. "Character and Civilization" is published in The Outlook.

headline: Racetrack and farm show
summary: The party spends the day at the racecourse known as the Hippodrome and at the farm exposition.

headline: An honorary degree and "Truths and Half Truths"
summary: The University of Buenos Aires gives Roosevelt an honorary doctor of laws, and he lectures at the Colon Theater on "Truths and Half Truths."

headline: A letter to Bamie
summary: From Buenos Aires, Roosevelt writes his sister Bamie about the journey.

headline: Troops at Campo de Mayo
summary: Roosevelt reviews troops at Campo de Mayo, stops at the Military Club, and speaks on "American Ideals" at a Museo Social Argentino banquet.

headline: Kermit is engaged
summary: A telegram reaches Kermit in Buenos Aires: Belle Willard has agreed to marry him.

headline: Edith feels left out
summary: Edith writes Ethel that she feels a little low, unable to help her husband and no longer needed by Kermit.

headline: Into the Argentine interior
summary: Roosevelt sets off into Santa Fe province, stopping at Rosario. "Democratic Ideals" appears in The Outlook, and he sends Sir Edward Grey a look back at the 1912 campaign.

headline: Library and schools in Tucuman
summary: In Tucuman, Roosevelt visits the library and the industrial schools.

headline: Sugar country
summary: Roosevelt tours sugar plantations around Tucuman.

headline: Three provincial capitals
summary: Traveling through Cordoba, San Luis and Mendoza, Roosevelt stops at the provincial capitals.

headline: Quentin turns 16
summary: Roosevelt is in Mendoza province. At Groton, Quentin turns 16.

headline: Wine country in Mendoza
summary: Roosevelt visits the agricultural college and wineries of Mendoza.

headline: Arriving in Chile
summary: Chilean officials welcome Roosevelt to Santiago.

headline: Lecture at the University of Chile
summary: Roosevelt calls on President Barros Luco and lectures to the University of Chile on democracy as a movement within a republic.

headline: In Santiago
summary: Roosevelt is in Santiago; nothing else is recorded.

headline: In Santiago
summary: Roosevelt is in Santiago; nothing else is recorded.

headline: Bamie's anniversary
summary: Roosevelt is in Santiago. At home, his sister Bamie marks 18 years of marriage.

headline: Edith sails for home
summary: At Valparaiso, Edith and Margaret leave Roosevelt and Kermit and board a ship for Panama. Roosevelt visits the Navy Club.

headline: Valparaiso and Santiago
summary: Roosevelt sees the sights of Valparaiso, then attends a reception by the American community in Santiago.

headline: Chile's naval base
summary: Roosevelt tours the naval base at Talcahuano, then turns back toward Argentina.

headline: Across the Chilean lakes
summary: Setting out from Puerto Varas, Roosevelt and Kermit travel by boat over Lake Llanquihue and Lake Esmeralda to Peulla.

headline: Over the Andes; the Autobiography appears
summary: Roosevelt and Kermit ride over the Andes to Lake Frias, then go by oxcart to Lake Nahuel Huapi and Bariloche. Back home, Scribner's publishes his Autobiography, and Boys' Life prints his "To All Boys."

headline: Motoring across Patagonia
summary: Roosevelt and Kermit drive across the barren Patagonian plains.

headline: Anniversary in Neuquen
summary: Roosevelt and Kermit reach Neuquen. It is the 27th wedding anniversary of Roosevelt and Edith.

headline: Bahia Blanca naval base
summary: Heading back toward Buenos Aires, Roosevelt stops to see the naval base at Bahia Blanca.

headline: Horsemen and flowers
summary: Back in Buenos Aires, the city's equestrian society hosts Roosevelt at the Club Hipico, and he visits the flower festival.

headline: Bound for Paraguay
summary: Roosevelt leaves Buenos Aires for Asuncion.

headline: North through Entre Rios
summary: The journey north passes through the provinces of Entre Rios and Corrientes.

headline: Guests in Asuncion
summary: In Asuncion, Roosevelt and Kermit stay with a former president of Paraguay.

headline: Villa Hayes with President Schaerer
summary: Roosevelt visits Villa Hayes with President Eduardo Schaerer.

headline: Up the Paraguay River
summary: In the afternoon Roosevelt starts up the Paraguay River aboard President Schaerer's yacht, with Tex Rickard along. His book Through the Brazilian Wilderness, and his 1913 diary, both pick up the story here.

headline: Piranhas and a family letter
summary: Roosevelt and Kermit catch a piranha and reach Concepcion just before midnight. He writes Ted's wife Eleanor, glad she is expecting again, with news of Kermit, Archie and Quentin.

headline: Reviewing Paraguay's army
summary: In Concepcion, Roosevelt and Kermit stroll the streets, attend a reception, inspect army barracks, and Roosevelt speaks at City Hall. Back on the river he shoots two crocodilians. Edith and Margaret sail from Panama for home.

headline: Colonel Rondon comes aboard
summary: Steaming north through tropical country, the yacht reaches Brazil's border at the Apa River at noon, where Colonel Candido Rondon and the Brazilian members join. They take on wood at Porto Murtinho. Roosevelt writes Lodge that the Monroe Doctrine should rest on shared agreement.

headline: Six caymans
summary: Under gray skies, Father Zahm baptizes two children in a river town, and Roosevelt shoots caymans, which he likens to crocodiles.

headline: Under the flag past Coimbra
summary: Rain falls over marshy plains to the east as the boat, flying the American flag, passes Coimbra. Roosevelt later describes the river's golden sunsets in his book.

headline: Reunion at Corumba
summary: At Corumba the town council hosts a reception and official dinner. Roosevelt and Kermit rejoin Cherrie and Miller, who have gathered about 800 bird and mammal specimens.

headline: Packing up at Corumba
summary: The expedition sorts and packs gear while Colonel Rondon checks supplies. Roosevelt hears plenty of animal tales, many about piranhas.

headline: Up the Taquari after an anteater
summary: Aboard the shallow river steamer Nyoac, the party heads up the Taquari toward Senhor de Barros's ranch, Las Palmeiras. Roosevelt shoots a giant anteater and many caymans, and they camp on shore.

headline: Riding to the fazenda; Margaret ill
summary: The party rides 20 miles over five or six hours to the de Barros ranch, with baggage hauled by oxcart. In New York, Edith and Margaret arrive home, Margaret gravely ill.

headline: Hunting the Pantanal
summary: Roosevelt and Kermit ride and hunt all day through the Pantanal swamp, and Kermit shoots a giant anteater.

headline: A jaguar for Roosevelt
summary: Kermit brings down two large marsh deer, and Roosevelt kills a jaguar and fires at a cayman.

headline: Kermit's jaguar
summary: Kermit gets a jaguar and Roosevelt a capybara. They push their horses through a stream full of piranhas, and Roosevelt marvels at the birdlife.

headline: Back toward the Taquari
summary: The party rides overland back to the Taquari. Roosevelt drops a wood ibis in flight.

headline: Downriver; the Federal Reserve becomes law
summary: Roosevelt and Kermit ride to the boat and steam downstream, towing a small craft for a peon. In Washington, the Federal Reserve Act is signed into law.

headline: The River of Doubt party assembles
summary: Back at Corumba, Roosevelt and Kermit rejoin the rest aboard the Nyoac. The party includes Harper, Father Zahm and his aide Jacob Sigg, Cherrie, Miller, Fiala, Colonel Rondon, Captain Magalhaes, Lieutenants Lyra and Filho, geologist Oliveira and taxidermist Reinisch. Roosevelt writes Edith.

headline: Christmas on the Paraguay
summary: On Christmas the Nyoac pushes upstream against a strong current, the expedition on deck and Kermit busy preparing skins.

headline: Flies and heat on the Sao Lourenco
summary: The Nyoac turns up the narrower Sao Lourenco, with biting flies everywhere and the thermometer at 100 degrees.

headline: Rain on the Cuiaba
summary: Steaming up the Cuiaba in heavy rain, the boat pulls in at a ranch to take on milk and beef.

headline: Welcome at Sao Joao
summary: The party reaches Sao Joao, the ranch of Brazil's agriculture secretary, Senhor da Costa Marques, for a big reception. Afternoon rain, 97 degrees.

headline: A peccary with a spear
summary: Father and son da Costa Marques take the party out after jaguars on an overcast day. Roosevelt kills a wild boar with a spear before heavy rain sets in.

headline: Downstream in a downpour
summary: In soaking rain the party heads back down the Cuiaba to the Sao Lourenco and anchors by the bank for the night.

headline: Machetes, ants and a capybara
summary: In steady rain the hunters cut through dense jungle, beset by mosquitoes and fire ants. Roosevelt shoots a monkey, the party bags coatis and bush deer, and when the sun breaks through around 2 he gets a capybara. Packed for the trip: Gibbon, Sophocles, More's Utopia, Marcus Aurelius and Epictetus.

headline: A hard, empty New Year's hunt
summary: Up at 5, the party eats hardtack, ham, sardines and coffee, then tramps all day through jungle and marsh in the heat and comes back with nothing.

headline: Back onto the Paraguay
summary: The expedition runs down the Sao Lourenco to the Paraguay and begins working upstream.

headline: Parakeets on the river; Margaret dies
summary: Steaming up the Paraguay, Roosevelt watches parakeets build nests. At home, Margaret Roosevelt, who sailed south with the party, dies of typhoid fever.

headline: Quiet nights on deck
summary: Going up the Paraguay, the party watches wildlife by day and enjoys calm nights on deck.

headline: At Sao Luis de Caceres
summary: Leaving the marshes behind, the party reaches Sao Luis de Caceres late in the day, and Roosevelt stays with Lieutenant Lyra. In the United States, Margaret Roosevelt is buried.

headline: Up the River of Tapirs
summary: The expedition heads up the Sepotuba, known as the River of Tapirs, and pitches camp at Porto Campo. Baggage goes ahead to a staging point, and the flag is raised each day.

headline: Camp life at Porto Campo
summary: At Porto Campo the party observes wildlife and hunts.

headline: In camp
summary: The expedition stays in camp at Porto Campo.

headline: A tapir in the water
summary: With four canoes, three dugouts and one Canadian, the party hunts tapir. Hunting on foot with Fiala, Roosevelt takes a bush deer and later shoots a tapir as it swims.

headline: Peccaries elude them
summary: A hunt for white-lipped peccaries comes up empty, and the bugs make it miserable: ticks, wasps, mosquitoes and fire ants.

headline: Five peccaries with Rondon
summary: Roosevelt and Colonel Rondon try again for peccaries and get five, plus a small bush deer.

headline: The supply boat is back
summary: The supply boat comes back to camp at Porto Campo.

headline: Breaking camp for Tapirapoan
summary: The party strikes camp, packs a launch and houseboat, and starts up the Paraguay for Tapirapoan with 30 men and five dogs, in rain.

headline: Reading Gibbon at a mile and a half an hour
summary: The boat crawls upriver while the men cook on deck over a makeshift hearth. Roosevelt's reading includes Gibbon, Scott's Quentin Durward and the Song of Roland. At home, Alice's grandmother Lee dies, leaving her an annual income from a trust.

headline: Ants in the tents
summary: A man who went missing is found, lunch is on an island, and the party reaches Tapirapoan. Ants chew through their tents at night.

headline: Into the real wilderness
summary: At Tapirapoan, Roosevelt readies for the unexplored country with Kermit, Colonel Rondon, Cherrie, Miller, Fiala, two Brazilians and the paddlers. He writes Quentin about the trip and Kermit, and reports early results to Frank Chapman.

headline: Vampire bats
summary: At Tapirapoan, Roosevelt studies vampire bats.

headline: The ox train goes ahead
summary: Seventy pack oxen leave Tapirapoan ahead of the party. In the United States, Bamie turns 59.

headline: Kermit hunts
summary: At Tapirapoan, Kermit goes out hunting.

headline: At Tapirapoan
summary: The expedition is at Tapirapoan; nothing else is recorded.

headline: Mule train to the Sepotuba falls
summary: The party sets out on riding mules and covers 15 miles to the Sepotuba waterfall.

headline: Hacking through the forest
summary: Turning west away from the river, the riders cut their way through dense forest with machetes and make camp in rain.

headline: Up onto the Parecis Plateau
summary: A steep climb brings the party to the rim of the Parecis Plateau, where the day is cool and free of mosquitoes.

headline: Over the great divide
summary: Riding across the high plateau, the party passes the watershed that separates the Amazon basin from the Paraguay's, with rain in the afternoon.

headline: Campfire stories
summary: Heading north, Kermit shoots two pampas deer bucks. That night stories go around the campfire while Roosevelt writes; it rains.

headline: On the trail
summary: The expedition is traveling; nothing else is recorded.

headline: On the trail
summary: The expedition is traveling; nothing else is recorded.

headline: Riding in heavy rain
summary: The expedition travels on through heavy rain.

headline: Telegraph line and a swim
summary: After a late start the party strikes a telegraph line, crosses the Sacre, and sees the falls at Salto Bello, where the motor road ends. The men go swimming.

headline: A ball game near Utiarity
summary: Two miles from Utiarity Falls, Roosevelt watches Indians play an unusual form of ball. It rains.

headline: Rain at Utiarity Falls
summary: The expedition is at Utiarity Falls in the rain.

headline: Pausing at Utiarity Falls
summary: Roosevelt's expedition is at Utiarity Falls, where a native village sits beside a station on Brazil's telegraph line.

headline: A live armadillo for the collection
summary: The rain stops though clouds hang on. Roosevelt heads out alone with his rifle and comes back carrying a living armadillo for naturalist Leo Miller, then sits by the falls watching the village men dance.

headline: The expedition splits and heads north
summary: Father Zahm turns back for Tapirapoan with specimens, while Fiala and Lauriado break off to descend the Juruena. Under clearing skies, Roosevelt, Kermit, Rondon, Lyra, Olivera, Cherrie and Miller push on with mules and two ox carts, covering about 15 miles of wilderness.

headline: Biting insects at the Burity River
summary: Fair skies, fierce insects. The party camps on the western bank of the Burity, where the men wash in the river before rain moves in.

headline: Watching the Nhambiquara
summary: Through a downpour the party fords the Burity and camps where the Huatsui River begins, an automobile still traveling with them. Roosevelt studies the Nhambiquara people he meets along the way.

headline: Lightening the load
summary: The expedition trims its baggage to travel lighter.

headline: Camp on a Tapajós headwater
summary: A brief day's march ends at a stream that feeds the Tapajós. George Cherrie returns to camp with bird specimens.

headline: Twenty miles to Juruena
summary: Under clear skies the party covers 20 miles and pulls into Juruena by mid-afternoon, an outpost with a garrison and a telegraph office.

headline: A working rest day at Juruena
summary: The expedition stays put. Specimens are added to the collection, film is developed and journals caught up. Roosevelt watches native dancing as heavy rain falls.

headline: Gibbon and Arsène Lupin by the campfire
summary: Back on the trail in the rain, the soaked party covers 15 miles and crosses the river by ferry. Evenings bring more campfire stories, and Roosevelt reads Gibbon alongside an Arsène Lupin detective tale.

headline: Marching on
summary: The expedition continues its overland march; no details are recorded.

headline: Alice turns 30 back home
summary: Roosevelt's party is still marching through the interior. In the United States, his daughter Alice celebrates her 30th birthday.

headline: Still on the trail
summary: The party keeps traveling; nothing more is recorded.

headline: Another day of travel
summary: The expedition continues north with no further details noted.

headline: Last of the carts at Campos Novos
summary: The party reaches Campos Novos and links up with Amilcar and Mello and the pack train. From here on, everything moves without carts.

headline: An afternoon camp
summary: The expedition keeps moving and pitches camp in the afternoon.

headline: Vilhena telegraph post
summary: The party arrives at the telegraph station of Vilhena. Back in the United States, Alice and Nick Longworth mark eight years of marriage.

headline: Heading north
summary: The expedition continues northward.

headline: Northward again
summary: Another day of northward travel, with nothing else recorded.

headline: First sight of the River of Doubt
summary: After woods give way to open country, the party spots a small brook and recognizes it as the source of the Rio da Dúvida, the River of Doubt. Roosevelt jots notes on local people and their dances; rain falls.

headline: Attempted theft at camp
summary: Local people try to make off with things from the expedition's camp.

headline: Through hill pastures to Tres Burity
summary: The march crosses rolling grassland and reaches a ranch at Tres Burity.

headline: An archery exhibition at Bonifacio
summary: At Bonifacio, local Indians show off their skill with bows and arrows for the visitors.

headline: Two parties, two rivers
summary: After seven miles the travelers meet Amilcar again and divide. Amilcar, Miller and Mello will follow the Gy-Paraná; Roosevelt, Kermit, Rondon, Lyra, Cherrie and the doctor take the River of Doubt with 16 paddlers, seven canoes and food for 50 days.

headline: Fixing the camp's position
summary: The party's camp is plotted at about 12° south latitude, 60° west longitude. Roosevelt writes Robert Bridges about a chapter of his expedition book.

headline: Seven dugouts ready
summary: In camp, the expedition's seven canoes are all heavy dugouts hollowed from logs.

headline: Into the unknown on the River of Doubt
summary: Roosevelt's party pushes off down the River of Doubt, a waterway no mapmaker has charted. They survey and measure the river as they paddle.

headline: Mapping the first stretch
summary: The survey canoes lead off while Cherrie gathers specimens near camp. Roosevelt and Cherrie follow around midday. Where the Bandeira joins, the river broadens; the team maps 16.5 kilometers. Film footage shows Roosevelt and the party in their canoes.

headline: Ants, bees and monkey for supper
summary: The men wash in the river before dawn, then paddle through heavy rain to map 20.5 kilometers. Stingless bees pester them, ants chew through even their clothing, and a monkey becomes dinner. In New York, Edith takes a hotel room to be near Ethel as her baby's birth approaches.

headline: Scouting the Navaite rapids
summary: After 20 kilometers under light rain, the party camps and scouts the rapids ahead, which they name Navaite. Here the river squeezes to under 24 feet across.

headline: Hauling dugouts around Navaite
summary: The whole day goes into dragging the heavy canoes and supplies overland past the rapids.

headline: Fly dope and hungry termites
summary: The portage continues through pouring rain. The insects are so savage the men smear on 'fly dope,' and termites are devouring clothes and equipment.

headline: A sunken canoe raised
summary: The portage wraps up by morning. One dugout goes under and must be hauled back up before the party heads downriver again, faces and hands puffy from bites. They make 12 kilometers and camp among giant ants.

headline: Winding river, slow progress
summary: The twisting river yields 19 kilometers. The men gather wild honey and sample the sap of the 'milk-tree.' Rapids ahead mean another portage. After 100 river kilometers, they sit just 55 kilometers, as the crow flies, from the starting point.

headline: A grandson born in New York
summary: On the river, the party moves camp around the rapids while Kermit finds yet another rapid downstream. In New York City, Ethel delivers an eight-pound boy after a 48-hour labor: Richard Derby Jr., Roosevelt's grandson.

headline: French poetry from Kermit
summary: While the portage goes on, Roosevelt hunts in the forest without luck. Kermit loans him a volume of French poems.

headline: Portage day
summary: Another day spent carrying canoes and gear around the rapids.

headline: Running two rapids
summary: The canoes travel just 1.5 kilometers but shoot two rapids rather than carrying around them. The pests never let up: ants, termites and biting flies.

headline: Two canoes smashed overnight
summary: Two dugouts tear loose in the night and are wrecked in the current. The party will have to carve replacements.

headline: Carving a new dugout
summary: The men set to hollowing out a huge tree trunk for a canoe. Roosevelt hunts in the forest, while Kermit has better luck finding food elsewhere.

headline: Working by candlelight
summary: Canoe building goes on from morning until ten at night, the last hours lit by candles.

headline: Racing the rapids to save food
summary: In drenching rain the new canoe is launched near noon and the party moves again. Short on time and food, they run the rapids, bailing after each one, until past 5 p.m., making 16 km and camping in darkness. The Outlook prints his 'South America and the Monroe Doctrine.'

headline: Simplicio drowns; Kermit nearly lost
summary: After 6 easy kilometers the party hears rapids. Scouting them, Kermit's canoe is caught by a whirlpool and swept over. Paddler Simplicio is killed; Kermit, pulled under, fights his way out, and his dog reaches shore too. Simplicio is buried before camp.

headline: Losing the rope and pulleys
summary: Under black skies and blinding rain, loads go overland and empty canoes run the rapids. One lost canoe carried the ropes and pulleys, ending heavy portages. Indians kill Kermit's dog. With four canoes and two-thirds of the food left, men will walk the banks, spare clothes are dropped, and quinine is given daily.

headline: Half walking, half paddling
summary: Rondon, Lyra, Kermit, Cherrie and nine others hike the bank, while Roosevelt, the doctor and six men, three of them lamed by swollen feet, ride the canoes. They cover 7 kilometers and run two rapids.

headline: The Rio Roosevelt gets its name
summary: A tributary is found joining the river and named Rio Kermit, while the main stream itself gets a new name: Rio Roosevelt. The canoes shoot another set of rapids and slip past an Indian village, covering 8 km.

headline: Swimming with piranha
summary: The men build more canoes. Some go swimming despite piranha in the water, and ants overrun the camp.

headline: Exploring the forest
summary: As canoe building continues, Roosevelt explores the surrounding forest.

headline: Chile essay appears at home
summary: The crew keeps working on canoes. In The Outlook, Roosevelt's 'Chile and the Monroe Doctrine' is published.

headline: Six canoes and moving again
summary: With two fresh dugouts, the fleet stands at six. The party gets underway and covers 10 km, though easing the canoes down the newest rapids eats up six hours.

headline: Cherrie talks of Vermont
summary: The party makes 13 km, seven hours of it working through a 4-km stretch of rapids. Cherrie talks about his home in Vermont.

headline: Eating palm hearts
summary: With rations shrinking, the men cut palm tops to eat. Big rapids hold progress to 1.5 km.

headline: Half the food gone
summary: After bringing the canoes through the rapids, the party names a tributary the Taunay. Half the provisions are eaten, two men have fever, and more rapids rumble ahead. At home, Edith returns from New York and opens Sagamore Hill.

headline: Rock carvings found
summary: The three most skilled boatmen take the canoes through the rapids. The party discovers carved symbols on rocks.

headline: Drenched and worn out
summary: Three kilometers bring more rapids, which take the whole day. After a ten-minute paddle, still more rapids appear. In heavy rain, the men camp soaked and exhausted.

headline: A cataract ahead
summary: The canoes shoot rapids and pass a stream the party names the Cherrie River. Kermit finds a perilous three-kilometer cataract downstream, so the loads must be cut further.

headline: Lowering canoes through a gorge
summary: The men ease the canoes down rapids inside a steep-sided gorge.

headline: Packing loads over a mountain
summary: Canoe lowering continues while the cargo is carried up and over the mountain.

headline: One monkey for the whole party
summary: A single monkey is shot, giving each man a few good bites. In heavy rain five canoes come down safely and a sixth breaks. Insects eat Roosevelt's last clothes. At home, Scribners publishes his two-volume natural history of African big game, written with Edmund Heller.

headline: Spirits sag among the men
summary: The canoes are finally all lowered, but some of the men are losing heart.

headline: Three kilometers and another gorge
summary: Underway again, the party manages only 3 km, most of the men on foot. Ahead lie more rapids in a deep canyon.

headline: Murder in camp
summary: Starting down the rapids, the party loses a canoe; the boots and clothing of Kermit and Lyra are falling apart. Then Julio, one of the paddlers, shoots and kills fellow camarada Paishon. Edith writes Bamie with news.

headline: Roosevelt's leg strikes a boulder
summary: While working a canoe through the rapids, Roosevelt slams his leg against a rock and comes down with fever. Kermit has dysentery. At home, Ethel marks her first wedding anniversary.

headline: Delirious with fever
summary: Julio is spotted in the jungle but left alone and never seen again. Roosevelt's fever climbs to 39°C; out of his head, he recites poetry as the party keeps working down the rapids.

headline: Roosevelt asks to be left behind
summary: As the party portages more rapids, Roosevelt urges his companions to go on without him so they can survive. Far away in Bogota, American and Colombian envoys sign a treaty, negotiated under Secretary of State Bryan, that voices regret over the 1903 loss of Panama and promises Colombia $25 million.

headline: Thirty-six kilometers of flat water
summary: The land flattens and the party makes 36 km, passing a large unmapped river that joins the Rio Roosevelt.

headline: Monkeys and piranha for food
summary: Only 5 km today through a chain of rapids; cargo goes around two of them before the canoes are run. Three monkeys and two piranha go into the pot.

headline: Archie turns 20
summary: The expedition is in camp. At Harvard, Archie celebrates his 20th birthday.

headline: Wishing for a birch-bark canoe
summary: Run, portage, run, more rapids: under 5 km in all. Roosevelt wishes for a light birch-bark canoe instead of the cumbersome dugouts. A toucan, piranha and a turtle feed the party.

headline: Still burning with fever
summary: Loads are carried down to the base of the rapids, followed by a 30- to 40-minute run before more rapids appear. Roosevelt remains feverish. At Sagamore Hill, Clifford and Teresa Richardson are guests.

headline: An Easter feast of fish
summary: On Easter Sunday the party paddles ten minutes and portages for eight hours, but 28 big fish mean everyone eats well for once.

headline: Silence at last
summary: After a day of portaging, a late 15-km run brings the party to a camp where, the roar of rapids is gone for the first time in more than a month.

headline: Sickened by nuts and meat
summary: A 32-km run takes the canoes through a few minor rapids and one portage. The men fall ill after eating nuts and meat.

headline: Out of the wilderness
summary: Still queasy, the men cover 25 km and spot 'J.A.' carved on a post, a rubber tapper's mark. Houses follow, then talk with settlers: they have made it out. Roosevelt's fever lingers; abscesses on his leg need a drain, and Rondon notes erysipelas in the left leg hurt in 1902.

headline: Downriver from house to house
summary: The party makes long runs downstream each day, spending nights at riverside homes.

headline: No more foraging
summary: Roosevelt purchases provisions for the men, ending their need to live off the land.

headline: Still sick on the river
summary: The trip downstream goes on with Roosevelt still ill.

headline: A guide and a gift from Senhor Barboso
summary: The party engages a rubber worker as guide. Senhor Barboso supplies a canoe and food and will not take payment. Past the mouth of the Rio Branco, they portage rapids; the cook buys a trumpeter bird.

headline: A shelter for the invalid
summary: A sun shelter is rigged over the ailing Roosevelt in the lighter canoe they acquired. A stop at a store yields sugar and tobacco, and the party covers 52 km. In Colorado, National Guard troops massacre striking miners at Ludlow.

headline: Trading dugouts for boats
summary: A good day's run brings the party to the Inferno rapids. At a house they pick up a large boat and a light one, leaving two dugouts behind.

headline: Down the Inferno rapids
summary: Canoes, boats and gear are worked down the Inferno rapids, a brief run, in the rain.

headline: Nearly 50 kilometers
summary: The canoes cover close to 50 km and shoot the Infernino rapids fully loaded. Night is spent in a grimy house.

headline: Last dugout replaced
summary: Fifty kilometers bring the party to the Carupanan rapids. At a store run by Senhor Caripe, they receive a boat to replace their final dugout.

headline: Kermit shoots a caiman
summary: Guided by Caripe, the party spends a day and a half on the fairly easy Carupanan rapids. Kermit kills a caiman. On the broader river, harsh sun beating down through the trees is hard on the sick Roosevelt.

headline: Flags at the Castanho
summary: Past the last dangerous rapids, at 1 p.m. the party reaches the Castanho, where Lieutenant Pyrineus has waited a month, Brazilian and American flags flying. Where the two rivers meet, they form the Aripuanã.

headline: The Rio Roosevelt made official
summary: In a small ceremony Rondon lays out the expedition's findings and formally names the river Rio Roosevelt: 750 km in two months by canoe. Leaving Lyra and Pyrineus, the boats reach São João at 1 p.m. in heavy rain, and Roosevelt lodges with Senhor Caripe.

headline: Steamer to Manaus
summary: At São João the party abandons boat and canoe and boards Pyrineus's river steamer for a 36-hour trip to Manaus.

headline: Into the Amazon
summary: The steamer works down the lower Madeira and enters the Amazon in the afternoon. Back home, Corinne marks her 32nd wedding anniversary.

headline: Reaching Manaus
summary: At 1 a.m. the party arrives at Manaus on the Rio Negro and finds Miller. Mr. Robiliard of the Booth Line books passage for Roosevelt and Kermit and pays the camaradas in gold sovereigns. Dr. Cajazeira drains Roosevelt's leg abscess. Roosevelt wires Lauro Müller with results; the naturalists count 2,500+ birds and 500 mammals.

headline: Leaving Manaus
summary: The party sails from Manaus for Belém aboard the Dunstan. Rondon writes that their findings disprove claims made by the explorer Landor, and Roosevelt sends Lauro Müller a complete account of the expedition.

headline: Down the Amazon
summary: Roosevelt's steamer continues down the Amazon.

headline: Still on the Amazon
summary: Another day steaming toward the sea on the Amazon.

headline: Bedridden, writing to Arthur Lee
summary: Aboard ship on the Amazon, Roosevelt tells his English friend Arthur Lee about his fever and abscesses and looks ahead to a visit to England.

headline: In Pará
summary: The party is in Pará, Brazil.

headline: Farewells at Belém
summary: At Belém Roosevelt meets ethnologist William Farabee of the University of Pennsylvania, then boards the Aidan. Fifty-five pounds lighter and leaning on a cane, he bids goodbye to Rondon, Dr. Cajazeira, Lyra and Kermit.

headline: Sailing north for home
summary: The Aidan leaves Belém bound for Barbados and New York.

headline: At sea aboard the Aidan
summary: Roosevelt is at sea, steaming north toward New York.

headline: At sea aboard the Aidan
summary: Roosevelt is at sea, steaming north toward New York.

headline: At sea aboard the Aidan
summary: Roosevelt is at sea, steaming north toward New York.

headline: Fifty books from Barbados
summary: When the ship calls at Bridgetown, Barbados, Roosevelt buys 50 books, and he will finish every one before reaching New York.

headline: Reading his way north
summary: At sea, Roosevelt works through the stack of books from Barbados.

headline: At sea, bound for New York
summary: Roosevelt is aboard the Aidan, heading home.

headline: At sea, bound for New York
summary: Roosevelt is aboard the Aidan, heading home.

headline: At sea, bound for New York
summary: Roosevelt is aboard the Aidan, heading home.
